pages.title: Use with an AI agent
pages.description: Connect your coding agent to an MCP server that returns the real API of every DooDesch mod.
pages.markdown:
Connect the `doodesch-docs` MCP server to your agent. It then reads the real API instead of guessing method names.

**You need:** Node.js, and an agent that speaks MCP over stdio (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others).

## Steps

1. Get the server:

   ```bash
   git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Docs.git
   npm ci --prefix ScheduleOne-Docs/mcp
   ```

2. Add it to your agent's MCP config:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "doodesch-docs": {
         "command": "node",
         "args": ["/path/to/ScheduleOne-Docs/mcp/index.mjs"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

The server downloads the docs from this site on first use and caches them for six hours.

## Check it works

Ask your agent: "Use get_api_surface for hotline." The answer lists the Hotline types with their signatures.

## Tools

| Tool | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `get_api_surface` | Every public type and member of one mod, with signatures and the version that added it. |
| `search_docs` | Search the docs, for one mod or one kind of page. |
| `get_page` | One page in full, as markdown. |
| `list_mods` | All mods, which ones have an API, and their type names. |
| `list_pages` | The page index. |

`get_api_surface` comes from the mod's source at its release tag. A member it does not list does not exist.

## Work offline

Download the bundle once and point the server at it:

```bash
curl -O https://docs.doodesch.de/mcp-corpus.json
DOCS_BUNDLE=./mcp-corpus.json node /path/to/ScheduleOne-Docs/mcp/index.mjs
```

When the site is not reachable, the server uses its cached copy.

## Without MCP

The site root has `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `llms-small.txt`. They hold the same text, without the structured API.

pages.markdown:
Find your task in the table. Click the guide and follow its steps.

| I want to | Use | Start with |
|---|---|---|
| Add a gamemode to the main menu | SideHustle | [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/) |

| Add tattoos to the tattoo shop | Inkorporated | [Make a tattoo pack](/mods/inkorporated/guides/getting-started/) |
| Add NPCs to the world | Personnel | [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/) |

## Before you start

- Every library is optional for your players. [Call another mod's API](/using-a-mod-api/) shows how your mod keeps working without it.
- Each library has an API reference with every type and member. Open it from the library's page in the sidebar.
- A coding agent can read the same API. See [Use with an AI agent](/agents/).

pages.title: Fix a broken install
pages.description: Find the mod that stops your game from loading or working, and report it so it gets fixed.
pages.markdown:
Find your symptom below. Check `Schedule I/MelonLoader/Latest.log` first: it lists every mod that loaded, every mod that failed, and the error.

## A mod does nothing

- A dependency is missing. Install everything the mod's page lists under "Requires".
- The log shows the mod failed to load. The error line under it names the cause.
- MelonLoader is older than 0.7.3. Update it.

## The game crashes or does not start

Find the mod by halving:

1. Disable half of your mods. Start the game.
2. If the problem is gone, it is in the disabled half. If not, it is in the enabled half.
3. Repeat with the half that has the problem. Five rounds find one mod out of thirty.

A mod manager disables mods per profile. By hand, move DLLs from `Mods/` to another folder.

## A mod broke after an update

- You updated the mod but not its dependencies. Update them together.
- The game updated. Read the mod's changelog for a fixed version.

## Report a bug

Open the support link on the mod's page and attach:

- `MelonLoader/Latest.log` as a file, not pasted in pieces
- the mod version and the game version
- singleplayer, host or client
- what you did right before the problem

A log helps much more than a screenshot.

## Ask a person

The [DooDesch Mods Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) helps when the log does not tell you enough. Bring the log.

pages.title: Install mods
pages.description: Install a DooDesch Schedule I mod with a mod manager or by hand.
pages.markdown:
Install a mod and everything it needs. A mod manager does it in one click.

## With a mod manager

1. Install [r2modman](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ebkr/r2modman/) or [Gale](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/Kesomannen/GaleModManager/).
2. Select Schedule I and create a profile.
3. Search the mod and click Install. The manager also installs MelonLoader, S1API and every other dependency.
4. Start the game from the manager.

Each mod page links to its Thunderstore package.

## By hand

1. Install MelonLoader 0.7.3 or newer from [github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader](https://github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader/releases). Use only this source.
2. Start the game once. MelonLoader creates its folders. Close the game.
3. Put the mod's `.dll` into `Schedule I/Mods/`.
4. Install every mod that the mod's page lists under "Requires" in the same way.

## Check it works

Open `Schedule I/MelonLoader/Latest.log`. The mod is in the list of loaded mods.

## Update a mod

Update the mod and its dependencies together. A mod that needs a newer dependency can load and then fail later.
After a game update, read the mod's changelog before you report a bug.

## Next

- [Fix a broken install](/fix-install/)
- [All mods](/mods/)

pages.title: ChassisApi
pages.description: Public entry point for other mods: read and change the seat profiles Chassis uses per vehicle code.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public static partial class ChassisApi
```

Namespace `Chassis.Api`

Public entry point for other mods: read and change the seat profiles Chassis uses per vehicle code.

Precedence, last one wins: a profile a mod registers with [`Register`](#register), the JSON file in UserData/Chassis/<code>.json. The file wins so a player or the debug console can always correct a mod's values. Changes take effect on the next seat change; [`Changed`](#changed) tells seated rigs to re-read now.

## Fields

### ResolveUnknownOwner

```csharp
public static Func<LandVehicle, OwnerRecord> ResolveUnknownOwner
```

Type: [`OwnerRecord`](../ownerrecord/)

Host: asked once for a player-owned vehicle that has no record yet, for example one bought before Chassis kept owners. Return the owner and lock state to import, or null to let the vehicle belong to the host.

## Properties

### LocalDriverThrottle

```csharp
public static float LocalDriverThrottle { get; }
```

Added in `1.3.0`

The local driver's own throttle this physics step, before mods add to it in their own UpdateThrottle postfix. Chassis records it first; a pusher mod adds the pusher's input after that, so a seated body's hands follow only the driver's keys.

### LocalPlayerCode

```csharp
public static string LocalPlayerCode { get; }
```

The local player's code, empty before the player exists.

### FirstPersonActive

```csharp
public static bool FirstPersonActive { get; }
```

The local player looks through the eyes of their seated body (key V).

### FirstPersonKey

```csharp
public static KeyCode FirstPersonKey { get; }
```

The key that switches the first-person view, for a mod's own key hints.

### Folder

```csharp
public static string Folder { get; }
```

Folder of the JSON profiles.

### Codes

```csharp
public static IEnumerable<string> Codes { get; }
```

Every vehicle code that has a profile.

### GaugeSources

```csharp
public static IEnumerable<string> GaugeSources { get; }
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Every gauge source by name: the built-in ones and those mods registered. A gauge, a switch's [`ControlProfile.Source`](../controlprofile/#source) and [`VehicleTelemetry.Get`](../vehicletelemetry/#get) read them.

**Value** Built in, with their units: "speed" (km/h or mph by the player's setting), "speed_kmh", "speed_mph", "speed_raw" (vanilla's signed km/h without the display factor), "rpm" (800 idle to 6000), "throttle" (-1 to 1), "handbrake", "brake", "reverse", "lights", "hazard" (each 0 or 1), "indicator" (-1, 0, 1), "indicator_left" and "indicator_right" (1 in the lit half of the flash), "steer" (-1 to 1), "steer_deg" (front wheel degrees), "clock" (HHMM), "clock_hours" (0 to 12), "clock_minutes" (0 to 60), "odometer" and "trip" (km or miles by the player's setting), "odometer_km", "trip_km", "occupied" and "driver" (0 or 1).

### UsesMph

```csharp
public static bool UsesMph { get; }
```

Added in `1.2.0`

True when the player set speeds and distances to miles (preference `SpeedUnit` = mph).

## Events

### IndicatorChanged

```csharp
public static event Action<LandVehicle, int> IndicatorChanged
```

Raised on every peer with the vehicle and the new side when an indicator changes: -1 left, 1 right, 0 off, 2 hazard lights.

### OwnersChanged

```csharp
public static event Action OwnersChanged
```

Raised on every peer after the host's owner and lock records arrived and something changed.

### FirstPersonChanged

```csharp
public static event Action<bool> FirstPersonChanged
```

Raised on this peer with the new state whenever the local first-person view turns on or off.

### TuningChanged

```csharp
public static event Action<LandVehicle, string> TuningChanged
```

Added in `1.3.0`

Raised on every peer with the car and the key after its tuning changed ("*": everything at once).

### Changed

```csharp
public static event Action<string> Changed
```

Raised with the vehicle code after a profile was registered, loaded or edited.

### ControlUsed

```csharp
public static event Action<ControlUse> ControlUsed
```

Type: [`ControlUse`](../controluse/)

Added in `1.2.0`

Raised on every peer after any switch was used, built-in actions included.

### HeadlightsChanged

```csharp
public static event Action<LandVehicle, bool> HeadlightsChanged
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Raised on every peer when a vehicle's headlights go on (true) or off (false).

### BrakeChanged

```csharp
public static event Action<LandVehicle, bool> BrakeChanged
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Raised on every peer when a vehicle's brakes go on (true) or off (false).

### ReverseChanged

```csharp
public static event Action<LandVehicle, bool> ReverseChanged
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Raised on every peer when a vehicle starts (true) or stops (false) driving backwards.

### DriverChanged

```csharp
public static event Action<LandVehicle, bool> DriverChanged
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Raised on every peer when someone takes the wheel (true) or the driver's seat empties (false); players and NPCs.

## Methods

### PoseAsPusher

```csharp
public static bool PoseAsPusher(
    Player player,
    LandVehicle vehicle,
    bool glide = true)
```

Added in `1.3.0`

Poses a player's body behind a vehicle with the hands on the handles from [`ChassisProfile.Push`](../chassisprofile/#push). For the local player the key hints switch to the pusher's keys. Returns false with the reason logged when the vehicle has no push profile or the body cannot be posed.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `glide` | true eases the body into the pose over a moment, false puts it there at once. |

### ReleasePusher

```csharp
public static void ReleasePusher(Player player)
```

Added in `1.3.0`

Lets go: the body of a player posed with [`PoseAsPusher`](#poseaspusher) moves on its own again.

### PushedBy

```csharp
public static LandVehicle PushedBy(Player player)
```

Added in `1.3.0`

The vehicle a player is posed behind, or null.

### AddKeyHint(string, string, Func<KeyHintContext, bool>, params KeyCode[])

```csharp
public static void AddKeyHint(
    string id,
    string label,
    Func<KeyHintContext, bool> show,
    params KeyCode[] keys)
```

Types: [`KeyHintContext`](../keyhintcontext/)

Added in `1.1.0`

Adds a line to the key hints at the bottom left while the local player sits in or pushes a vehicle, below First Person and Horn and above Indicators. `show` runs every frame and picks the vehicles and seats the key works in; null shows it in every vehicle. The same id again replaces the entry. Letters follow the keyboard layout, so `KeyCode.Y` shows the key labelled Y.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | Your own unique id, e.g. "mymod.siren". |
| `label` | The text next to the key, e.g. "Siren". |
| `show` | Whether the line shows for the vehicle and seat in [`KeyHintContext`](../keyhintcontext/); null shows it always. |
| `keys` | One key or several shown side by side, e.g. `KeyCode.LeftArrow, KeyCode.RightArrow`. |

**Example**

A siren key only for the driver of the mod's own vehicle:

```csharp
ChassisApi.AddKeyHint("mymod.siren", "Siren", c => c.Driver && ChassisApi.CodeOf(c.Vehicle) == "mymod_cruiser", KeyCode.H);
```

### AddKeyHint(string, string, Func<KeyHintContext, bool>, Func<KeyCode>)

```csharp
public static void AddKeyHint(
    string id,
    string label,
    Func<KeyHintContext, bool> show,
    Func<KeyCode> key)
```

Types: [`KeyHintContext`](../keyhintcontext/)

Added in `1.1.0`

Adds a key hint whose key can change while the game runs, for a key from a mod's preferences. The key is read every frame and the hint follows it.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | Your own unique id, e.g. "mymod.siren". |
| `label` | The text next to the key, e.g. "Siren". |
| `show` | Whether the line shows for the vehicle and seat in [`KeyHintContext`](../keyhintcontext/); null shows it always. |
| `key` | Read every frame, e.g. `() => myKeyEntry.Value` for a MelonPreferences entry. |

### RemoveKeyHint

```csharp
public static bool RemoveKeyHint(string id)
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Removes a key hint a mod added; false when there was none with that id.

### Assign

```csharp
public static void Assign(LandVehicle vehicle, string code)
```

Gives one vehicle the profile of another code. For mods that build their vehicle on a vanilla one (a "veeper" under a camper van): without this, the profile would follow the vanilla code to every vehicle of that kind. Call it on every peer; it holds until [`Unassign`](#unassign) or until the vehicle is gone.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `code` | The profile code to use, e.g. "mymod_camper"; it may be registered before or after this call. |

### Unassign

```csharp
public static void Unassign(LandVehicle vehicle)
```

Ends an [`Assign`](#assign): the vehicle uses the profile of its own vehicle code again.

### CodeOf

```csharp
public static string CodeOf(LandVehicle vehicle)
```

The profile code a vehicle uses: the assigned one, else its vehicle code.

### For

```csharp
public static ChassisProfile For(LandVehicle vehicle)
```

Types: [`ChassisProfile`](../chassisprofile/)

The profile a vehicle uses, or null when Chassis leaves it to vanilla.

### RegisterSound

```csharp
public static void RegisterSound(string name, AudioClip clip)
```

Makes a clip available to profiles by name ([`HornProfile.Clip`](../hornprofile/#clip), [`HornProfile.Chirp`](../hornprofile/#chirp)).

| Parameter | |
|---|---|

```csharp

    string code,
    Func<LandVehicle, GameObject> build,

```

Types: [`ChassisProfile`](../chassisprofile/)

Added in `1.2.0`

Builds a mod's own interior into every vehicle that uses the profile `code`, in place of the base interior's seats, dashboard and wheel. The lining and the tinted glass of [`InteriorProfile`](../interiorprofile/) stay; set [`InteriorProfile.Lining`](../interiorprofile/#lining) to false or [`InteriorProfile.Glass`](../interiorprofile/#glass) to null in `configure` to drop them. Call it on every peer; the same code again replaces the factory and rebuilds the vehicles that have one.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `code` | The profile code, e.g. "shitbox" or a mod's own code from [`Assign`](#assign). |
| `build` | Makes the interior for one vehicle. Chassis parents the object to the vehicle's frame and keeps its local position, rotation and scale, so place it in the frame's space (x right, y up, z forward, metres). |
| `configure` | Changes the profile to match the new interior: [`ChassisProfile.Steering`](../chassisprofile/#steering), [`ChassisProfile.Gauges`](../chassisprofile/#gauges), [`ChassisProfile.Controls`](../chassisprofile/#controls), the driver's hands. It runs once on every profile object of this code: the one there now, the one Chassis fits for a vanilla car the first time one is seen, and one from a JSON file. Null leaves the profile as it is. |

**Example**

An interior from an AssetBundle prefab for the Shitbox, with its own wheel and speedometer:

```csharp
ChassisApi.SetInterior("shitbox",
    vehicle => UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate(myCockpitPrefab),
    profile =>
    {
        profile.Steering = new SteeringProfile { Path = "MyCockpit/Wheel", Axis = Vector3.forward, Ratio = 8f, Max = 300f };
        profile.Gauges.Clear();
        profile.Gauges.Add(new GaugeProfile { Name = "speedo", Path = "MyCockpit/SpeedoNeedle", Source = "speed_kmh", Max = 160f });
    });
```


pages.title: ChassisProfile
pages.description: Where occupants sit and hold on in one vehicle type, keyed by its vehicle code.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class ChassisProfile
```

Namespace `Chassis.Api`

Where occupants sit and hold on in one vehicle type, keyed by its vehicle code. Every point is in the space of the vehicle's model frame: the transform at [`Frame`](#frame) under the vehicle, or the vehicle root when that is empty. Left-side points are the mirror of the right-side values stored here, about the seat's own centre plane (through the seat root, turned by its yaw); in wheel mode the hands mirror about the steering column.

The same object backs the JSON file (UserData/Chassis/<code>.json) and the C# API, so a value set from code, from the file or from the debug console is the same value.

Points are `Vector3` values in metres in the frame's own axes: x to the vehicle's right, y up, z forward. Angles are in degrees. Weights run from 0 (the animation decides) to 1 (the profile decides). In the JSON file a vector is `[x, y, z]` and a colour is `[r, g, b, a]` with each channel from 0 to 1.

**Example**

A profile for a vehicle a mod builds on a vanilla one, with the driver fitted to the vanilla seat:

```csharp
var frame = vehicle.transform.Find("MyModel");
var profile = new ChassisProfile { Code = "mymod_cart", Frame = "MyModel" };
profile.Seats.Add(ChassisApi.FitSeat(vehicle, 0, frame, frame.Find("SteeringWheel")));
ChassisApi.Register(profile);
ChassisApi.Assign(vehicle, "mymod_cart");
```

## Fields

### Code

```csharp
public string Code = string.Empty
```

Vehicle code (`LandVehicle.VehicleCode`) this profile belongs to.

**Value** Lower case, matched without case. The vanilla cars are "shitbox", "shitbox_police", "veeper", "bruiser", "bruiser_police", "dinkler", "hounddog", "cheetah" and "hotbox"; the wheelchair from the mod Rollin is "rollin_wheelchair". A mod vehicle can use a code of its own and get it with [`ChassisApi.Assign`](../chassisapi/#assign). [`ChassisApi.Codes`](../chassisapi/#codes) lists every code that has a profile.

### Frame

```csharp
public string Frame = string.Empty
```

Path of the model frame below the vehicle root, or empty for the root itself.

**Value** Transform names joined with "/", as `Transform.Find` takes them, e.g. "Body/Model". When that path does not exist, the first transform named like its last part is used. Rollin's wheelchair uses "ChassisModel"; the vanilla cars leave it empty.


One entry per `LandVehicle.Seats` index that should show a seated body.

pages.description: One switch in the cockpit a seated player can use in first person: look at it and click, or turn a knob with the mouse wheel.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class ControlProfile
```

Namespace `Chassis.Api`

Added in `1.2.0`

One switch in the cockpit a seated player can use in first person: look at it and click, or turn a knob with the mouse wheel. Everyone within reach (about 0.9 m from the eyes) can use it; the click goes through the host to every peer, and Chassis keeps and saves the state of toggles and knobs.

**Example**

A toggle for the headlights and a button for a mod's own action:

```csharp
profile.Controls.Add(new ControlProfile { Name = "lights", Kind = "toggle", Path = "Dash/LightSwitch", Action = "lights", Source = "lights" });
profile.Controls.Add(new ControlProfile { Name = "siren", Kind = "button", Path = "Dash/SirenButton", Action = "mymod.siren" });
```

## Fields

### Name

```csharp
public string Name = string.Empty
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Name of the switch, unique in the profile; the saved state and [`ChassisApi.ControlValue`](../chassisapi/#controlvalue) use it.

### Label

```csharp
public string Label = string.Empty
```

Added in `1.2.0`

The name the player reads under the centre dot while looking at the switch.

**Value** For example "Hazard lights". Empty shows [`Name`](#name) with a capital first letter and spaces for "_".

### Kind

```csharp
public string Kind = "button"
```

Added in `1.2.0`

"button", "toggle" or "knob".

**Value** "button" fires its action on a click and springs back. "toggle" flips between 0 and 1 on a click. "knob" steps between [`Min`](#min) and [`Max`](#max) with the mouse wheel; a click puts it back to [`Default`](#default).

### Path

```csharp
public string Path = string.Empty
```

Added in `1.2.0`

The transform that moves and that the player aims at, below the vehicle's frame.

**Value** A path or one name, searched as [`GaugeProfile.Path`](../gaugeprofile/#path). Its renderers give the area to aim at unless [`BoxSize`](#boxsize) is set.

### Action

```csharp
public string Action = string.Empty
```

Added in `1.2.0`

What the switch does.

**Value** A built-in action: "lights" (headlights on/off), "hazard" (hazard lights on/off), "indicator" (a knob from -1 left to 1 right), "indicator_left", "indicator_right", "horn" or "trip_reset". Any other name is a mod's own action from [`ChassisApi.RegisterControlAction`](../chassisapi/#registercontrolaction); empty does nothing but keep the state.

### Source

```csharp
public string Source = string.Empty
```

Added in `1.2.0`

A source whose value the switch shows instead of its own state, or empty.

**Value** For switches whose state can change without them: "lights" for a light switch (the light key also switches), "hazard", "indicator". Any source from [`ChassisApi.GaugeSources`](../chassisapi/#gaugesources) works.

### Axis

```csharp
public Vector3 Axis = Vector3.right
```

Added in `1.2.0`

The axis the switch turns about (toggle, knob) or moves along (button), in its own space.

**Value** A direction, e.g. (1, 0, 0) for a rocker switch that tips forward and back, (0, 0, 1) for a button pushed forward.

### Angle

```csharp
public float Angle = 30f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Toggle: degrees between off and on. Knob: degrees from [`Min`](#min) to [`Max`](#max).

**Value** The rest pose is the middle: a toggle stands at -Angle/2 off and +Angle/2 on.

### Press

```csharp
public float Press = 0.004f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Button: how far it moves along [`Axis`](#axis) while pressed, in metres.

### Min

```csharp
public float Min
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Knob: lowest value.

### Max

```csharp
public float Max = 1f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Knob: highest value.

### Step

```csharp
public float Step = 0.1f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Knob: change per notch of the mouse wheel.

### Default

```csharp
public float Default
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Toggle and knob: the value before anyone touched it, and a knob's value after a click.

### BoxCenter

```csharp
public Vector3 BoxCenter
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Centre of the area to aim at, in the switch transform's own space; used when [`BoxSize`](#boxsize) is set.

### BoxSize

```csharp
public Vector3 BoxSize
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Size of the area to aim at in metres, in the switch transform's own space; zero uses its renderers.

**Value** Set it for a switch with no renderer of its own, or to make a small one easier to hit.

pages.title: GaugeProfile
pages.description: One display in the cockpit: a needle that turns with a value, a lamp that glows above a threshold, or digits.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class GaugeProfile
```

Namespace `Chassis.Api`

Added in `1.2.0`

One display in the cockpit: a needle that turns with a value, a lamp that glows above a threshold, or digits. It reads a source by name ([`ChassisApi.GaugeSources`](../chassisapi/#gaugesources)) and moves a transform of the vehicle's model or interior. Chassis draws gauges on every peer, for vehicles near the camera.

**Example**

A speedometer needle that sweeps from 0 to 160 km/h across 270 degrees:

```csharp
profile.Gauges.Add(new GaugeProfile { Name = "speedo", Kind = "needle", Path = "Dash/SpeedoNeedle", Source = "speed_kmh", Min = 0f, Max = 160f });
```

## Fields

### Name

```csharp
public string Name = string.Empty
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Name the debug output and warnings use, e.g. "speedo".

### Kind

```csharp
public string Kind = "needle"
```

Added in `1.2.0`

"needle", "lamp" or "digits".

**Value** "needle" turns the transform at [`Path`](#path) from [`From`](#from) to [`To`](#to) degrees about [`Axis`](#axis). "lamp" makes every renderer below it glow in [`Color`](#color) while the value is above [`Threshold`](#threshold). "digits" puts a text below it that shows the value in [`Format`](#format).

### Path

```csharp
public string Path = string.Empty
```

Added in `1.2.0`

The transform to move, light or write on, below the vehicle's frame.

**Value** A path like "Chassis_Interior/Dash/SpeedoNeedle", or one name like "SpeedoNeedle" that is searched in the whole frame. A needle's transform should sit at the pivot of the needle. Chassis logs one warning per vehicle code when the path is not found.

### Source

```csharp
public string Source = "speed"
```

Added in `1.2.0`

The value the gauge shows, by source name.

**Value** A built-in source such as "speed", "rpm", "lights" or "clock_hours", or a name a mod registered with [`ChassisApi.RegisterGaugeSource`](../chassisapi/#registergaugesource). The full list with units is on [`ChassisApi.GaugeSources`](../chassisapi/#gaugesources).

### Min

```csharp
public float Min
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Needle: the value at [`From`](#from). Values outside Min and Max stop at the end of the dial.

**Value** In the unit of the source, e.g. 0 for a speedometer.

### Max

```csharp
public float Max = 1f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Needle: the value at [`To`](#to).

**Value** In the unit of the source, e.g. 160 for a speedometer that ends at 160 km/h.

### From

```csharp
public float From = -135f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Needle: angle at [`Min`](#min), in degrees about [`Axis`](#axis) from the needle's rest pose.

**Value** With the default axis (0, 0, -1) on a needle that points up at rest, -135 points to the lower left as the driver sees it.

### To

```csharp
public float To = 135f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Needle: angle at [`Max`](#max), in degrees.

**Value** 135 points to the lower right with the default axis; From -135 to To 135 sweeps 270 degrees clockwise.

### Axis

```csharp
public Vector3 Axis = new Vector3(0f, 0f, -1f)
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Needle: the turning axis in the needle transform's own space.

**Value** A direction. (0, 0, -1) turns clockwise as seen by a driver who looks along the vehicle's forward axis at a dial that faces back towards them.

### Smooth

```csharp
public float Smooth = 0.12f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Needle and digits: seconds the shown value takes to follow the source; 0 follows at once.

### Threshold

```csharp
public float Threshold = 0.5f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Lamp: glows while the value is above this.

**Value** 0.5 suits the on/off sources, which read 0 or 1.

### Color

```csharp
public Color Color = new Color(1f, 0.42f, 0f)
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Lamp: glow colour. Digits: text colour.

**Value** Channels from 0 to 1. In JSON: [1, 0.42, 0, 1] for amber.

### Format

```csharp
public string Format = "0"
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Digits: number format of the value.

**Value** A .NET numeric format in invariant culture: "0" for whole numbers, "0.0" for one decimal, "000000" for an odometer with leading zeros. The source "clock" formats as "00:00" by itself.

### Size

```csharp
public float Size = 0.025f
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Digits: height of one line of text in metres.

**Value** 0.02 to 0.03 reads well on a dashboard at arm's length.

pages.title: HandProfile
pages.description: Hand targets of a seated body: on push rims, on the steering wheel or at a fixed grip.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class HandProfile
```

Namespace `Chassis.Api`

Hand targets of a seated body: on push rims, on the steering wheel or at a fixed grip. Right side; the left is mirrored.

## Fields

### Mode

```csharp
public string Mode = "fixed"
```

"rim": hands ride the push rims of two wheels. "fixed": hands stay at [`GripStart`](#gripstart). "wheel": hands hold the steering wheel at [`GripStart`](#gripstart) and turn with it up to [`FollowMax`](#followmax) degrees.

### FollowMax

```csharp
public float FollowMax = 90f
```

Wheel mode: the hands follow the steering wheel this far either way, then stay.

### LeftWheel

```csharp
public string LeftWheel = string.Empty
```

Rim mode: name of the left wheel transform in the model.

**Value** A transform name below the frame, e.g. "RimPivot_L" on the wheelchair. Empty outside rim mode.

### RightWheel

```csharp
public string RightWheel = string.Empty
```

Rim mode: name of the right wheel transform in the model.

**Value** A transform name below the frame, e.g. "RimPivot_R" on the wheelchair. Empty outside rim mode.

### GripStart

```csharp
public Vector3 GripStart
```

Right hand where a push stroke starts. Rim mode: from the wheel centre; fixed mode: in the frame.

**Value** In metres. Rim mode: offset from the right wheel's centre, e.g. (0.04, 0.26, 0.15) on the wheelchair. Fixed and wheel mode: a point in the frame; for the wheel, about 0.17 m right of its centre.

### GripEnd

```csharp
public Vector3 GripEnd
```

Rim mode: right hand where the stroke ends and the hand lets go.

**Value** Offset from the right wheel's centre in metres, e.g. (0.04, 0.15, 0.27) on the wheelchair.

### Recovery

```csharp
public float Recovery = 0.35f
```

Seconds the hand takes from the end of a stroke back to its start.

### RotationWeight

```csharp
public float RotationWeight
```

How strongly the hands turn to the grip, 0 to 1; 0 leaves the wrists to the animation.

### RimRadius

```csharp
public float RimRadius
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Wheel mode: radius of the steering wheel's rim, from the steering pivot to the middle of the rim. Above 0 the hands close around the rim at [`GripAngle`](#gripangle): palm on the rim, fingers around it, thumb on the inside, and [`GripStart`](#gripstart) and [`RotationWeight`](#rotationweight) are not used. 0 keeps the wrists at [`GripStart`](#gripstart) with the fingers as the animation leaves them.

**Value** In metres, e.g. 0.18 on a car wheel 0.39 m across. [`ChassisApi.FitSeat`](../chassisapi/#fitseatlandvehicle-int-transform-transform-float) measures it from the wheel's mesh.

### RimThickness

```csharp
public float RimThickness = 0.03f
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Wheel mode: thickness of the rim the fingers close around.

**Value** In metres, e.g. 0.03.

### RimOffset

```csharp
public float RimOffset
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Wheel mode: how far the rim's middle sits from the steering pivot along the column, towards the driver, in metres. 0 when the pivot is the rim's centre; set it when the pivot sits at the hub behind the rim.

### GripAngle

```csharp
public float GripAngle
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Wheel mode with a [`RimRadius`](#rimradius): where the right hand holds the rim, the left one mirrored.

**Value** Degrees from level towards the top of the wheel: 0 holds it at quarter to three, 30 at ten to two, negative below.

### Elbow

```csharp
public Vector3 Elbow = new Vector3(0.55f, 0.85f, -0.4f)
```

Elbow bend goal (right side).

**Value** A point in the frame the elbow bends towards, in metres: right of and behind the hand points it outwards.

### LeanStart

```csharp
public Vector3 LeanStart
```

Point the spine reaches for at the start of a stroke.

### LeanStartWeight

```csharp
public float LeanStartWeight
```

How strongly the spine reaches for [`LeanStart`](#leanstart), 0 to 1.

### LeanEnd

```csharp
public Vector3 LeanEnd
```

Point the spine reaches for at the end of a stroke.

### LeanEndWeight

```csharp
public float LeanEndWeight
```

How strongly the spine reaches for [`LeanEnd`](#leanend), 0 to 1.

pages.title: Chassis API
pages.description: Look up every public type and member of Chassis 1.8.1.
pages.markdown:
## Use this API

Reference `Chassis.dll` from your Mods folder:

```xml
<Reference Include="Chassis">
  <HintPath>$(ModsDirectory)\Chassis.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Chassis")]
```

Without Chassis its types are missing too. Call it only after you know it loaded.

Source: [`Api/ChassisApi.Fit.cs`, `Api/ChassisApi.Instruments.cs`, `Api/ChassisApi.KeyHints.cs`, `Api/ChassisApi.Occupants.cs`, `Api/ChassisApi.Pushers.cs`, `Api/ChassisApi.Tuning.cs`, `Api/ChassisApi.Vehicles.cs`, `Api/ChassisApi.cs`, `Api/ChassisProfile.cs`, `Api/InstrumentProfiles.cs`, `Api/PaintTarget.cs`, `Api/ProfileJson.cs`, `Api/TuningPart.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/blob/v1.8.1/Api/ChassisApi.Fit.cs) at `v1.8.1`.

### Kind

```csharp

```

"seat" (cushion and backrest), "bench" (a seat across several places), "dash", "gauges" (the hood over the dials), "wheel", and the instrument pieces "needle", "rocker" (a switch that tips), "button" (a round push button facing back), "stalk" (a lever pointing left) and "lamp" (a small block a lamp gauge lights).

Name of the part's object, so gauges, switches and other parts can find it; empty names it by kind.


Name of another kit part this one hangs below and moves with, or empty for none.

pages.title: Chassis changelog
pages.description: Every released version of Chassis and what changed in it.
pages.markdown:
All notable changes to Chassis are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/), and this
project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

## [1.8.1] - 2026-10-28

### Fixed
- The horn no longer carries across the map: it fades with distance, sounds duller far away and is silent past 80 m.

## [1.8.0] - 2026-10-27

### Added
- New "Reflections" row in the graphics settings, Low to Ultra. High and Ultra give sharper chrome that updates faster.

### Fixed
- Tuned cars no longer reverse almost as fast as they drive forward.
- Lowered suspension now shows on big vehicles like the RV.
- Underglow no longer lights the inside of the car.

### For mod authors
- `ChassisApi.HornClip` returns the sound a vehicle's horn plays.

## [1.7.1] - 2026-10-27

### Fixed
- Window tints are clearly darker; the game's fog washed them out to grey.
- Changing the window tint no longer flashes the stock body colour for a moment.
- Chrome paint looks like chrome and reflects the street around the car, also while it drives; metallic paints look
  metallic.
- Neon lights the ground in an even band along the sills and bumpers, with no tube in sight.

## [1.7.0] - 2026-10-26

### Fixed
- Key hints on Left Ctrl show up at the bottom left: the game has no picture for that key and dropped them.

### For mod authors
- `ChassisApi.PreviewTuning`, `PreviewPart` and `EndPreview` show a part or a paint on this machine only, without
  saving or syncing it.
- `ChassisApi.SetPaintTargets` puts the body paint on your own model instead of the stock body; `Secondary` targets
  take the second paint.
- `ChassisApi.PaintRenderers` paints a model with no car under it, on this machine only.
- `ChassisApi.AddKeyHint` takes any key: one the hint strip has no picture for is drawn on a wide key with its name.

## [1.6.1] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed
- The cheetah's body beside the rear window is no longer see-through.

## [1.6.0] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed
- Cars bought while Steam was not ready at the start are yours again in a lobby: locked cars let you in and the
  Yesla app shows.

### For mod authors
- `SeatProfile.Recline` leans the seated body back about the hips with a straight back; hands, feet and eyes keep
  their points. Console: `chassis profile set recline <degrees>`.

## [1.5.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added
- Drivers hold the steering wheel: both hands close around the rim and turn with it, for you and for NPC drivers.

### For mod authors
- `HandProfile.RimRadius`, `RimThickness`, `RimOffset` and `GripAngle` close the hands around the rim. `FitSeat`
  measures `RimRadius` from the wheel's mesh.

## [1.4.0] - 2026-10-21

### Added
- Hold G to keep the horn sounding; it stops when you let go.
- Steering is calmer at speed: the wheels turn less the faster you go and ease back to straight. `SpeedSteering`
  turns it off.

## [1.3.0] - 2026-10-21

### Changed
- The drivable wheelchair moved into its own mod, [Rollin](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Rollin). Install
  Rollin to keep riding and pushing wheelchairs.
- A repaint at Marco's replaces paint that a tuning mod gave the car.

### For mod authors
- Tuning API: `RegisterTuningPart`, `InstallPart` and `RemovePart` for parts with their own model and driving factors.
- Built-in parts: engine, brakes and transmission stages 1-3, suspension 1-4, turbo, drift tyres.
- `SetPaint` (primary, secondary, finish), `SetRimColor`, `SetXenon`, `SetNeon`, `SetWindowTint`, `SetTyreSmoke` and
  `SetHorn`. `SetTuning` and `GetTuning` store keys of your own mod.
- The host checks each change against the owner, syncs it and saves it with the car. `TuningStatsOf` and
  `TuningChanged` read it.
- `PoseAsPusher`, `ReleasePusher` and `PushedBy` let a player push a vehicle from behind, as Rollin's wheelchair does.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-10-21

### Added
- The speedometer and rev counter in the vanilla cars move, dash lamps show indicators and headlights. `SpeedUnit` sets
  `kmh` or `mph`.
- In first person, look at a dash switch and left-click it: lights, hazard lights, indicator stalk (also mouse wheel),
  horn. Switches click, indicators tick.
- A dot in the screen centre shows where you look while your view is below the windscreen, with the switch's name.
- The vanilla cars flash their own amber indicator lamps outside, at the rear part of the brake light in red where a car
  has none.
- Guns hit NPCs in cars. A driver who goes down falls out and the car stops.

### Fixed
- Vehicle owners and locks are no longer lost when the game saves.
- Seats and the driver's legs no longer stick out under the cars.
- The steering wheel no longer spins faster than the hands could turn it.
- Getting in crouched no longer leaves you crouched in the seat.

### For mod authors
- `ChassisApi.SetInterior` builds your own interior; `ChassisProfile.Gauges` and `ChassisProfile.Controls` bind
  needles, lamps, digits and clickable switches.
- `ChassisApi.Telemetry`, `ReadGauge` and `RegisterGaugeSource`: speed, rpm, pedals, lamps, steering, clock, odometer,
  trip, each with a validity flag.
- `RegisterControlAction`, `UseControl`, `ControlUsed` and the events `HeadlightsChanged`, `BrakeChanged`,
  `ReverseChanged`, `DriverChanged`.
- `RegisterOccupantDown` keeps a shot NPC slumped in its seat instead of falling out; `RemoveOccupantDown` removes it.
- `chassis telemetry` and `chassis zones` work in the release build. The GitHub release also carries
  `Chassis_1.2.0_debug.zip` with the developer console commands.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-10-20

### Added
- The key hints at the bottom left show the vehicle's keys: V First Person, G Horn, and the arrow keys for
  Indicators on vehicles with indicator lamps.
- Behind a wheelchair the key hints show Push and Let Go, with your own key bindings.

### Fixed
- NPCs in low cars like Sam's and Michael's Coupe drive off again instead of sitting still at the curb.

### For mod authors
- `ChassisApi.AddKeyHint` puts your own key into the key hints, a fixed key or one from your preferences.
  `RemoveKeyHint` takes it out.
- The `show` callback gets a `KeyHintContext` with `Vehicle`, `Profile`, `Seat`, `Driver` and `Pushing`.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-10-20

### Changed
- Chassis has its own icon in Thunderstore and r2modman.

### For mod authors
- Every type and member is listed in the [API reference](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/chassis/api/), linked from
  the README.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-10-20

### Added
- You sit visibly in the driver's seat with both hands on the wheel, and the wheel turns as you steer. Co-op
  players see it too.
- Press V in a vehicle to switch to first person.
- G sounds the horn. The left and right arrow keys set the indicators on vehicles that have indicator lamps.
- Vanilla cars get seats, a dashboard, a steering wheel and tinted glass. NPC drivers sit visibly, police included.
  `BaseInterior` turns both off.

### For mod authors
- `ChassisApi.Register` adds a vehicle profile from code; `FitSeat` builds a seat profile from the vanilla seat.
- `Honk`, `SetIndicator`, `SetLocked`, `SetOwner`, `SetPart` and `SetStorageEnd` act on a `LandVehicle` and sync in
  co-op.
- `FirstPersonActive`, `FirstPersonChanged`, `IndicatorChanged` and `OwnersChanged` report state to your mod.

pages.title: Console commands
pages.description: Look up every chassis console command, in the release build and in the debug build.
pages.markdown:
Look up a `chassis` command here. Open the in-game console and type it. `chassis help` lists the commands of the
build you run.

## Release build

These work in the normal build that players install.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis help` | List the commands of this build. |
| `chassis telemetry [net id]` | Print every instrument source with its validity flag, and the bound gauges and switches of your car. Without a net id it reads the car you sit in, or the nearest car. |
| `chassis zones [off]` | Show the hit zones of the dash switches (green) and the reach (yellow rings). `off` hides them. |

## Debug build

Every GitHub release carries `Chassis_<version>_debug.zip` next to the normal build. It is the same version with
the developer commands below. Get it from the [releases page](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/releases)
and replace `Mods/Chassis.dll` with the DLL from the zip. Players use the normal build.

Many commands act on the host only. They say so when a client runs them.

### Dash switches

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis aim <switch>` | Turn the first person view to a switch of your car, for example `chassis aim hazard`. |
| `chassis click` | Click the switch in view, as the left mouse button does. |
| `chassis scroll <n>` | Turn the switch in view by `n` steps, as the mouse wheel does. |
| `chassis outline` | Print where the highlight copies of the switch in view sit. |
| `chassis ctl <switch> [value]` | Use a switch of your car through the API. |
| `chassis coast [km/h] [s]` | Hold your car at a speed along its facing. Default 40 km/h for 5 s. |

### Vehicle

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis car` | Print the vehicle: code, profile, owner, indicator state, parts. |
| `chassis car help` | List the `car` subcommands. |
| `chassis car enter [code] [seat]` | Get into the nearest vehicle, or the nearest one of this code. The lock is checked. Seat 1 and up is a passenger seat. |
| `chassis car put <code> <x> <y> <z> [yaw]` | Spawn a car at this pose and stand beside it (host). |
| `chassis car bones` | Print head, hips, knees and feet of your avatar in the vehicle's space. |
| `chassis car remove` | Despawn the vehicle you sit in, or the nearest one (host). |
| `chassis car go [throttle] [steer] [s]` | Drive through the game's own control override, each value from -1 to 1. Sit in the driver seat first. |
| `chassis car slide [km/h] [deg] [s]` | Hold the car at a speed, turned off its facing, to test tyre slip and drift smoke. |
| `chassis car wheels` | Print drift state, smoke and smoke colour per wheel. |
| `chassis car honk [flash]` | Sound the horn, as the G key does. |
| `chassis car blink l\|r\|off` | Set the indicator, as the arrow keys do. |
| `chassis car lock on\|off` | Lock or unlock the vehicle (owner only). |
| `chassis car part <name> open\|close` | Open or close a lid from the profile. |
| `chassis car side front\|rear` | Set which end the storage opens from. |
| `chassis car rain on\|off\|auto` | Force rain for the wipers. |
| `chassis car assign <code>\|off` | Give the vehicle another profile. |
| `chassis car owners` | Print every owner record this peer knows. |
| `chassis car owner <player code>` | Give the vehicle to another player (host). |
| `chassis exit` | Leave the vehicle, as the interact key does. |
| `chassis view [pitch]` | Switch first person on or off while seated, as the V key does. A pitch turns it on and looks down that far. |
| `chassis drive <fwd> <steer> [s]` | Driver input for `s` seconds (default 3). |
| `chassis cam <dist> <yaw> <height>` | Orbit camera around your vehicle, or the nearest seated body. `chassis cam off` ends it. |
| `chassis lights [net id]` | Print the lamp meshes of a car and every renderer with its materials. |
| `chassis crouch [on\|off]` | Crouch or stand, as the crouch key does. |
| `chassis crouch keep\|fix` | `keep`: a body that gets in crouched stays crouched, as in vanilla. `fix`: it sits upright, the default. |
| `chassis hints [format]` | Print the vehicle key hints. A format with `{0}` relabels the arrow keys. |
| `chassis status` | Print seated bodies, pushers, the view, the key hints and the current vehicle. |
| `chassis despawn car` | Remove the nearest car within 30 m. |
| `chassis feet` | Print the ankle axes of every seated body. |

### Tuning

The `tune` commands act on the car you sit in, the nearest car within 15 m, or a car by net id: `chassis tune #<net id> ...`.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis tune` | Print the car's tuning keys and driving factors. |
| `chassis tune help` | List the `tune` subcommands. |
| `chassis tune parts [slot]` | List the parts that fit the car. |
| `chassis tune part <id>` | Install a part. It replaces the part in that slot. |
| `chassis tune remove <slot>` | Put the stock part back in that slot. |
| `chassis tune set <key> <value>` | Set any key, for example `paint C81E1E,metallic`, `rims 202020,chrome`, `xenon 9FB8FF`, `neon 00FFAA,lr`, `tint 10121480`, `smoke FF2080` or `horn <sound>`. |
| `chassis tune unset <key>` | Remove one key. |
| `chassis tune clear` | Put everything back to stock. |
| `chassis tune stats` | Print the stock and the current driving values. |
| `chassis tune demo` | Register demo parts (wing, bumper, exhaust, rims) that fit this car's code. |
| `chassis tune marco open\|<colour>\|close` | Open Marco's repaint menu for the car, pick and buy a colour through the menu's own buttons, or close it. |

### Interior

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis interior on\|off\|rebuild` | Switch the base interior and the tinted glass of the vanilla cars on or off, or build it again. |
| `chassis interior lift <m>` | Set the lowest cushion top above the car's underside and fit the vanilla cars again. |
| `chassis interior glass [r g b a] [smooth] [metal] [premul 0\|1] [inside]` | Tint the glass live. |

### Seat profiles

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis profile list` | List the vehicle codes that have a profile. |
| `chassis profile show [code]` | Print the profile as JSON. Without a code it shows the vehicle you sit in. |
| `chassis profile set <field> <values> [code] [seat]` | Move a value and write the JSON. Fields: `root`, `eyes`, `gripstart`, `gripend`, `elbow`, `foot`, `footrot`, `knee`, `stand`, `handle`, `pushelbow` take `<x> <y> <z>`. `leanstart`, `leanend` take `<x> <y> <z> <w>`. `yaw`, `recovery`, `handrotw`, `footrotw`, `followmax`, `reach` take one value. `handmode` takes `rim`, `fixed` or `wheel`. |
| `chassis profile save [code]` | Write the profile to `UserData/Chassis/<code>.json`. A file there wins over a profile from code. |
| `chassis profile reload` | Read the defaults and the files again. |

### Shots into cars

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis target seat` | Put the nearest NPC on foot within 30 m into the driver's seat of the nearest car (host). |
| `chassis target patrol` | Put the nearest officer on foot into the nearest car and drive the closest patrol route (host). |
| `chassis target near [m]` | Put you `m` metres (default 6) off the left side of the car with the nearest seated NPC, facing it. |
| `chassis target gun` | Equip the first ranged weapon in the hotbar. Run `give revolver` first. |
| `chassis target shoot [head\|body] [n]` | Fire the equipped gun `n` times at the nearest seated NPC, without spread. |
| `chassis target keep on\|off` | Register a `RegisterOccupantDown` handler that keeps every downed NPC in its seat, or remove it. |
| `chassis target list` | List the seated NPCs. |
| `chassis target slump [h f w]` | Print or set the height, forward offset and weight of the slumped pose. |

### Wheelchairs

The wheelchair commands moved to [Rollin](/mods/rollin/guides/console-commands/) as `rollin` commands.

### Test clients

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `chassis creator` | Finish an open character creator with the default looks. |
| `chassis notice` | Close the offense notice after an arrest. |

pages.title: Chassis
pages.description: Vehicle framework for Schedule I: visible seated occupants, hands on the wheel, first-person cabins and new rideables.
pages.markdown:
| | |
|---|---|
| Latest release | `1.8.1` |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Chassis/) |
| Requires | MelonLoader 0.7.3 |
| API | [Reference](/mods/chassis/api/) |
| Help | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/chassis) |

📖 **API documentation:** [docs.doodesch.de/mods/chassis/api/](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/chassis/api/)

> Drivers and passengers sit in the car where you can see them, with their hands on a steering
> wheel that turns. Chassis adds a first person view, a horn, indicators, locks and owners, and a
> base interior for the vanilla cars. Other mods build their vehicles on it.



![Chassis](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/header.jpg)

## Features

- **Visible occupants:** Players and NPCs in a vehicle sit visibly in their seats, police
  included. The driver holds the steering wheel with both hands, and the wheel turns when you
  steer.
- **First person view:** Press `V` in a vehicle to look from your seat. Your body stays visible
  below you, and only your own copy of your head is hidden.
- **Horn:** Press `G`. `H` stays the headlights.
- **Indicators:** The left and right arrow keys switch them on vehicles that have indicator lamps.
  Press the same key again to switch off. After the turn they switch off on their own.
- **Owner and lock per player:** Each player-owned vehicle has an owner, and the owner can lock
  it. A locked vehicle lets in only its owner. Others can ride along while the owner sits
  inside. There is no key for the lock: other mods set it through the API. Vehicles
  from older saves belong to the host.
- **Moving parts:** The steering wheel follows the front wheels.
- **Base interior for the vanilla cars:** Seats, a dashboard, a steering wheel and tinted glass,
  so you can see who sits inside.
- **Working dashboard:** The speedometer and the rev counter move, and lamps show the indicators
  and the headlights. In first person, look at a switch and left-click it: light switch, hazard
  lights, indicator stalk (also with the mouse wheel) and the horn in the wheel centre.
- **Indicators outside:** The vanilla cars flash their own amber indicator lamps. A rear without
  one flashes part of the brake light in red.
- **Shots into cars:** Guns hit NPCs that sit in a car. A driver who goes down falls out next to
  the car, and the car stops.
- **Wheelchairs:** Riding and pushing the wheelchairs moved to its own mod,
  [Rollin](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Rollin). Without Rollin the wheelchairs stay vanilla props.
- **Showroom cars:** The display cars at Hyland Auto can be entered before you buy one. The engine
  starts, but they stay on their display. They are not saved and do not belong to anyone.
- **Key hints:** The keys of the vehicle show at the bottom left, next to the game's own: First
  Person, Horn, and Indicators on vehicles with indicator lamps. While you push a vehicle (Rollin's
  wheelchair) they show Push and Let Go with your own key bindings.
- **Co-op:** Seats, horn, indicators, locks and owners sync through the host.

## Controls

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| `V` | First person view in a vehicle |
| `G` | Horn |
| `H` | Headlights (vanilla) |
| `Left arrow` / `Right arrow` | Indicator left / right. Press again to switch off. |
| `Left click` | In first person: use the switch you look at. A dot in the screen centre shows that you can. |
| `Mouse wheel` | In first person: turn the knob or stalk you look at. |

## Screenshots

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Driver in the seat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/01-seated-driver.jpg) | ![First person view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/02-first-person.jpg) |
| ![Base interior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/03-interior.jpg) | ![NPC driver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/04-npc-driver.jpg) |
| ![Working dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/09-dash.jpg) | ![Indicators outside](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/10-indicators.jpg) |
| ![Key hints](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/main/docs/img/08-key-hints.jpg) | |

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


| Component | Version / Source |
|-----------|------------------|
| Schedule I | `0.4.7f12` (IL2CPP, current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | [`0.7.3+`](https://github.com/LavaGang/MelonLoader) |

Every player in a co-op session needs Chassis.


</details>

<details><summary>Installation</summary>


### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

Install with a mod manager (r2modman / Gale) from the Schedule I community. MelonLoader comes in
as a dependency.

### Manual

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I ([melonwiki.xyz](https://melonwiki.xyz/)).
2. Drop **`Chassis.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.


</details>

## Configuration

Settings live in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `Chassis`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `BaseInterior` | `true` | Seats, dashboard, steering wheel and tinted glass for the vanilla cars, and visible NPC drivers. |
| `SpeedUnit` | `kmh` | `kmh` or `mph`: the speedometer and the odometer. |

## For mod authors

The public API is the static class `ChassisApi` in the namespace `Chassis.Api`
([`Api/`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/blob/v1.8.1/Api/)). Reference `Chassis.dll` and add Chassis as a dependency of your package.
Every type and member: [API reference](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/chassis/api/).
Developers and AI coding agents: read [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/blob/v1.8.1/AGENTS.md) - depend on the API, do not copy the source.

- **Profiles:** A `ChassisProfile` per vehicle code holds seats, steering wheel, lids, lamps,
  horn and interior. `ChassisApi.Register` adds one from code, `ChassisApi.Assign` gives one
  vehicle the profile of another code, and `ChassisApi.FitSeat` makes a first seat profile from a
  vanilla seat. `Changed` reports every change.
- **JSON files:** Profiles also load from `UserData/Chassis/<vehicle code>.json`. A file wins
  over a profile from code, so a player can always correct the values. `ChassisApi.Save` writes
  the current profile to its file.
- **Horn, indicators, parts:** `Honk`, `SetIndicator`, `Indicator`, `IndicatorLit`,
  `IndicatorChanged`, `SetPart`, `PartOpen`, `SetStorageEnd`, `RegisterSound`.
- **Owner and lock:** `OwnerOf`, `IsMine`, `IsLocked`, `SetLocked`, `SetOwner` (host),
  `OwnersChanged`, `ResolveUnknownOwner` (host, for vehicles without a record).
- **First person:** `FirstPersonActive`, `FirstPersonKey`, `FirstPersonChanged`.
- **Key hints:** `AddKeyHint` puts your own key into the key hints, `RemoveKeyHint` takes it
  out. The `show` callback gets a `KeyHintContext` (`Vehicle`, `Profile`, `Seat`, `Driver`,
  `Pushing`).
- **NPCs that go down in a seat:** `RegisterOccupantDown` decides whether a shot NPC stays slumped
  in its seat instead of falling out (host only). The handler gets an `OccupantDown` (`Vehicle`,
  `Npc`, `Seat`, `Dead`); `RemoveOccupantDown` takes it out.

### Interiors, gauges and switches

- **Your own interior:** `SetInterior(code, vehicle => yourPrefabInstance, profile => ...)`
  replaces the base interior's seats, dashboard and wheel for one vehicle code. The lining and the
  tinted glass stay unless the callback turns them off. The callback names your wheel, gauges and
  switches in the profile.
- **Gauges:** `ChassisProfile.Gauges` binds a transform by name or path to a source. Kinds:
  `needle` (turns between `From` and `To`), `lamp` (glows above `Threshold`) and `digits` (text).
- **Sources:** `GaugeSources` lists them: speed, rpm, throttle, handbrake, lamps, steering, clock,
  odometer, trip, occupied, driver. `RegisterGaugeSource` adds your own. `Telemetry(vehicle)`
  reads all of them at once, each with a `Valid` flag. Throttle and handbrake reach passengers
  about 0.4 s late.
- **Switches:** `ChassisProfile.Controls` makes a transform clickable in first person: `button`,
  `toggle` or `knob`. Built-in actions are `lights`, `hazard`, `indicator`, `horn` and
  `trip_reset`; `RegisterControlAction` adds your own. Clicks go through the host, and toggle and
  knob states are saved with the vehicle.
- **Events:** `ControlUsed`, `HeadlightsChanged`, `BrakeChanged`, `ReverseChanged`,
  `DriverChanged`.
- **Console:** `chassis telemetry` prints every source with its validity and every bound gauge
  and switch of your car. `chassis zones` shows the hit zones of the switches. Both work in the
  release build. A gauge or switch whose path is not found logs one warning per vehicle code.
- **Debug build:** every GitHub release also carries `Chassis_<version>_debug.zip`. It adds the
  developer console commands, among them `chassis profile` (edit and save seat profiles live),
  `chassis interior`, `aim`, `click` and `ctl`; `chassis help` lists them all. Players use the
  normal build.
- **Example:** [`Examples/ChassisCockpitExample`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Chassis/blob/v1.8.1/Examples/ChassisCockpitExample) gives the
  Shitbox a cockpit of its own with a speedometer, odometer digits and a beacon switch.

### Tuning

A vehicle's tuning is a list of keys that your mod writes through `ChassisApi`, for example a tuning
shop or a garage app. The host checks each change against the vehicle's owner, syncs it to every
player and saves it with the vehicle.

- **Parts:** `RegisterTuningPart` adds a part with its own model, fit and driving factors (torque,
  gearing, brake, grip, steer, mass, spring, damper, downforce, ride height). `InstallPart` and
  `RemovePart` fit it to a vehicle. Built-in parts: engine, brakes and transmission stages 1-3,
  suspension 1-4, turbo and drift tyres.
- **Looks:** `SetPaint` (primary and secondary, with a finish), `SetRimColor`, `SetXenon`,
  `SetNeon`, `SetWindowTint`, `SetTyreSmoke` and `SetHorn`.
- **Paint on your own model:** `SetPaintTargets` names the material slots that take the body paint,
  per vehicle or per vehicle code. Without targets the paint goes on the vanilla body. A target
  marked `Secondary` takes the second paint instead (stripes, trim); `HasSecondPaint` tells a shop
  to offer it. A target marked `Flat` drops its colour texture while painted, for a dark or two-toned
  texture that would darken the paint. `PaintTargetsOf` reads them. `PaintRenderers` paints slots that belong to no vehicle, for a model
  that stays when its vehicle is gone.
- **Your own keys:** `SetTuning`, `GetTuning` and `ClearTuning`.
- **Preview:** `PreviewTuning`, `PreviewPart` and `EndPreview` show a change on this machine only,
  without the host and without saving, for a shop that shows a part before the player buys it.
  `IsPreviewing` and `ShownTuning` read it.
- **Read:** `Tuning`, `InstalledPart`, `TuningStatsOf` (the driving factors in effect) and the
  event `TuningChanged`.
- **Example:** [Rollin](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Rollin) builds the wheelchair
  on Chassis and tunes it with rockets, spoilers, neon and hats.

## Building from source

The project compiles two targets from one source tree: `net6.0` for IL2CPP and `netstandard2.1`
for Mono. It reads the game and MelonLoader reference DLLs from `../Workspace/lib/<il2cpp|mono>/`
(`game/` and `melonloader/`). Point `WorkspaceLibPath` at another folder with the same layout if
needed.

```sh
dotnet build Chassis.csproj -c Release                         # both targets
dotnet build Chassis.csproj -c Release -f netstandard2.1       # Mono only
dotnet build Chassis.csproj -c Release -p:WorkspaceLibPath=/path/to/lib
```

The IL2CPP build is at `bin/Release/net6.0/Chassis.dll`. Debug builds add console commands
(`chassis help`).

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


- **DooDesch** - mod author.


</details>

pages.title: CategoryRef
pages.description: Fluent handle to a declared category.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class CategoryRef
```

Namespace `Clipwise.Api`

Fluent handle to a declared category. Every [`Item`](#item) call lands in it, so the source and category key are stated once.

## Properties

### Source

```csharp
public string Source { get; }
```

The registering mod's reverse-DNS id.

**Value** E.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed". Empty when null was passed.

### Id

```csharp
public string Id { get; }
```

The category's id within [`Source`](#source).

**Value** E.g. "bred". Empty when null was passed.

### Key

```csharp
public string Key { get; }
```

The canonical `"source:id"` key this category is addressed by.

**Value** E.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed:bred". Pass it as the category of [`Clipboard.RegisterItem`](../clipboard/#registeritem).

## Methods

### Item

```csharp
public CategoryRef Item(
    string id,
    string itemId,
    string[] tags = null,
    int sortOrder = 0,
    string sortKey = null,
    string description = null,
    int precedence = 0)
```

Place an item in this category. See [`Clipboard.RegisterItem`](../clipboard/#registeritem) for the parameters.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | This mod's own key for the entry, e.g. "headband". |
| `itemId` | The game's `ItemDefinition.ID`, e.g. "b2s_headband_seed". |
| `tags` | Namespaced filter tags, e.g. `new[] { "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1" }`. |
| `sortOrder` | Position inside the category, lower first. |
| `sortKey` | Text that orders entries inside the category, e.g. "Headband". Null uses the display name. |
| `description` | Tooltip text. Null shows none. |
| `precedence` | Higher wins when several sources claim the same item; default 0. |

**Returns** This handle, for chaining.

pages.title: Clipboard
pages.description: Clipwise's modder API.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public static class Clipboard
```

Namespace `Clipwise.Api`

Clipwise's modder API. Reference Clipwise.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod.

The management clipboard shows every selectable item of a field in one flat, unscrollable icon grid. Clipwise replaces that with a searchable, tabbed picker. Tell it which category your items belong to and they get their own tab instead of being mixed into the vanilla ones.

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when Clipwise is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so this can ship unconditionally with no hard dependency. Registration order does not matter: calls made before Clipwise loads are queued and replayed on bind.

```csharp
using Clipwise.Api;
Clipboard.Category("doodesch.breedtoseed", "tier-1", "Bred - Tier 1", sortOrder: 100)
         .Item("headband", "b2s_headband_seed", sortKey: "Headband",
               tags: new[] { "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1" });
```

Tip: a class named `ClipwiseProbe` with a static `Register()` is auto-discovered and called on bind (see [`AutoRegister`](#autoregister)), so a mod's Core does not have to wire anything.

Identifiers: `source` is the reverse-DNS id of the registering mod (`"doodesch.breedtoseed"`). A category's canonical key is `"source:id"`. Tags MUST be namespaced the same way (`"doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1"`) - bare tags are rejected by the host so two unrelated mods cannot fight over a name like "tier3". The `clipwise:` namespace is reserved for the host.

All calls MUST be made from the Unity main thread.

A source and a category id must not be empty and must not contain ":" or whitespace; the host rejects them otherwise. The source "clipwise" is reserved for the host. An item id (`ItemDefinition.ID`) is matched without case. A tag is "namespace:path" with both parts non-empty, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1"; a tag without a namespace or in the "clipwise" namespace is dropped. Sort orders sort lower first.

**Example**

A tab of its own for a mod's seeds, with a labelled tag chip, from a probe class:

```csharp
internal static class ClipwiseProbe
{
    public static void Register()
    {
        Clipboard.RegisterTagLabel("mymod.seeds:tier/1", "Tier 1");
        Clipboard.Category("mymod.seeds", "bred", "My Seeds", sortOrder: 100)
                 .Item("lemon", "mymod_lemon_seed", tags: new[] { "mymod.seeds:tier/1" }, sortKey: "Lemon");
    }
}
```

## Properties

### Available

```csharp
public static bool Available { get; }
```

True only when the Clipwise host is installed AND bound. Rarely needed - the API is a safe no-op when absent.

### AbiVersion

```csharp
public static int AbiVersion { get; }
```

The host's ABI version: 0 when Clipwise is absent, 1 for the initial contract. Use this only to gate on capabilities added in a later ABI; everything below degrades to a no-op on its own.

**Value** 0 without Clipwise. 1 for the initial contract. 2 once [`Facts`](#facts) is available.

## Methods

### Category

```csharp
public static CategoryRef Category(
    string source,
    string id,
    string label,
    int sortOrder = 0,
    string iconItemId = null)
```

Types: [`CategoryRef`](../categoryref/)

Declare a category - one tab in the picker. `sortOrder` orders the tabs (lower first; vanilla sits at 0). `iconItemId` optionally names an item whose icon represents the tab. Returns a fluent builder for the items in it. Load-order-proof.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `source` | The reverse-DNS id of the registering mod, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed". No ":" and no whitespace; "clipwise" is reserved. |
| `id` | The category id within the source, e.g. "bred". No ":" and no whitespace. The tab's key is "<source>:<id>". |
| `label` | The tab text, e.g. "Breed to Seed Strains". Null or blank shows the id. |
| `sortOrder` | Tab position, lower first. Vanilla sits at 0. Equal values sort by key. |
| `iconItemId` | An `ItemDefinition.ID`, e.g. "b2s_headband_seed". Null or blank sets no icon item. |

**Returns** A handle that places items in this category.

### RegisterCategory

```csharp
public static void RegisterCategory(
    string source,
    string id,
    string label,
    int sortOrder = 0,
    string iconItemId = null)
```

Same as [`Category`](#category) without the builder, for callers that keep their own loop.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `source` | As in [`Category`](#category). |
| `id` | As in [`Category`](#category). |
| `label` | As in [`Category`](#category). |
| `sortOrder` | As in [`Category`](#category). |
| `iconItemId` | As in [`Category`](#category). |

### RegisterItem

```csharp
public static void RegisterItem(
    string source,
    string id,
    string itemId,
    string category,
    string[] tags = null,
    int sortOrder = 0,
    string sortKey = null,
    string description = null,
    int precedence = 0)
```

Place one item in a category. `id` is this mod's own stable key for the entry, unique within `source`; `itemId` is the game's `ItemDefinition.ID` the entry stands for; `category` is a canonical category key (`"source:id"`). `sortKey` orders entries inside the category (falls back to the item's display name); `description` shows up in the tooltip; `precedence` breaks ties when several sources claim the same item (higher wins).

Returns nothing on purpose: a call queued before Clipwise loaded cannot know whether the future host accepts it. Re-registering the same (source, id) is an idempotent upsert, so calling this twice is safe. Load-order-proof.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `source` | The reverse-DNS id of the registering mod, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed". No ":" and no whitespace. |
| `id` | This mod's own key for the entry, e.g. "headband". Null or blank is rejected. |
| `itemId` | The game's `ItemDefinition.ID`, e.g. "b2s_headband_seed". Matched without case. Null or blank is rejected. |
| `category` | A category key "<source>:<id>", e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed:bred". Null or blank places the item as if it were not registered. A key that was never declared shows as a tab with a label made from its id. |
| `tags` | Namespaced filter tags, e.g. `new[] { "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1" }`. Bare tags and tags in the "clipwise" namespace are dropped. Null adds no tags. |
| `sortOrder` | Position inside the category, lower first. Equal values fall back to `sortKey`. |
| `sortKey` | Text that orders entries inside the category without case, e.g. "Headband". Null uses the display name. It never changes the shown name. |
| `description` | Tooltip text. Null or blank shows none. |
| `precedence` | Higher wins when several sources claim the same item; default 0. A user override file beats every API claim. Equal precedence goes to the claim whose source, then id, sorts first. |

### RegisterTagLabel

```csharp
public static void RegisterTagLabel(string tag, string label)
```

Give a tag a human-readable label for its filter chip, e.g. `"mymod:tier/1"` -> `"Tier 1"`. Without this the chip shows the tag's last path segment. Load-order-proof.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `tag` | The full tag, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1". Null or empty is ignored. |
| `label` | The chip text, e.g. "Tier 1". Null or empty is ignored. Registering the same tag again replaces it. |

### Facts

```csharp
public static void Facts(string source, Func<string, string> provider)
```

Answer for your own items with extra rows on the picker's detail card.

`provider` is handed one `ItemDefinition.ID` and returns one `"LABEL value"` line per row, separated by newlines. An empty answer, a blank value or a missing line simply leaves that row OUT - never show a label with nothing under it.

```csharp
Clipboard.Facts("doodesch.breedtoseed", itemId =>
{
    StrainDef s = StrainTable.BySeedId(itemId);
    if (s == null) return null;
    string who = Register.ShownName(s);          // live, and never the raw Steam name
    return who == null ? null : "DISCOVERED BY	" + who;
});
```

ASKED EVERY TIME THE PICKER OPENS, never cached. That is why this takes a callback rather than a string: a name that resolves against a live register has to be read live, or a player who renames themselves keeps seeing the old name here after every other surface has caught up.

Only the source that registered an item is asked about it. Load-order-proof; no-op without Clipwise; needs host ABI 2.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `source` | The source that registered the items, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed". One provider per source; a second call replaces the first. |
| `provider` | Gets the `ItemDefinition.ID` and returns lines of label, a tab character and value, e.g. `"DISCOVERED BY\tAlex"`. Lines are split at `\n` and both parts are trimmed. Null or empty shows no rows. At most 12 rows show. A throw leaves the rows out and logs a warning. |

### AutoRegister

```csharp
public static void AutoRegister()
```

Discover a convention type named `ClipwiseProbe` with a static `Register()` in THIS mod's own assembly and invoke it once - so a mod never has to wire a Register() call into its Core. Drive it from a `[ModuleInitializer]` in the probe file. No-op + load-order-proof.
