- **Relations.** Pick the NPCs that know yours and how the player unlocks them.
- **Test.** Pick a save; the game restarts into it and puts you right next to your NPC.
- **Phone app.** In a loaded save, jump to an NPC, set its start point or a route stop where you
  stand, and see a look change on the live NPC.
- **Projects.** Saved as you go, with undo and redo, a history to step back to, and edits on several
  NPCs at once. Import any installed Personnel pack as a project.
- **Installed packs.** Switch a pack on or off, or remove it, from the start page.
- **Publish.** Builds a Thunderstore-ready zip (manifest, README, LICENSE) under
  `UserData/Personify/Exports/`.
- **Inkorporated tattoos.** If [Inkorporated](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Inkorporated)
  is installed, its tattoo packs appear in the tattoo picker; the art is copied into your pack.

## Screenshots

| | |
|---|---|
| ![The Look area with the live 3D preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify/main/docs/img/editor-look.jpg) | ![The Role area of a customer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify/main/docs/img/editor-role.jpg) |
| ![The Routine area with the day on the town map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify/main/docs/img/editor-routine.jpg) | ![The phone app in a loaded save](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify/main/docs/img/phone-app.jpg) |

![An NPC from the editor in town](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify/main/docs/img/in-town.jpg)

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


| Component | Version / Source |
|-----------|------------------|
| Schedule I | IL2CPP (current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+` |
| S1API | [ifBars/S1API_Forked](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ifBars/S1API_Forked/) `3.2.1+` |
| Side Hustle | [DooDesch-SideHustle](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/SideHustle/) `3.2.1+` - the hub the editor opens from |
| Sideload | [DooDesch-Sideload](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Sideload/) `1.36.0+` - draws the editor and the phone app |
| Personnel | [DooDesch-Personnel](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Personnel/) `2.4.4+` - runs your NPCs in the game |
| Inkorporated | optional - its tattoo packs show up in the tattoo picker |


</details>

<details><summary>Installation</summary>


### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager
Install with r2modman / Gale from the Schedule I community; the dependencies are pulled in
automatically.

### Manual
1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **S1API**, **Side Hustle**, **Sideload** and **Personnel**.
3. Drop **`Personify.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.


</details>

## Usage

1. Main menu -> **Side Hustle** -> **Personify**.
2. Create a project (it becomes your pack) and add NPCs with **+ New NPC**.
3. Work through **Look**, **Role**, **Routine** and **Relations**. The problems list names what is
   still missing.
4. **Add to my game** installs the pack. **Test** starts a save of your choice next to the NPC.
5. **Publish** writes the zip to `UserData/Personify/Exports/`. Add a 256x256 `icon.png` before you
   upload it to Thunderstore.

Tips:

- Escape or right-click steps back one level. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y undo and redo.
- Select several NPCs in the list to change them together.
- **History** in the project menu steps a project back to an earlier state.
- Own tattoos come from [Inkubator](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Inkubator): install its export as
  an Inkorporated pack and the tattoos show up in the picker.
- The NPC id (`packname_npcname`) is what other mods reference; renaming an NPC changes it.

## Configuration

No settings. Projects are stored under `UserData/Personify/Projects/`, exports under
`UserData/Personify/Exports/`. Projects from 1.x open as they are.

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


- **DooDesch** - mod author.
- **[ifBars/S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API)** - the modding API this is built on.


</details>

pages.title: API
pages.description: Public, stable entry point for other mods (e.g.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public static class API
```

Namespace `Personnel`

Public, stable entry point for other mods (e.g. Backrooms) that want to consume user-authored NPC definitions. Reference Personnel.dll and declare `[MelonOptionalDependencies("Personnel")]`. The primitive most consumers need is [`BuildAvatarSettings`](#buildavatarsettings) / [`ApplyAppearance`](#applyappearance) - realise a definition's look onto any live `Avatar`. Definitions are loaded from packs on startup; register your own programmatically via [`Register`](#register).

A definition id is lower case: letters and digits, every other run of characters turned into "_". A pack entry uses its authored `id`, or else `<packId or folder name>_<npc name>`, e.g. "examples_pale". Packs load from UserData/Personnel/Packs/<pack>/manifest.json on startup.

**Example**

Give a live avatar the look of a pack NPC:

```csharp
if (Personnel.API.TryGet("examples_pale", out var def))
{
    Personnel.API.ApplyAppearance(avatar, def);
    Personnel.API.ApplyDistortion(avatar, def);
}
```

## Properties

### All

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<NpcDef> All { get; }
```

All loaded NPC definitions (pack-sourced + API-registered).

**Value** Pack-sourced and API-registered definitions together. Empty when no pack is installed and nothing was registered.

## Methods

### TryGet

```csharp
public static bool TryGet(string id, out NpcDef def)
```

Look up a definition by id (case-insensitive).

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | A definition id such as "examples_pale", the same value as `Id`. Null or blank returns false. |
| `def` | The first definition with that id, or null when the method returns false. |

### Register

```csharp
public static bool Register(NpcDef def)
```

Register a definition programmatically (de-duplicated by Source/Id). Returns false on duplicate.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `def` | The definition. `Id` must be set, or the call returns false. An empty `Source` becomes "API". A second definition with the same Source and Id, ignoring case, returns false. Leave `PackDir` null: a definition with a PackDir counts as pack-sourced and [`Reload`](#reload) drops it. |

### BuildAvatarSettings

```csharp
public static AvatarSettings BuildAvatarSettings(NpcDef def)
```

Realise a definition's appearance into a vanilla `AvatarSettings`. Registers any custom PNG layers on first use. Call from the main thread (it touches Unity resources).

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `def` | The definition, e.g. from [`TryGet`](#tryget). |

**Returns** The settings, or null when `def` is null.

### ApplyAppearance

```csharp
public static bool ApplyAppearance(Avatar avatar, NpcDef def)
```

Build the definition's `AvatarSettings` and load it onto a live avatar.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `avatar` | A live avatar in the scene. |
| `def` | The definition, e.g. from [`TryGet`](#tryget). |

**Returns** false when the avatar or the definition is null or no settings could be built.

### ApplyDistortion

```csharp
public static void ApplyDistortion(Avatar avatar, NpcDef def)
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Apply a definition's extreme body distortion (Personify's Experimental tab: bone scale/hide, mesh hide) onto a live avatar. A separate pass from [`ApplyAppearance`](#applyappearance) since vanilla AvatarSettings has no such concept - call this right after loading the normal appearance.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `avatar` | A live avatar, with its normal appearance already loaded. |
| `def` | The definition. Its `Appearance.Distortion` keys are the bones "HeadBone", "HipBone", "LeftFootBone", "RightFootBone", "LeftShoulder", "RightShoulder", "MiddleSpine", "LowerSpine" and "LowestSpine", which take a scale or a hide, plus "FaceMesh" and "BodyMesh0", "BodyMesh1" and so on, which only take a hide. A bone missing from the dictionary goes back to scale 1 and visible. Other keys are ignored. |

### Reload

```csharp
public static void Reload()
```

Rescan the packs folder (drops+reloads pack-sourced defs, keeps API-registered ones).

### ConfigureFromDef

```csharp
public static void ConfigureFromDef(NPCPrefabBuilder builder, NpcDef def)
```

Configures an S1API `NPCPrefabBuilder` from a definition - identity + full appearance (+ the def's spawn position if it has one). This is the one call needed to turn a Personnel definition into a real, networked, save/load-safe S1API NPC. Prefer subclassing `PersonnelNpc` (which calls this for you); call this directly only if you keep your own `NPC` subclass and want to configure it inside its `ConfigurePrefab`.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `builder` | The builder S1API passes to your NPC's `ConfigurePrefab`. |
| `def` | The definition. Its `SaveId`, or else its Id, becomes the S1API identity that saves store. The display name splits at the first space into first and last name; an empty name becomes "NPC". |

**Example**

```csharp
protected override void ConfigurePrefab(NPCPrefabBuilder builder)
{
    if (Personnel.API.TryGet("examples_pale", out var def))
        Personnel.API.ConfigureFromDef(builder, def);
}
```

### AddMapMarker

```csharp
public static void AddMapMarker(GameObject npcRoot)
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Adds a map marker (the game's own `NPCPoI`) to a live custom NPC so players can find it on the phone map. Client-local and cosmetic - no economy role, no networking. Safe to call once the NPC object exists (e.g. from `PersonnelNpc`'s creation hook); no-ops if the map manager or NPC component is not ready.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `npcRoot` | The NPC's root object, the one that carries the game's `NPC` component, e.g. `gameObject` inside the NPC class. |

pages.title: Personnel API
pages.description: Look up every public type and member of Personnel 2.4.5.
pages.markdown:
## Use this API

Reference `Personnel.dll` from your Mods folder:

```xml
<Reference Include="Personnel">
  <HintPath>$(ModsDirectory)\Personnel.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Personnel")]
```

Without Personnel its types are missing too. Call it only after you know it loaded.

First steps: [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/).

Source: [`API.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personnel/blob/v2.4.5/API.cs) at `v2.4.5`.

pages.title: Personnel changelog
pages.description: Every released version of Personnel and what changed in it.
pages.markdown:
All notable changes to Personnel are documented here. This project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [2.4.5] - 2026-10-31

### Fixed

- NPCs from packs no longer hang sideways in the air and stand still after you load a save from the menu.

## [2.4.4] - 2026-10-31

### Fixed

- Personnel loads with MLVScan again. MLVScan 2.1.7 disabled it for a hidden PowerShell window behind Personify's Test
  button, which also took Personify and NPC Cards down.

## [2.4.3] - 2026-10-31

### Fixed

- Installed cards converted from another mod now list their original author. Cards installed earlier show it after
  the next install.

## [2.4.2] - 2026-10-31

### Fixed

- Big heads, tiny heads, missing heads and hidden faces from NPC packs now show on NPCs in the world. They worked
  only in the editor.
- Custom body pictures on NPCs draw in their list position again. They no longer vanish under underwear or clothing.

## [2.4.1] - 2026-10-30

### Fixed

- NPCs from cards and packs wear their shirts and trousers again. Many walked around in underwear.

## [2.4.0] - 2026-10-29

### Added

- NPC cards: install NPCs from NPC Vault (personify.doomods.com) or from card images in `UserData/Personnel/Import`.
- Console: `personnel cards` lists installed cards, `personnel card import` and `personnel card remove` add and
  remove one, `personnel connect` links the game to your NPC Vault account.

### For mod authors

- `CardsApi` lists, installs and removes cards, browses NPC Vault, links a device and uploads. NPC Cards and
  Personify use it.

## [2.3.0] - 2026-10-29

### Added

- Pack NPCs can be suppliers: they sell seeds and other goods by phone and drop them off like the game's own
  suppliers.
- Pack NPCs can carry their own contact picture in the phone.
- Pack NPCs can say their own lines: greetings, phone messages and answers. Lines a pack leaves out stay the
  game's.

### For mod authors

- Manifest `schemaVersion: 3` adds the `supplier` block, `portrait` (a PNG in the pack) and `lines`. Packs with
  schema 1 and 2 load unchanged. Format: the pack format guide on docs.doodesch.de.
- `UserData/Personify/World/npcs.json` lists every NPC of the loaded save (id, name, region, role, source).
- `Personnel.Testing.LaunchMarker.Write(saveSlot, npcId)` loads that save on the next start and puts the player
  next to the NPC; `RestartGame()` restarts the game for it.

## [2.2.3] - 2026-10-21

### Fixed

- The example NPC Errand Eddie shows up in Northtown and works at the Motel Office. Before, he never spawned in
  the world.
- Custom NPCs no longer turn into a flat grey figure when you load a second save without restarting the game.

### Changed

- With `LoadExamplePack` on, an unchanged example pack from an older version is updated. One you edited is kept.

## [2.2.2] - 2026-10-16

### Fixed

- Customers made in Personify can buy again and no longer freeze facing you after a deal attempt.

### Changed

- A customer with connections starts locked and opens with a free sample, like vanilla customers.

## [2.2.1] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed

- Custom tattoos and face layers from packs show on NPCs again on game 0.4.7.
- A pack car without a position spawns where its NPC starts, not at the edge of the map.

### Changed

- Needs S1API 3.2.1, up from 3.1.1. Update it along with the mod.

## [2.2.0] - 2026-08-13

### Fixed

- An NPC whose pack sets only a skin colour gets matching eyelids. They fell back to the default tan, which
  read as pale lids on any dark skin.
- Face layers are placed the way the game reads them: the mouth first, the facial hair second. A pack that
  listed them in another order had a detail layer drawn in the hair colour.
- Face layers past the fifth are dropped and named in the log. They used to overwrite the facial hair instead.
- Body layers past the eighth are dropped on the S1API prefab path too. Only the runtime path had that
  ceiling, so a prefab NPC lost a garment with nothing said.

## [2.1.1] - 2026-08-01

### Changed

- Runs on Schedule I 0.4.6f11.
- Needs S1API 3.1.1, up from 3.0.5. Update it along with the mod.

## [2.1.0] - 2026-07-30

Writing a schedule meant guessing coordinates, because the game shows none anywhere. Now the console
hands them to you.

### Added

- Dev-console commands for pack authors (console has to be enabled in Settings):
  - `personnel pos [HH:MM]` - the spot you are standing on, as `[x, y, z]` or as a finished `walkTo`
    action for that time.
  - `personnel spawn` - the same spot as a `spawn` block, with `rotationY` and `region` filled in.
  - `personnel route HH:MM` - collects a step per stop in `UserData/Personnel/route.json`;
    `personnel route show` prints the block ready to paste into `"schedule": [ ... ]`, `clear`
    starts over.
  - `personnel npcs [filter]` - loaded definitions, and where the physical ones are right now.
  - `personnel help` - the list.
- Results are copied to the clipboard and written to the MelonLoader log, with an in-game
  notification confirming the command ran.

## [2.0.0] - 2026-07-22

NPC mods without code: a pack manifest can now describe everything an NPC needs - where it spawns,
what it does all day, its economy role - and Personnel spawns it as a real world NPC on its own.

### Added

- `autoRegister` (pack level) / `spawn.auto` (per NPC): Personnel registers opted-in NPCs as real,
  networked, saved world NPCs with no consumer mod involved. A kill switch lives in the settings
  (`EnableAutoRegister`). Packs that already ship a consumer DLL are safe: a compiled NPC class for
  the same id always wins over the generated one.
- `spawn` grew `rotationY` (spawn yaw), `region` (now actually applied) and `physical`. Non-physical
  NPCs are phone contacts only - no world body, no pathing cost. Default: physical exactly when the
  NPC has a schedule.
- `schedule`: full daily schedules in the manifest - `walkTo`, `stayInBuilding`, `sit`,
  `useVendingMachine`, `useAtm`, `useSlotMachine`, `locationDialogue`, `locationAction`,
  `driveToCarPark`, `dealSignal`. Times are `"HH:MM"` strings.
- `relationships`: `delta`, `unlocked`, `unlockType`, `connections` (by NPC id).
- `customer`: the whole customer economy - spending, orders per week, preferred day/time, standards,
  direct approach, first sample, mutual relation requirement, call-police chance, dependence,
  affinities, preferred properties.
- `dealer`: type, cut, signing fee, home, completed-deals variable, quality tolerances. Definitions
  with a dealer block now get the proper dealer base prefab (previously manifest dealers were built
  on the civilian prefab).
- `inventory`: random cash range, startup items (with quantities), clear-each-night.
- `contact`: `mapMarker: false` removes the phone-map marker, `visible: false` (experimental) skips
  the contact unlock.
- `behavior.aggression`, `maxHealth` and `scale` are now actually applied to spawned NPCs.
- Id stability: an authored `id` in the manifest is respected (previously always derived from folder
  and name), `packId` pins the derivation prefix, and `saveId` lets a renamed NPC keep matching old
  saves. `schemaVersion` marks the manifest format (current: 2).
- Distant custom NPCs get a proper billboard impostor instead of a blank one (on S1API builds that
  support impostor configuration).

### Changed

- Pack and NPC registration order is now deterministic across machines - co-op peers agree on it.
- Contact unlock and map marker are unchanged by default but can be opted out per NPC.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-07-08

### Fixed

- Custom NPCs now show their real name in the phone Contacts app (previously "???") and can be found
  on the map. Personnel unlocks each spawned NPC's contact and gives it a map marker.
- Clothing no longer carries over from one spawned NPC to the next. The game clears only six of its
  eight avatar layer slots, so an NPC with more layers than that leaves a garment bound to the material
  for whoever is applied after it.
- A definition asking for more than eight body layers no longer loses one at random. The surplus is
  dropped deliberately, clothing first, and named in the log.

### Added

- Opt-in economy roles via a pack's `behavior.conversation`: `"customer"` or `"dealer"` makes the NPC
  a real customer or dealer, while the default `"none"` stays a plain, non-economy contact.
- `API.AddMapMarker(GameObject)` to add a map marker to any live custom NPC.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-07-06

Initial release.

### Added

- NPC pack loading from `UserData/Personnel/Packs/<PackName>/` (`manifest.json` + optional PNGs),
  with per-pack log lines listing the loaded NPC ids.
- Deep appearance definitions mirroring the S1API avatar-settings surface: body, skin, hair, face,
  eyes, eyebrows, clothing layers, accessories, and custom PNG layers loaded from the pack folder.
- Duplicate-proof NPC ids, always derived as `packname_npcname` (normalized); manifest `id` fields
  are ignored.
- `PersonnelNpc` base class: one tiny subclass per NPC turns a pack definition into a full S1API NPC
  (prefab, networking, save/load handled by S1API).
- Public API: `All`, `TryGet`, `Register`, `BuildAvatarSettings(def)`, `ApplyAppearance(avatar, def)`,
  `ConfigureFromDef(builder, def)`, `OnReloaded`, `Reload`.
- Bundled example pack (off by default, `LoadExamplePack`) with two NPCs as a copyable template.
- Mod Manager & Phone App settings integration.

pages.title: Add a custom PNG layer
pages.description: Ship your own face paint, tattoo or shirt print on a Personnel NPC with a PNG file.
pages.markdown:
Add your own art to an NPC with a PNG in the pack folder. Custom layers work like [Inkorporated](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Inkorporated) tattoos and follow the same rules.

**You need:** an NPC pack. See [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/).

## Steps

1. Know the rule: the PNG is a full UV-space skin texture, not a sticker. The body shares one UV unwrap for torso, arms and legs. The face has its own. The opaque pixels must sit at the UV position of the target body part. Everything else must be transparent. A shape centered on a blank canvas lands wherever the UV center is, often on the legs or arms.
2. Create the PNG with a transparent background (RGBA). Use 2048x2048 for body layers and 512x512 for face layers. There is no size limit. Resolution changes sharpness only, not placement.
3. Paint over aligned art. The PNGs of the Inkorporated example pack are aligned to the same UVs. So are the files in the `Templates/` folder that a DEBUG build of Inkorporated exports.
4. Put the PNG next to `manifest.json` in the pack folder.
5. Reference it in the manifest. Use `faceLayers` for face art and `bodyLayers` for body art:
   ```json
   "faceLayers": [ { "file": "warpaint.png", "tint": "#FFFFFF" } ],
   "bodyLayers": [ { "file": "sleeve.png",   "tint": "#C0FFEE" } ]
   ```
6. Restart the game.

Colour art works. The default tint is white, and the manifest `tint` multiplies over the PNG.

## Check it works

The NPC shows the art on the intended body part. The [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify) editor previews a PNG live on the menu character. Use it to check alignment before you restart the game.

If the art lands on the wrong part, check the UV alignment first. Then check that a face design is in `faceLayers` and a body design is in `bodyLayers`.

## Next

- [Pack format](/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/)
- [Multiplayer and saves](/mods/personnel/guides/multiplayer-and-saves/)
- [Troubleshooting](/mods/personnel/guides/troubleshooting/)

pages.title: Make an NPC pack
pages.description: Write a manifest.json that adds your own NPC to Schedule I, with no code.
pages.markdown:
Write a pack folder with one `manifest.json`. Personnel loads it and spawns your NPC in the world.

**You need:** Personnel and S1API installed. See [Install](/install/) for MelonLoader, S1API and the mod DLL.

## Steps

1. Create the folder `Schedule I/UserData/Personnel/Packs/MyPack/`.
2. Create `manifest.json` in that folder:
   ```json
   {
     "name": "My Pack",
     "author": "you",
     "autoRegister": true,
     "npcs": [
       {
         "id": "mypack_pale",
         "name": "Pale",
         "appearance": { "skinColor": "#8899AA", "hairPath": "Avatar/Hair/Spiky/Spiky" },
         "spawn": { "x": -64.25, "y": 1.07, "z": 84.49, "rotationY": 325, "region": "Northtown", "physical": true }
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
3. Set the spawn point. Stand where the NPC must appear. Enable the console in Settings, press the backtick key, and run `personnel spawn`. Paste the result into `spawn`.
4. Optional: add a `schedule`. Walk to each stop and run `personnel route 07:00`. Then run `personnel route show` and paste the steps into `"schedule": [ ... ]`.
5. Restart the game. Pack changes need a restart.

To start from a working pack, set `LoadExamplePack` to `true` under `[Personnel_01_Main]` in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg`. Restart. Personnel writes `UserData/Personnel/Packs/Examples/`. An unedited older example pack is updated. An edited one is never touched.

To design the look in a live editor, use [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify). Export the pack and copy the `Personnel/Packs/<name>` folder into `UserData/Personnel/Packs/`.

## Check it works

`MelonLoader/Latest.log` lists each pack with its ids:

```
[Personnel] Pack 'MyPack' (My Pack): 1 NPC(s) [mypack_pale].
```

In game, the NPC stands at the spawn point.

If you do not set `autoRegister`, Personnel only loads the definitions. A mod must then spawn them through the [API](/mods/personnel/api/).

## Next

- [Pack format](/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/)
- [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/)
- [Multiplayer and saves](/mods/personnel/guides/multiplayer-and-saves/)
- [Troubleshooting](/mods/personnel/guides/troubleshooting/)
- [API reference](/mods/personnel/api/)

pages.title: Keep NPCs working in multiplayer and saves
pages.description: Make Personnel NPCs and custom layers stay in sync across co-op players and across save and load.
pages.markdown:
Follow these rules so Personnel NPCs spawn, sync and save correctly.

**You need:** an NPC pack. See [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/).

## Steps

1. Install the same packs on every player's machine. This is the same rule as for mods.
2. Spawn NPCs on the host. The host spawns the NPC as a FishNet network object. Clients receive it like any S1API NPC.
3. Keep ids stable. S1API saves NPCs through the game save system, and the definition id is the identity. Never change an id after release. See [Pack format](/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/#ids-and-saves).
4. Use custom PNG layers only with the pack on every client. The game syncs layers as resource-path strings, not texture bytes. Each client registers the texture from its own copy of the pack.

## Check it works

- A player without the pack sees the NPC without the custom art. No desync and no crash.
- After save and load, Personnel registers the texture again from the pack at startup.
- If you remove the pack, the layer disappears from the look without an error.

## Appearance-only mods

`BuildAvatarSettings` and `ApplyAppearance` write plain vanilla `AvatarSettings` onto an avatar. Your mod's own system decides whether that look syncs or saves. Personnel adds no networking.

## Next

- [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/)
- [Troubleshooting](/mods/personnel/guides/troubleshooting/)
- [API reference](/mods/personnel/api/)

pages.title: Pack format reference
pages.description: Look up every manifest.json field of a Personnel NPC pack, from appearance to schedule and economy roles.
pages.markdown:
Look up the `manifest.json` fields of an NPC pack. A pack is this folder:

```
Schedule I/UserData/Personnel/Packs/<PackName>/
├── manifest.json
└── *.png              (optional custom layers, referenced by the manifest)
```

Needs Personnel 2.0+ for `autoRegister`, `spawn`, `schedule` and economy roles. Needs Personnel 2.3+ (`schemaVersion` 3) for `supplier`, `portrait` and `lines`.

## manifest.json

```json
{
  "name": "My Pack",
  "author": "you",
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "autoRegister": true,
  "npcs": [
    {
      "id": "mypack_pale",
      "name": "Pale",
      "appearance": {
        "gender": 0.5,
        "height": 1.0,
        "weight": 0.4,
        "skinColor": "#8899AA",
        "hairPath": "Avatar/Hair/Spiky/Spiky",
        "hairColor": "#101014",
        "leftEye":  { "top": 0.5, "bottom": 0.5 },
        "rightEye": { "top": 0.5, "bottom": 0.5 },
        "eyeBallTint": "#FFFFFF",
        "faceLayers": [ { "file": "grin.png", "tint": "#FFFFFF" } ],
        "bodyLayers": [ { "path": "Avatar/Layers/Top/T-Shirt", "tint": "#334455" } ],
        "accessories": [ { "path": "Avatar/Accessories/Feet/Sneakers/Sneakers", "color": "#FFFFFF" } ]
      },
      "behavior": { "aggression": 0.2, "maxHealth": 100, "scale": 1.0 },
      "spawn": {
        "x": -64.25, "y": 1.07, "z": 84.49,
        "rotationY": 325.0,
        "region": "Northtown",
        "physical": true
      },
      "contact": { "visible": true, "mapMarker": true },
      "relationships": {
        "delta": 1.5,
        "unlockType": "Recommendation",
        "connections": [ "mypack_other_npc", "jessi_waters" ]
      },
      "customer": {
        "spending": { "min": 300, "max": 900 },
        "ordersPerWeek": { "min": 1, "max": 3 },
        "preferredOrderDay": "Friday",
        "orderTime": "19:30",
        "standards": "Moderate",
        "allowDirectApproach": true,
        "guaranteeFirstSample": false,
        "mutualRelationRequirement": { "min": 1.0, "max": 4.0 },
        "callPoliceChance": 0.05,
        "dependence": { "base": 0.2, "multiplier": 1.0 },
        "affinities": { "marijuana": 0.6, "cocaine": -0.3 },
        "preferredProperties": [ "energizing", "calming" ]
      },
      "inventory": { "cash": { "min": 20, "max": 120 }, "items": [ "baggie" ], "clearEachNight": true },
      "schedule": [
        { "type": "stayInBuilding", "time": "09:00", "duration": 240, "building": "Motel Office" },
        { "type": "walkTo", "time": "14:00", "position": [-64.25, 1.07, 84.49] }
      ],
      "extensions": { }
    }
  ]
}
```

Every field is optional. A minimal NPC only needs a `name`. Colours are `#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA` hex strings. Personnel logs a warning for an unknown value and skips it. A broken field never removes the whole NPC.

## Ids and saves

- Personnel uses an authored `id` as given, normalized to lowercase `a-z0-9_`.
- Without `id`, Personnel derives `normalize(packId or folder name)_normalize(npc name)`.
- `packId` (top level) fixes the derivation prefix. Renaming the pack folder then keeps the ids.
- Ids must be unique inside a pack. The startup log prints the ids of each pack.
- The id is the save identity. Never change it after you ship the pack.
- To rename, set `saveId` to the OLD id. Existing saves then keep matching.

## Auto-registration

Set `"autoRegister": true` at top level, or `"auto": true` inside one NPC's `spawn`. Personnel then registers the NPC as a real S1API world NPC. It is networked, saved and follows its schedule.

- Everyone in a co-op session needs the same packs.
- If a mod ships a compiled class for the same NPC id, the compiled one wins. The log says so.
- The setting `EnableAutoRegister` turns auto-registration off globally.

## spawn

| Key | Meaning |
|-----|---------|
| `x`, `y`, `z` | Spawn position. |
| `rotationY` | Spawn yaw in degrees. |
| `region` | `Northtown`, `Westville`, `Downtown`, `Docks`, `Suburbia` or `Uptown`. |
| `physical` | `true`: real world body that moves, collides and runs its schedule. `false`: phone contact only, almost no cost. Default: `true` exactly when the NPC has a `schedule`. |
| `auto` | Overrides the pack's `autoRegister` for this NPC. |

Keep most NPCs of a large pack non-physical. For many physical NPCs, [Siesta](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Siesta) lowers the AI cost.

## schedule

An array of actions. `type` decides the other fields. Times are `"HH:MM"` strings, durations are in-game minutes, positions are `[x, y, z]`.

| type | Fields |
|------|--------|
| `walkTo` | `time`, `position`, `faceDestination`, `within`, `warpIfSkipped` |
| `stayInBuilding` | `time`, `duration`, `building` (name), `doorIndex` |
| `sit` | `time`, `duration`, `seatSet` (name) or `seatSetPath`, `includeInactive`, `warpIfSkipped` |
| `useVendingMachine` | `time`, `machineGuid` (optional, nearest otherwise) |
| `useAtm` | `time`, `atmGuid` (optional) |
| `useSlotMachine` | `time`, `position`, `bet`, `mode` (`single`, `spinCount`, `untilTime`, `untilBroke`, `untilTimeOrBroke`), `spins`, `endTime`, `timeBetweenSpins`. Experimental in multiplayer. |
| `locationDialogue` | `time`, `position`, `greetingOverride`, `choice`, plus the `walkTo` fields |
| `locationAction` | `time`, `position`, `duration`, `action` (`smokeBreak`, `graffiti`, `drinking`, `holdItem`), `equippablePath`, `graffitiRegion` |
| `driveToCarPark` | `time`, `parkingLot` (name), `vehicle` (name) or `createVehicle: { "code": "shitbox", "position": [x,y,z], "rotationY": 0 }` |
| `dealSignal` | No fields. Lets a dealer break its schedule for deals. |

- An unknown building or seat name logs a warning. The NPC skips that step.
- `warpIfSkipped: true` places the NPC at the destination when no player was nearby and the step was skipped. Without it the NPC misses the stop and the log says nothing.
- NPCs move only on the navmesh. An unreachable destination leaves the NPC where it was.
- `y` need not be exact. The game samples the navmesh within about 5 units of the destination.

## Console commands for coordinates

Needs Personnel 2.1+. Enable "Console enabled" in Settings and press the backtick key. Each result goes to your clipboard and to `MelonLoader/Latest.log`.

| Command | Result |
|---------|--------|
| `personnel pos` | `[x, y, z]` for any `position` field |
| `personnel pos 07:30` | A finished `walkTo` action for that time |
| `personnel spawn` | A `spawn` block with `x`, `y`, `z`, `rotationY` and `region` filled in |
| `personnel route 07:30` | Appends a `walkTo` step to `UserData/Personnel/route.json` |
| `personnel route show` | Prints the collected steps, ready to paste into `"schedule": [ ... ]` |
| `personnel route clear` | Starts a new route |
| `personnel npcs [filter]` | Loaded definitions, and where the physical ones are now |

Vanilla `teleport <property|npc id>` moves you fast, for example `teleport rv` or `teleport jessi_waters`.

Without Personnel 2.1: run `save` in the console, then read `Position` from `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\TVGS\Schedule I\Saves\<SteamID>\SaveGame_1\Players\Player_0\Player.json`.

## Roles: customer, dealer and supplier

A `customer`, `dealer` or `supplier` block gives the NPC that economy role. If more than one exists, `dealer` wins, then `supplier`, then `customer`. Personnel applies only the fields you set. The rest keep the game defaults.

- `customer`: `spending`, `ordersPerWeek`, `preferredOrderDay` (`Monday` to `Sunday`), `orderTime`, `standards` (`VeryLow`, `Low`, `Moderate`, `High`, `VeryHigh`), `allowDirectApproach`, `guaranteeFirstSample`, `mutualRelationRequirement`, `callPoliceChance`, `dependence`, `affinities`, `preferredProperties`.
- `affinities` maps a drug type to a value from -1 to 1. Types: `marijuana`, `methamphetamine`, `cocaine`, `mdma`, `shrooms`, `heroin`.
- `preferredProperties` takes property ids such as `energizing`.
- `dealer`: `type` (`player` or `cartel`), `cut`, `signingFee`, `home` (building name), `completedDealsVariable`, `allowInsufficientQuality`, `allowExcessQuality`.
- `supplier`: `items` (item ids such as `ogkushseed` or `cocaleaf`), `minOrderLimit`, `maxOrderLimit`, `recommendMessage` (text of the customer who recommends the supplier), `unlockHint` (text on the locked contact), `stashDeadDrop` (GUID of a vanilla dead drop for the cash stash; empty puts a stash next to the spawn).

A supplier works like the vanilla ones: the player orders by phone, the goods wait at a dead drop, and the debt is paid into the stash. The price of an item is its game price. The debt limit grows from `minOrderLimit` to `maxOrderLimit` with the relationship. A supplier always stands in the world, so `spawn.physical: false` is ignored.

```json
"supplier": {
  "items": ["ogkushseed", "sourdieselseed"],
  "minOrderLimit": 50,
  "maxOrderLimit": 500,
  "recommendMessage": "Talk to Sully, he sells seeds.",
  "unlockHint": "A customer can recommend him."
}
```

## portrait

`"portrait": "portrait.png"` sets the picture of the phone contact. Use a square PNG in the pack folder. Without it the game takes a picture of the NPC.

## lines

Own texts of the NPC. Every list holds variants; the game picks one at random. A text you leave out keeps the vanilla text of the NPC's role.

```json
"lines": {
  "greeting": ["Sully's open for business.", "You again? Good."],
  "phone": {
    "deaddrop_ready": ["Sully here. Your stuff waits at <LOCATION>."],
    "deaddrop_requested": [["Got it.", "Give me <TIME>."]]
  },
  "reactions": { "annoyed": ["Hey, watch it."] }
}
```

- `greeting`: what the NPC says when you talk to it, at any time of day.
- `phone`: texts by key. A variant is one message, or a list of messages sent in a row.
- `reactions`: short world reactions by key: `annoyed`, `hurt`, `panic_start`, `noticed_pickpocket`.

Phone keys and their placeholders:

| Role | Keys |
|------|------|
| Customer | `contract_request`, `contract_accepted`, `contract_rejected`, `offer_expired`, `counteroffer_accepted`, `counteroffer_rejected` (`<PRODUCT>`, `<PRICE>`, `<QUALITY>`, `<LOCATION>`, `<WINDOW_START>`, `<WINDOW_END>`); `awaiting_deal`, `late_deal`, `deal_completed`, `customer_rejected_deal`, `offer_reject`, `post_deal_recommend` (`<NAME>`), `sample_sufficient`, `sample_insufficient` |
| Dealer | `dealer_rob_defended`, `dealer_rob_partially_defended`, `dealer_rob_loss`, `inventory_depleted` |
| Supplier | `deaddrop_requested` (`<TIME>`), `deaddrop_ready` (`<LOCATION>`), `supplier_request_repayment` (`<DEBT>`), `supplier_unlocked`, `supplier_meet_confirm` (`<LOCATION>`) |

Any other vanilla key goes to the generic module. `"Module/key"` (for example `"Generic/first_contract_request"`) picks the module by name.

## contact and relationships

- `contact.mapMarker: false` removes the phone-map marker.
- `contact.visible: false` skips the contact unlock, so the NPC shows as "???". Experimental.
- `relationships.delta` is 0 to 5.
- `relationships.unlocked` is a boolean.
- `relationships.unlockType` is `Recommendation` or `DirectApproach`.
- `relationships.connections` lists NPC ids. Use pack-prefixed ids for pack NPCs and plain ids such as `jessi_waters` for vanilla NPCs.

## Layers

Each entry in `faceLayers`, `bodyLayers` and `accessories` uses one source:

| Key | Meaning |
|-----|---------|
| `path` | A Resources path of an in-game layer or accessory. Personify stores these. |
| `file` | A PNG in the pack folder. Personnel registers it as a custom layer at load. See [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/). |
| `tint` (alias `color`) | Hex tint. Default white. |

A `file` in `faceLayers` registers on the face mesh. A `file` in `bodyLayers` registers on the body mesh. Accessories take only `path`. Custom accessory meshes are not supported.

## extensions

Free-form blocks keyed by consumer name, for example `"backrooms": { ... }`. Personnel passes them through untouched. Each consumer reads its own block.

## Publish a pack

1. Export the pack from [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify). It wraps the pack for Thunderstore with `manifest.json`, README and LICENSE, and your pack under `Personnel/Packs/<name>/`.
2. Add a 256x256 `icon.png`.
3. List `DooDesch-Personnel` as a dependency and upload.

pages.title: Troubleshoot Personnel
pages.description: Find the cause and fix for a Personnel pack that does not load, spawn or render.
pages.markdown:
Find your symptom below. Check `MelonLoader/Latest.log` first.

## My pack does not load

Every pack logs one line. A broken pack logs a warning with the file name:

- `manifest has no 'npcs' array`: the JSON root must contain `"npcs": [ ... ]`.
- `failed to read manifest.json`: the JSON is invalid. A trailing comma is the usual cause.
- `an NPC entry has no 'name'`: give every NPC a `name`.

The manifest must be at `UserData/Personnel/Packs/<YourPack>/manifest.json`. Use one folder per pack.

## The log lists my NPCs, but nothing appears in the world

Without `autoRegister`, Personnel only loads definitions. Set `"autoRegister": true`, or let a mod that uses the [API](/mods/personnel/api/) spawn the ids. An NPC with `"physical": false` appears only as a phone contact.

## An NPC does not walk its schedule

- A step with an invalid `time`, `position` or `type` logs a warning and is skipped.
- An unknown building or seat name logs a warning and the NPC skips that step.
- An unreachable destination leaves the NPC where it stood. Pick a point on the navmesh.
- A step skipped because no player was nearby needs `warpIfSkipped: true`.

## My mod's spawn fails or uses defaults

- `no definition '<id>' found`: the pack is not installed, or the id is wrong. Check the startup log for the exact ids. Without an authored `id`, the id is `packname_npcname`, lowercase.
- Make `DefId` a compile-time constant. Personnel reads it from an uninitialized instance, so a field set in your constructor returns null.
- Spawn after a save is loaded, on the host.

## A custom PNG lands on the wrong limb or shows as a blob

The PNG is a full UV-space texture. Align it to the target UV. See [Custom PNG layers](/mods/personnel/guides/custom-png-layers/). Also check the list: `faceLayers` files go to the face mesh, `bodyLayers` files to the body mesh.

## Another player does not see the custom art

That player needs Personnel and the same pack. See [Multiplayer and saves](/mods/personnel/guides/multiplayer-and-saves/).

## The example pack does not appear

Restart the game after you set `LoadExamplePack`. Personnel never overwrites a `Packs/Examples` manifest you edited. Delete the folder to get a fresh copy.

## Still stuck

Send `MelonLoader/Latest.log` and the pack's `manifest.json` to support.

pages.title: Personnel
pages.description: The NPC framework for Schedule I - NPC packs as plain folders, spawned by mods as real S1API NPCs.
pages.markdown:
| | |
|---|---|
| Latest release | `2.4.5` |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personnel) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Personnel/) |
| Requires | MelonLoader 0.7.3, S1API Forked 3.2.1 |
| Start here | [Make an NPC pack](/mods/personnel/guides/getting-started/) |
| API | [Reference](/mods/personnel/api/) |
| Help | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/personnel) |

> The NPC framework for Schedule I. Personnel lets anyone ship custom NPCs as simple pack folders -
> designed in [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify) or written by hand -
> and lets mods spawn them as real, first-class S1API NPCs: networked, saved, and walking the world
> as if the mod author had built them in code. Built on [S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API).



![A pack NPC next to the car he drove across town](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personnel/main/docs/img/header.jpg)

Personnel is primarily a **library / dependency**. On its own it adds no NPCs - it's the thing NPC
packs and NPC-spawning mods depend on. Install it alongside an NPC pack and the NPCs appear:
since 2.0 a pack can opt into **auto-registration** and needs no mod code at all.

## Documentation

  format and id rules, the API (spawning real S1API NPCs), custom PNG layer authoring, multiplayer,
  troubleshooting.
- 🧩 **[Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify)** - the in-game editor that
  designs and exports these packs.

## Features

- **NPC mods without code.** A pack manifest can carry the whole NPC: spawn point and region, a
  daily schedule (walk routes, buildings, seats, vending machines, slot machines, dialogue spots,
  car trips), customer, dealer or supplier economy, inventory, relationships, a contact picture and
  the NPC's own greetings, phone texts and reactions. Flip
  `"autoRegister": true` and Personnel spawns them as real world NPCs that run their day on their
  own.
- **Real S1API NPCs, not props.** Prefab, networking, save/load and mugshot are handled by S1API -
  the same machinery hand-coded NPC mods use.
- **Deep appearance.** The full avatar-settings surface: body, skin, hair, face, eyes, eyebrows,
  clothing layers, accessories, plus **custom PNG layers** (e.g. tattoos) loaded from the pack folder.
- **Physical or contact-only.** Most roster NPCs can stay phone contacts (near-zero cost); only the
  ones that should walk the world are physical. Big packs stay fast, also on Steam Deck.
- **NPC packs are plain folders** - a `manifest.json` plus optional PNGs under
  `UserData/Personnel/Packs/<PackName>/`. Design them live in-game with
  [Personify](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personify).
- **Coordinates from the console.** The game shows none, so `personnel pos 07:30` gives you a
  finished `walkTo` action for the spot you are standing on, `personnel spawn` a full spawn block,
  and `personnel route` collects a whole day's route. Everything lands on your clipboard.
- **Stable, save-safe ids** with rename escape hatches (`packId`, `saveId`).
- **Bundled example pack** (off by default) drops a working manifest template to copy.

## Screenshots

![A pack NPC driving his own car through town](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personnel/main/docs/img/driving.jpg)

![The same drive at night](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Personnel/main/docs/img/night-drive.jpg)

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


| Component | Version / Source |
|-----------|------------------|
| Schedule I | IL2CPP (current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+` |
| S1API | [ifBars/S1API_Forked](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ifBars/S1API_Forked/) |


</details>

<details><summary>Installation</summary>


### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager
Install with r2modman / Gale from the Schedule I community; the dependencies (MelonLoader, S1API) are
pulled in automatically. Then install any NPC pack or NPC mod that lists Personnel as a dependency.

### Manual
1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **S1API** (its DLLs go in `Mods/` and `Plugins/` per its own instructions).
3. Drop **`Personnel.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.
4. Add NPC packs (see below), or enable the bundled example pack (see Configuration).


</details>

## For players: using NPC packs

An NPC pack is just a folder under:

```
<Schedule I>/UserData/Personnel/Packs/<PackName>/
```

containing a `manifest.json` and any PNGs it references. On startup Personnel logs each loaded pack
with the NPC ids it provides. Packs with `autoRegister` bring their NPCs into the world by
themselves; older appearance-only packs are used by whatever consumer mod spawns them. In co-op,
everyone needs the same packs installed - the same rule as for mods.

## For pack authors: the pack format

The comfortable way is the in-game editor **Personify** (a Side Hustle gamemode): design NPCs live on
the menu character, then hit Export - it writes a ready-to-publish pack. By hand, create
`UserData/Personnel/Packs/<YourPack>/manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "My Pack",
  "author": "you",
  "schemaVersion": 3,
  "autoRegister": true,
  "npcs": [
    {
      "name": "Pale",
      "appearance": {
        "gender": 0.5, "height": 1.0, "weight": 0.4,
        "skinColor": "#8899AA", "hairPath": "", "hairColor": "#101014",
        "faceLayers": [ { "file": "grin.png", "tint": "#FFFFFF" } ]
      },
      "spawn": { "x": -64.25, "y": 1.07, "z": 84.49, "region": "Northtown", "physical": true },
      "schedule": [
        { "type": "stayInBuilding", "time": "09:00", "duration": 240, "building": "Motel Office" },
        { "type": "walkTo", "time": "14:00", "position": [-64.25, 1.07, 84.49] }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- An authored `id` is respected (normalized); without one it is derived as `<packname>_<npcname>`.
  Ids are the save identity - never change them once a pack shipped (use `saveId` when renaming).
- Appearance mirrors the S1API avatar-settings surface; every field is optional and defaults to the
  game's baseline. Layers take either a `path` (existing game layer) or a `file` (pack-relative PNG).
- On top of `appearance` there are `spawn`, `schedule`, `customer`, `dealer`, `supplier`, `inventory`,
  `relationships` and `contact` blocks, a `portrait` (phone contact picture) and own `lines` - the
  [Pack Format documentation page](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/personnel/guides/pack-format/)
  documents every field.
- Enable the example pack (Configuration below) for a complete, working template.

## For mod developers: spawning the NPCs

Reference `Personnel.dll` (add `[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Personnel")]`) and declare one
tiny subclass per NPC you want - then spawn it the normal S1API way:

```csharp
public sealed class PaleNpc : Personnel.PersonnelNpc
{
    protected override string DefId => "examples_pale";   // id from an installed pack
}

// wherever you populate the world:
var npc = new PaleNpc();          // S1API builds the prefab, networks and saves it
npc.Position = spawnPoint;        // then use S1API as usual: schedules, dialogue, ...
```

`DefId` must return a constant (S1API builds prefabs from uninitialized instances). Lower-level
entry points on `Personnel.API`: `All` / `TryGet(id, out def)` to enumerate definitions,
`BuildAvatarSettings(def)` / `ApplyAppearance(avatar, def)` to realise just the look on any avatar,
and `ConfigureFromDef(builder, def)` if you keep your own `NPC` subclass. A complete reference
consumer lives in the repo as `PersonOfInterest`.

## Configuration

Settings live in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg`
under `Personnel_01_Main`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `LoadExamplePack` | `false` | When on, drops a small example pack into `UserData/Personnel/Packs/Examples` on startup (if not already there) - ready-made NPCs plus a manifest template to copy. Requires a game restart. An unedited older example pack is updated; an edited one is never touched. |
| `EnableAutoRegister` | `true` | Kill switch for pack auto-registration. When off, packs with `autoRegister` load as data only and nothing spawns. Requires a game restart. |

## How it works

Packs are parsed into plain definitions at startup (no Unity objects). When a consumer first uses a
definition, Personnel maps it onto S1API's avatar-settings builder; custom PNG layers are loaded into
textures, put on a clone of a built-in tattoo of the same kind, and registered in the game's avatar
object library under the layer path - so the game's own pipeline renders, saves and networks them like
built-in layers.
Full NPCs ride entirely on S1API's prefab/networking machinery via `PersonnelNpc`.

<details><summary>Compatibility</summary>


- IL2CPP build only (current Steam public branch).
- **Multiplayer:** NPCs spawned via S1API follow S1API's networking. Custom PNG layers are referenced
  by resource-path string - clients need Personnel and the same pack to render them; others simply
  don't show that layer (no desync, no crash).


</details>

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


- **DooDesch** - mod author.
- **[ifBars/S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API)** - the modding API this is built on.


</details>

pages.title: Polyfill changelog
pages.description: Every released version of Polyfill and what changed in it.
pages.markdown:
All notable changes to this project are documented here.

## [0.13.30] - 2026-10-28

### Added
- Type `polyfillcheck` in the console to see which of your mods are outdated or throw errors. The answer opens on
  polyfill.doomods.com as a link you can share.
- No game at hand: drop `MelonLoader/Latest.log` on [polyfill.doomods.com/check](https://polyfill.doomods.com/check).

## [0.13.29] - 2026-10-24

### Fixed
- Police Response Overhaul with S1API: the game no longer closes without an error after a sale.

## [0.13.28] - 2026-10-24

### Fixed
- DaffysHills: people walk the road up to Clifftop instead of freezing on it and jumping across.
- DaffysHills: the cabin no longer logs an error on every load.

## [0.13.27] - 2026-10-24

### Fixed
- Cartel Enforcer, NACops, DaffysHills, Smugglers Flight and Delivery Spots Revived load and run on 0.4.7 again.
- Cartel Enforcer and NACops: NPCs take the new speed when the mod changes it a second time.
- NACops and Smugglers Flight: characters the mod copies no longer log an error for every piece of clothing.

### For mod authors
- `polyfill-check` reports a constructor call whose parameters fit none of the game's constructors, such as
  Over The Counter's three-argument `SpeedControl`.

## [0.13.26] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed
- Over The Counter: accepting a desperation deal works again, and the customer runs to the meetup.
- Over The Counter: trees next to the dispensaries, the Westville shack and the warehouse no longer poke
  through the walls.
- A post office lost from a save comes back with its laundering station and storage rack, not owned.

## [0.13.25] - 2026-10-21

### Fixed
- Over The Counter: suppliers who wait in the warehouse stay at the meetup spot. They walked back to the
  warehouse right after the meetup started.
- Cash Stack Limit: moving cash no longer drops the frame rate for a second and a half.

## [0.13.24] - 2026-10-21

### Fixed
- Over The Counter: drifters and managers get their contact pictures again.
- Chemical Plant: no more error from its property on every load.

## [0.13.23] - 2026-10-21

### Fixed
- Over The Counter and Chemical Plant together no longer crash the game with a stack overflow.
- Over The Counter: drifters spawn on 0.4.7 again. Every spawn failed with a NullReferenceException at
  NPC.get_ID before.
- Over The Counter: no more trees standing inside the dispensary, the Westville shack and the warehouse.
- Contact pictures of characters added by mods, such as Static, Vic and Bella, show the face up close like the
  game's own. The face filled only half the picture before.
- Building mods that clear the ground around their buildings leave game businesses such as the post office
  standing.

## [0.13.22] - 2026-10-20

### Fixed
- Casino Direct Deposit: Philip offers "Quick question about payouts." again. It failed with "Method not found:
  set_GenericDialogue" before.
- Over The Counter: Static is set up on 0.4.7 again and reacts after taking cocaine. It failed with "Method not
  found: get_onConsumeDone" before.
- Rain, wet surfaces and wind keep running when a mod removes part of a building. The log filled with a
  NullReferenceException every frame before.

## [0.13.21] - 2026-10-20

### Fixed
- Deals Gone Wrong customers turn on you after a deal on 0.4.7 again. It failed with "Method not found:
  set_Aggression" before.
- Section 97: the deal completion popup shows after every sale again, and robberies still hide its title and payment.
- Multiplayer Tracker Fix: deals you tracked stay on the HUD and compass after loading a save.
- Visual Assets Overhaul keeps replacing icons after you load a save from the menu. They stopped for the rest of
  the session before.
- Visual Assets Overhaul no longer shows as needing a fix on the compatibility list.

## [0.13.20] - 2026-10-19

### Fixed
- DMT Mod mixes show DMT's own product icons on 0.4.7 again instead of the game's icon.
- Total Daily Profit no longer shows as blocked on the compatibility list.

## [0.13.19] - 2026-10-18

### Fixed
- Section 97 robberies, muggings and smash-and-grabs work on 0.4.7 again. Aiming at a cashier failed with
  "Method not found: SetPanicked" before.

## [0.13.18] - 2026-10-18

### Fixed
- Mods that change NPC walk or run speed no longer fail on 0.4.7, e.g. Better Dealers, HardcorePolice, DealerRoutes.
- Sleep mods open the bed menu on 0.4.7 again: MoreRealisticSleeping, Sleep Mod, SidewalkEconomy.
- Mods built on S1API 1.6.2 can make NPCs invincible on 0.4.7 again.

## [0.13.17] - 2026-10-17

### Fixed
- SimpleCall 1.2.1 can call dealers on 0.4.7 again. Every call failed with an error before.

## [0.13.16] - 2026-10-17

### Fixed
- Curfew+ 1.4.0 works on 0.4.7 again, and its night officers patrol instead of standing still.
- Curfew+'s night officers go off duty in the morning without a log warning for each one.

## [0.13.15] - 2026-10-17

### Changed
- The compatibility index now spots mods that catch their own errors and only print a warning, so a mod that
  quietly stopped working no longer shows as clean.

## [0.13.14] - 2026-10-17

### Fixed
- AutoRestock works again: on 0.4.7 it stopped while a save loaded and never restocked anything.

## [0.13.13] - 2026-10-16

### Fixed
- Ultimate Mod Menu 3.0 no longer crashes the game while a save loads.
- Mods no longer fail with "Ambiguous match" on game functions Polyfill gave their old form back.

## [0.13.12] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- With S1API 3.2.1, the game no longer crashes on the first save you load each session. Only the default
  game branch was affected, not Mono.

## [0.13.11] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- ModsApp and other mods built for both game branches no longer show "parts missing" over code they only
  run on Mono.

## [0.13.10] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- On 0.4.7, AutomatedTasks 1.3.0 finishes the cauldron again instead of stopping after the gasoline.
- AutomatedTasks pours soil, sows, waters, fertilizes and harvests your pots again. On 0.4.7 none of it started.

## [0.13.9] - 2026-10-14

### Fixed
- On 0.4.7, Time Never Stops 1.5.0 works again: time runs past 4 AM, and the 6:59 sleep ends the day and
  saves without counting an extra day.
  - Its silent sleep is not back yet, so the screen goes black for a few seconds during that sleep.

## [0.13.8] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed
- On 0.4.7, Mrs. Ming's Authentic Pets 2.0.2 stops dragging a loaded save down to 1-2 fps, and the dog
  toys are back on the shop's shelves.

## [0.13.7] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed
- Tweakables, Media Player and Wages Manager stop reading as blocked once Polyfill has repaired their
  phone app. The report said blocked while the app filled the screen.

### Changed
- `polyfillshow <mod>` lists what is still open first and says `repaired:` under what Polyfill put back.
  It prints 20 entries, and the one that decided a mod's state could be cut off.

## [0.13.6] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed
- On 0.4.7, the Tweakables 0.6.0 phone app fills the screen again, with the categories on the left and
  the settings next to them.
- On 0.4.7, NPCInteract360 1.1.1 lets you talk to an NPC from any side again.
- On 0.4.7, Ndrangheta Mafia 1.0.7 and TheMob Connector 1.0.7 get back the game functions they call, and
  the mod's goons wear their outfits again. Needs S1API 3.2.1 or newer.

## [0.13.5] - 2026-10-13

### Fixed
- On 0.4.7, InstantDelivery 1.6.0 finds Albert, Shirley and Salvador again, so its instant deliveries
  and no debt switches work for the three of them.

## [0.13.4] - 2026-10-12

### Fixed
- On 0.4.7, Tweakables 0.6.0 gets its teleport rotation and product icons back, and its "no trash" switch
  stops single trash items again, not only bags.
- On 0.4.7, SkillTree 3.4.0 can change the time when you sleep again. Without that, beds broke.
- AutomatedTasksMod 1.3.0 reacts to the chemistry station's Begin button again.

### Added
- On 0.4.7, TrashCollector 0.22.2 and SkillTree get back six trash functions the update removed.
- Chemical Plant 1.4.0 gets back four game functions it needs on 0.4.7 for its property, parking, trash
  and workers.
- Older mods that set the time of day, hide your own character or use an NPC's default dialogue find
  those game functions on 0.4.7 again.

## [0.13.3] - 2026-10-12

### Fixed
- On 0.4.7, ProduceMore 1.2.0's employees can walk to their stations and finish plant work again.

## [0.13.2] - 2026-10-12

### Fixed
- ProduceMore 1.2.0 shows drying rack progress and remaining time correctly again, including when you change its drying speed.

## [0.13.1] - 2026-10-05

### Fixed
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods built on S1API that add their own products or packaging show the right look
  and icon for them again.
- With Over The Counter installed, Polyfill no longer writes a "Could not find property" warning into
  the log at startup.

## [0.13.0] - 2026-10-01

### Fixed
- Production Expansion Reborn no longer crashes the game when you assign a customer to a dealer.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, the game no longer closes without an error at startup when Expanded Storage is
  installed.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, Production Expansion Reborn's cleaner stations throw their trash bags again
  instead of dropping them where they are made.

### Added
- On the 0.4.7 beta, RV Repair Van's questline starts again.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, K9 Patrol's dogs, Yoink, SimpleCall, CityCats and The Big Pimpin's messages work
  again.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, Lithium, Drones and BusinessTracker see a finished deal again, and Cartel
  Influence Enhancements' handover change runs again.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, All Your Clients Will Order, BFG Better Supplier and BFG Smart Deal Location read
  the open deal and supplier messages again.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, NetEye cameras, Personnel's custom NPCs and Police Response Overhaul load without
  errors about game functions the update removed.

## [0.12.11] - 2026-09-23

### Fixed
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that react to a finished deal see it again, like Over The Counter's handover.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that open a phone chat with a character work again, like Over The Counter's drifters.

## [0.12.10] - 2026-09-23

### Fixed
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that give characters their own look (custom NPCs, look editors) can dress them again.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods built on S1API that read the clock or react to sleeping work again.
- Over The Counter no longer fills the log with an error every frame on the 0.4.7 beta.

## [0.12.9] - 2026-09-23

### Fixed
- On the 0.4.7 beta, OG Backpack keeps what you put in it: the backpack saves again and is back after loading.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that add to the deal screen show up there again, like Over The Counter's fill button.

## [0.12.8] - 2026-09-23

### Added
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that finish a deal for you (drones, auto-delivery) can complete it again.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that add their own dialogue load again.

## [0.12.7] - 2026-09-23

### Added
- Ready for the Schedule I 0.4.7 beta: Polyfill knows what that update renamed, so more of your old
  mods load there.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that change how fast NPCs walk work again.
- On the 0.4.7 beta, mods that move an NPC to a spot work again, and the NPC keeps facing the way it faced.

### Fixed
- Polyfill no longer lists itself as broken on the 0.4.7 beta.

## [0.12.6] - 2026-09-12

### For mod authors
- An error on your mod's page now carries the path through your own code that led to it, up to
  five frames, not just the one where it failed.

## [0.12.5] - 2026-09-12

### For mod authors
- An error on your mod's page now carries two frames: your own method, and the frame that threw.
- Errors are no longer misattributed. Every mod claimed the `System` namespace, so any frame from
  inside .NET was booked against whichever mod was listed first.

## [0.12.4] - 2026-09-12

### Fixed
- A repair that takes the game down is remembered and skipped on the next start, so one bad
  combination cannot stop you playing. The log names it.

## [0.12.3] - 2026-09-08

### Fixed
- Over The Counter's drifters answer you again. The message has its accept and decline buttons,
  and the drifter has the deal instead of a stranger's greeting.
- The game no longer dies when a drifter deal is paid out.

### Added
- The compatibility index now says why a missing name is missing, not only that it is.

## [0.12.2] - 2026-09-07

### Added
- The mod page on polyfill.doomods.com now says why Polyfill refused a repair, instead of only
  that it did.

### Fixed
- Mules and Lithium stop being listed as broken. What they asked the game for was there all
  along, in a form Polyfill did not recognise.
- Text Your Friends draws its message bubbles and its player conversations again.

## [0.12.1] - 2026-09-07

### Fixed
- Mods that lay out the handover screen work again. The game renamed the two slot lists they fill.
- Mods that make an NPC invincible work again. The game moved that flag onto the NPC's own data.

## [0.12.0] - 2026-09-06

### Fixed
- Four supplier mods load again: Auto Pay Suppliers, BFG Better Supplier, Legal Produce and SkillTree.
  They read a supplier's order limit, which the game moved onto the NPC's own data.

## [0.11.18] - 2026-09-06

### Fixed
- Storage containers show the Delivery Manifest again, with its have and needed list and the Smart Fill
  button.
- A hired manager is called by their own name. They were taking the name of another character.

## [0.11.17] - 2026-09-06

### Fixed
- Drifters and shop customers keep their own name. They were taking the name of the character they were
  built from, so every one of them was somebody else.

## [0.11.16] - 2026-09-04

### Fixed
- Smart Employees syncs employee changes between players again. The game moved where lobby chat arrives,
  so the mod switched its multiplayer sync off.

## [0.11.15] - 2026-09-04

### Fixed
- The game starts again with Deep Pockets and Mules installed together. It closed before the main menu
  with nothing in the log, and more mods made it more likely.

## [0.11.14] - 2026-09-04

### Fixed
- Rains Car Dealership opens its dealer screen. Interacting with a car did nothing at all, and the
  interaction broke off there.
- Mods that free or lock your mouse work again. The game moved both away from the camera, so a mod
  asking for either one got nothing.
- Dealer mods set the cut and the signing fee again, and employee mods set an NPC's health and walking
  speed.
- Mods that hide an NPC's chat work again.
- Your character's appearance is readable again, and so is whether a conversation is open.

### Changed
- The listing stops calling a mod fixed when it is not. Anything Polyfill had an idea for counted as
  repaired, so a mod that still crashed could read "Works with Polyfill".
- A gap Polyfill cannot close now says why, instead of naming a lookalike and leaving it at that.

## [0.11.13] - 2026-09-03

### Fixed
- Over The Counter's Smart Fill takes the items off your stack. It put them in the handover and left
  the same stack in your hotbar as well.
- A client's chosen meeting place reaches the host again in HUB - MeetPoints. The host heard nothing,
  so the customer went to the vanilla spot.
- More Realistic Sleeping's app opens instead of waiting for two phone fonts it could never load,
  once every two seconds for the rest of the session.
- Mods that read an NPC's name keep working before the game has given that NPC one.
- Mods can work the roulette table's bet controls, the way they already could at the blackjack table.

### Changed
- Mods that work stop reading as broken. Over The Counter and DealOptimizer said blocked while their
  repairs were already in place.
- The key hints a mod asks for are loaded and cleared again, though the game dropped most of the sets
  they used to name.

## [0.11.12] - 2026-09-03

### Fixed
- The game stays open when you start a counteroffer. Two repairs got in the way of each other, and
  the game closed with no message and no crash report.
- More Realistic Sleeping works again. It makes an effect that the game renamed, and the old name
  could not make one.
- Tweakables waters, pours and sprays. Four of its jobs did not start, because it names a value
  differently from the game.
- Tweakables sets the order days. Its change did not start, and the log showed an error that named
  no mod.
- Price per gram shows the price per gram. The counteroffer screen moved the number into the box
  beside it.

### Changed
- OG Backpack, the employee mods and HUB - Dispensary show the correct state on
  polyfill.doomods.com. A repair that runs after the report was not counted.

## [0.11.11] - 2026-09-01

### Fixed
- Another fix for dedicated servers dying at startup. 0.11.10 guarded the wrong half and a server
  with TrashGrabber PLUS still died; S1API now only looks at mods that could hold its own NPCs.

## [0.11.10] - 2026-09-01

### Fixed
- Seeds and items a mod delivers by dead drop arrive again. With every dead drop in the world full,
  the game broke off instead of answering, and the delivery stopped halfway.
- Dedicated servers start again with S1API installed. The crash left nothing behind but
  `Internal CLR error` and no line saying which mod.
- A dedicated server starts straight away. The question about sharing findings arrived as a dialog
  box nobody was there to answer, and the first three startups each waited a minute for it.
- Sharing turned on by hand on a server now survives a restart. Every startup wrote
  `ShareFindings` back to off.

### Changed
- A dedicated server sends findings and crashes but no longer counts its uptime as playtime. A box
  running overnight with nobody on it says nothing about whether a mod works.
- Repairs that only change what you see - phone app layout, images drawn over the game, tree size -
  are skipped on a dedicated server.

## [0.11.9] - 2026-08-31

### Fixed
- Tweakables' raised deal cap works again. The higher number was worked out and then written nowhere,
  so you kept seeing the old limit with nothing to say why.

### Changed
- When something a mod needs cannot be put back, but Polyfill restores what it was for another way,
  the report says which fix covers it instead of only listing it as missing.

## [0.11.8] - 2026-08-31

### Fixed
- Media Player, Tweakables and Wages Manager fill the phone screen again instead of being squeezed into
  a strip at the top.
- Tweakables works again. Six of its features were not loading at all, the packaging skip and the raised
  deal cap among them.
- Mods that put you into a screen and hand control back afterwards work again.
- Mods that use the packaging station, the ATM or the main menu are no longer called broken when they
  are not.

## [0.11.7] - 2026-08-31

### Fixed
- Media Player's app fills the phone screen again. It had been squeezed into a strip at the top since
  the game rebuilt the screen it borrows.

### Added
- Polyfill now says when a mod borrows a piece of the game's own screens. Those mods can pass every
  check here and still look wrong on your phone.

## [0.11.6] - 2026-08-31

### Fixed
- Mods that open the sleep screen work again. The repair for it shipped in 0.11.3 and never once ran:
  it looked for the wrong thing and gave up without saying so.
- Mods built on the main menu's screens load again, LethalLizard's Mod Manager among them.
- Mods that read or change a dealer's cut work again.
- When Polyfill says a mod is missing something, it now shows enough of the name to tell it apart from
  what the game has. Two names that looked identical in the report were not.

### Added
- polyfill.doomods.com has a "Find this mod" button on every mod, so you can go and get the thing you
  just read about.

## [0.11.5] - 2026-08-30

### Fixed
- Polyfill stops listing a mod as broken when the game still has everything it asked for. It counted
  how many arguments a mod named instead of checking which ones.
- Mods that change the object and route pickers on the management clipboard work again. They loaded
  without complaining and then did nothing.
- Mods that open a storage screen from a container work again. Two of the three ways to open one were
  repaired and the third was missed.

## [0.11.4] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed
- Another fix for overlay mods: 0.11.3 stopped the crash but drew nothing, so a clock or a crosshair was
  simply missing. The image is on screen now.
- A repair that cannot do the job says so and steps aside, instead of leaving a mod loaded and silent.
  `polyfillfixes` shows it as failed and the log gives the reason.

## [0.11.3] - 2026-08-29

### Fixed
- Overlay mods draw again. ClockOverlay and EZCrosshair threw an error every frame instead of drawing,
  which filled the log and could take the game down with it.
- Mods that open or close the sleep screen work again. 0.4.6 replaced the call they use, and Polyfill
  now opens and closes it the way the game does.
- Mods that close the pause menu close it. They loaded without complaining and then did nothing.

## [0.11.2] - 2026-08-28

### Changed
- The sharing question now names everything that is sent: mod authors, how long you played, and any
  errors a mod threw. It said "mod names and versions only" and that was less than the truth.
- `polyfillshare on` says the same, and points at `polyfillshare show` so you can read the exact text.

## [0.11.1] - 2026-08-28

### Fixed
- polyfill.doomods.com counted every launch as a separate player. Your PC rolled a new id each time
  the game started, so six sessions looked like six people.

## [0.11.0] - 2026-08-28

### Added
- polyfill.doomods.com now says whether a mod actually works, not just whether it starts. Polyfill
  watches your session for errors and reports what it saw when you leave the game.
- The list shows how long people played before answering, so a mod nobody has really used says so
  instead of looking fine.

### Changed
- Reports go out when you quit, not while the game loads. A mod that starts and then breaks was
  passing the old check.
- Only the error type and the line it came from are sent. Never the error text, which can contain your
  save name or a folder path.

## [0.10.1] - 2026-08-28

### Fixed
- The sharing question stops coming back. It appeared on every launch and no button could stop it -
  the answer was written but never read back.

### Changed
- The compatibility list now says a mod "starts" rather than "works". Polyfill checks what a mod asks
  the game for while it loads, which is not the same as playing it.
- Reports say which Polyfill wrote them, so polyfill.doomods.com can show when a mod was fixed by an
  update rather than by a game change.

## [0.10.0] - 2026-08-28

### Added
- Check whether a mod still works before you install it: polyfill.doomods.com lists what other players
  reported for your game version.
- Polyfill asks once, on your first launch, whether it may send what it found. Say no and nothing ever
  leaves your PC.
  - `polyfillshare show` prints exactly what would be sent, `polyfillshare on` and `off` change your mind.
- Only mod names, versions and what Polyfill repaired are sent. Never your name, your save, your folders,
  or which mods you run together.

### For mod authors
- `polyfill-check YourMod.dll --game 0.4.6f13` lists what a game update broke in your mod, with no game
  and no MelonLoader installed.
  - It agreed with the in-game report on all 44 mods the two were run against.
- Your mod's page on the index names every member the game no longer has, and whether Polyfill bridged
  it, refused it, or found nothing to point at.

## [0.9.26] - 2026-08-26

### Fixed
- Absorbent Soil and NACops are no longer listed as broken. Both work on this version - the report was
  wrong about them, not the mods.

## [0.9.25] - 2026-08-26

### Fixed
- Your Over The Counter manager stops turning into a townsperson - their face, their name, their stock.
  If a manager is missing after you load a save, rejoin and they come back.

## [0.9.24] - 2026-08-26

### Fixed
- The Tweakables app opens on your phone again instead of sitting there dead.
- Suppliers show you their stock at the meetup. They used to just greet you until you shoved them.
- GraphicsMOD's lighting option turns the sun off again.

## [0.9.23] - 2026-08-21

### Fixed
- A patch a mod cannot bind no longer blocks every later patch of that same method. Harmony keeps the
  failed entry, and 0.9.19 left it there.
- Tweakables can raise how often a customer orders again, and GraphicsMOD's lighting option switches the
  sun instead of doing nothing.

## [0.9.22] - 2026-08-21

### Fixed
- Deal Optimizer re-evaluates a counteroffer after you change the quantity. The method kept its name and
  swapped its argument type, which Harmony can neither choose nor bind.
- Tweakables can patch the handover price box and the blackjack bet slider again. Polyfill's stand-ins
  carried the new argument names, and a patch binds by name.

### Added
- The blackjack bet slider, its handler and the bet label are reachable on the screen again, after 0.4.6
  moved them into the panel every casino game shares.

## [0.9.21] - 2026-08-21

### Fixed
- Enhanced PD stops logging an error every second. 0.4.6 moved the player lookups off Player onto
  PlayerManager, and the mod asks the old address once per raid tick.

## [0.9.20] - 2026-08-19

### Fixed
- The GreenTab app comes back after a trip to the main menu instead of failing to register, which took
  the whole app down rather than its icon.
- Unicorn's Custom Seeds can put its seeds in a supplier's shop again. Reading the list was bridged and
  writing it back was not.
- Installing through Vortex puts the plugin in the game's Plugins folder instead of bepinex/plugins.

## [0.9.19] - 2026-08-18

### Fixed
- The Heisenberg mod delivers Heisenberg again instead of a standard chemist: the flag that says an NPC
  has a last name moved in 0.4.6 and nothing had put it back.
- Deal Optimizer works on counteroffers and street deals again, and no longer throws at startup.
- One patch a mod cannot bind no longer costs it every patch after that one - Deal Optimizer lost seven
  working ones to a single dead target.

### Added
- A method that kept its name and now hands back a renamed type is repaired instead of only listed.
- The report names a patched method the game split into two overloads, which Harmony refuses to choose
  between.

## [0.9.18] - 2026-08-17

### Fixed
- Despawning an NPC stops filling your log with errors. The game asks one list of schedule actions
  whether they should start without checking they still exist.

## [0.9.17] - 2026-08-17

### Fixed
- The Over The Counter manager panel goes away when you put the clipboard on another employee, instead
  of staying up and drawing over theirs.

## [0.9.16] - 2026-08-17

### Fixed
- Instant Pack works again. The packaging and mixing screens renamed the property that hands out the
  station they belong to, and mods that ask for the old name got nothing.

## [0.9.15] - 2026-08-16

### Changed
- The log names which character each Over The Counter customer was built from, for the first eight. Ask
  for it if your customers all look alike.

## [0.9.14] - 2026-08-16

### Fixed
- Suppliers open their sales page again and the GreenTab app takes input after you return from the main
  menu. Both died in the same call Polyfill had written wrong.

## [0.9.13] - 2026-08-16

### Fixed
- Over The Counter's manager panel goes away when you put the clipboard down, instead of staying up and
  overlapping the next employee's panel.

## [0.9.12] - 2026-08-15

### Fixed
- You can move again after putting the manager clipboard away. It was hidden without being taken off the
  input stack, so the game still had it open while the screen said otherwise.

## [0.9.11] - 2026-08-15

### Fixed
- Ultimate Mod Menu starts. Its third way of looking a type up killed the game too, and so did the way
  Polyfill answered the first two.

## [0.9.10] - 2026-08-15

### Fixed
- Ultimate Mod Menu gets past its clipboard setup. 0.9.8 covered one of its two type searches, so the
  crash moved from the police patches to the next feature instead of going away.

## [0.9.9] - 2026-08-15

### Fixed
- Over The Counter can dress a drifter again. It writes a field 0.4.6 deleted, and the whole routine
  stopped before its own error handling could run.

## [0.9.8] - 2026-08-15

### Fixed
- Over The Counter's customers stop all being the same person. They were cloned from one prefab; now
  every spawnable civilian gets a turn, and the log names which ones your game has.
- Giving an Over The Counter manager a route works again. The button did nothing because the panel
  named a UI class 0.4.6 removed, which stopped the whole method from running.
- Ultimate Mod Menu no longer kills the game on startup with no message. It searched for game types in a
  way that loads every type there is, which the game does not survive.

### Changed
- `polyfillprobe` now calls static members too, so a repair like `Singleton<T>.Instance` can be
  checked rather than only listed.

## [0.9.7] - 2026-08-15

### Fixed
