pages.description: Every released version of RVRepairVan and what changed in it.
pages.markdown:
All notable changes to RVRepairVan are documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/), and this
project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

## [4.2.0] - 2026-10-28

### Added
- The hazmat suit and respirator in the RV can be taken out or hung back for free in the bodyshop (Interior, "Cook Gear").

### Fixed
- Number key 1 at Marco no longer buys an RV upgrade: his own choices come first again, the RV choices below them.

## [4.1.0] - 2026-10-27

### Added
- The roof hatch opens again when you leave the driver's seat, if it was open before you drove off.
- With the workshop floor you can build on all free floor: where the kitchen and the decor were, around the bed, and on the left side.
- Lowered suspension and nitro flames show on the RV.

### Changed
- Needs Chassis 1.8.0 and Marco's Bodyshop 1.1.0.

### Fixed
- The driver's view sits at eye height, not at chest height.
- In co-op, a passenger standing in the moving RV no longer sways for the others, and their view no longer shakes.

## [4.0.0] - 2026-10-27

### Added
- Marco paints the RV in his metallic, matte and chrome colours, the stripes and accents in a second colour. The paint stays after
  the trip home and a reload.
- The interior is sold part by part at Marco's Bodyshop. Take out only what you need, put it back later for free.
- The workshop floor is sold at the bodyshop too, with no other upgrade needed. It covers every free bit of floor.
- The roof hatch opens and closes with E from inside, and it shuts when you drive off.
- In the bodyshop menu, a part glows red when it comes out and green when it goes back in.

### Changed
- Needs Marco's Bodyshop 1.0.1, Chassis 1.7.1 and Sideload. Old saves with the gutted interior keep every part
  out and unlocked.

### Fixed
- The RV no longer slides sideways when you get out.
- Police no longer walk through the RV's walls. They come in through the door.

## [3.6.4] - 2026-10-26

### Changed
- The RV pulls harder below 10 km/h, so it gets going faster from a standstill.

### Fixed
- The RV gets up steep ramps, like the highway ramp at Hyland Point with Serena Flats, and pulls away on them from a stop. It used to stall and roll back.

## [3.6.3] - 2026-10-24

### Changed
- The RV quest saves into one file, `rv_state.json`, instead of 16. Old saves load as before.

### Fixed
- A damaged RV save file no longer resets the quest and the upgrades on the next save. The damaged file is kept beside it.

## [3.6.2] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed
- The new work floor no longer stays red in build mode when something stood in the RV before you bought it.

## [3.6.1] - 2026-10-22

### Fixed
- Driver and passenger sit on the RV cab chairs with their knees bent. They used to sink into the cushion with their legs
  stretched out.

## [3.6.0] - 2026-10-22

### Added
- You and your passenger sit visibly in the RV cab, and the wheel turns as you steer. `V` switches to first person.
- The driver holds the RV wheel with both hands around the rim, low left and right, and turns with it.

### Changed
- Needs Chassis 1.5.0. Horn on `G` and the indicators come from it.

## [3.5.8] - 2026-10-21

### Fixed
- Loading an older save no longer resets the RV questline progress.
- An arrest no longer leaves the RV stuck in the police impound. It goes back to its spot at the motel.
- Co-op: the station view no longer shakes while someone else drives the RV.
- Co-op: station ingredients stay put at a steady speed and only slide when the RV speeds up, brakes or turns.
- Building in the RV after a drive: no build spots outside the walls, and turned items stand flat on a slope.

## [3.5.7] - 2026-10-16

### Fixed
- Co-op: the RV no longer flies up and flips when a friend takes the wheel.
- Co-op: whoever drove the RV stays visible for the others after getting out.
- Co-op: the stock Veeper no longer flashes up for a moment when someone starts to drive.
- The camera no longer drifts off your body after a ride in the moving RV. A camera that already sits off snaps
  back once you stand on your own.
- The mod does half the work per frame: each of its checks ran twice.

## [3.5.6] - 2026-10-16

### Changed
- The RV steers like a big vehicle: full lock up to 20 km/h for parking, less lock above that, and the wheel turns
  slower.

## [3.5.5] - 2026-10-16

### Added
- Ride along while a friend drives: walk around in the back or take the new passenger seat next to the wheel.
- Stations work on the road. The view moves with the RV, and the bags on a packaging station stay on the table.
- The workshop floor reaches the rear wall, so the space where the bed stood takes racks and machines too.

### Fixed
- The RV no longer tips onto its side on the first drive after loading a save.
- Taking the wheel no longer throws the other player out of the RV.

## [3.5.4] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- Co-op: the second player sees the RV drive and gets "Drive" on its seat. On saves past the intro they saw the stock
  vehicle instead.

## [3.5.3] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- The save intercom and the hazmat suit inside the RV hang flat on the wall. They stood a hand's width off it.

## [3.5.2] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- Co-op: other players see the RV when you drive and park it, not a bare Veeper that glitches out and vanishes
  after you get out.

## [3.5.1] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- Workers you hire after building the crew quarters walk into the RV and work. They used to wait outside with
  nothing to do.
- The hazmat suit in the RV hangs flat on a wire hook like an empty suit, not like someone is standing in it.

## [3.5.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added
- Nods to a certain chemistry teacher's RV: new lines from Marco and Mrs. Ming, and props in and on the RV to find.
- The RV battery can go flat after 3 in-game days unused. Hold a battery at the wheel to swap it; `BatteryBreakdowns`
  turns this off.

### Changed
- The RV's save intercom sits next to the light switch by the door.

## [3.4.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added
- The steering wheel says "Missing engine" until Marco gets the engine running.

### Fixed
- The quest icon no longer turns into a white square after loading a save.
- With Schedule Maintenance installed, the RV door opens again: its Krystal Ship switches off once your RV is repaired.
- Driving the RV: the camera no longer jerks in and out past poles and power lines.
- Workshop floor: equipment placed before the upgrade no longer leaves a second raster that turns free spots red.

## [3.3.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added
- The RV's hazards blink while it stands on its home spot, so you can see where getting out puts it back home.

## [3.2.2] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- Parking the RV back on its spot works facing either way, so building and the crew come back after a drive.

## [3.2.1] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- Seeds no longer fall through pots in the RV while it is parked away from home.

## [3.2.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added
- The RV has a save intercom on the wall behind the door, like every other property.

## [3.1.1] - 2026-10-15

### Fixed
- The RV knocks people over when you drive into them, like any other car.

## [3.1.0] - 2026-10-15

### Added
- Marco sells a fifth build-out, **Get the engine running** ($10,000): drive the RV anywhere. `PriceEngine` sets the price.
- Parked away, the RV keeps its stations and the items you place in it. Crew and deliveries wait until it is back on its spot.
- Headlights (H), brake and reverse lights work while you drive. The light switch inside works wherever the RV stands.
- The RV rolls and steers on its own tyres, and the entry step folds in while you drive.

### Fixed
- A paid repair survives a restart again. On a slow load the RV came back wrecked and Marco asked for the money again.
- The repair sound follows the Master and Sound Effects sliders.
- Small gaps in the RV's walls no longer show the outside.

## [3.0.1] - 2026-10-14

### Changed
- Donna, Mrs. Ming and Marco got new lines. Every reply tells you where to go next, and Marco talks like he does in the game.
- Marco takes Mrs. Ming's name on your first visit. The extra "Fifty grand?" step is gone.
- "Can you go any lower?" is one choice now. Marco sends you for his package first, then takes packaged product from your hand.
- Marco texts you once the RV is repaired and mentions his build-outs.

## [3.0.0] - 2026-10-14

### Added
- Marco sells four build-outs once the RV stands again, each with its own cinematic. They build on each other.
  - **Gut the interior** ($2,500) clears out the bed, bench and cabinets.
  - **Build me a workshop floor** ($7,500) adds 24 tiles to the RV's 32.
  - **Make room for a crew** ($15,000): three employees can work in the RV. Place a locker inside.
  - **I need a loading dock** ($25,000): your supplier delivers to the RV.
- Every price is a setting, as are `CrewSize` and `BuildGridExtraTiles`. Marco's offer updates without a restart.
  `UpgradesEnabled` turns the shop off.
- `InstantRepair` fixes the RV for free the moment it is wrecked.
- `RepairTakesADay` leaves the RV with Marco for 24 in-game hours. He texts you when it is ready.

### Changed
- Works on game version 0.4.7 and needs S1API **3.2.1** or newer. With an older S1API the mod loads but does nothing.
- In co-op, whoever pays for the repair, a lost package or a build-out pays from their own cash. Without enough
  cash the deal is turned down.

### Fixed
- Donna, Mrs. Ming and Marco offered no option on game 0.4.7, so the questline could not start.
- Crew hired for the RV stood outside and never worked. They walk in through the door now and work inside.
- After loading, a repaired RV could show "Back on the Road" again with a marker on the RV.
- Loading a save from the main menu could clear your progress and restart the questline.

## [2.6.2] - 2026-08-04

### Fixed
- Talking to Mrs. Ming could show an option that did nothing when you clicked it, leaving
  the questline stuck. The same could happen with Donna and Marco.
- When the game is slow handing over an NPC's dialogue, the mod waits for it now. If it
  never shows up at all, the NPC just says their line out loud and the step still goes through.

## [2.6.1] - 2026-08-01

### Changed
- Runs on Schedule I 0.4.6f11.
- Needs S1API 3.1.1, up from 3.0.5. Update it along with the mod.

## [2.6.0] - 2026-07-08

### Added
- The built-in translations are now always visible on disk: next to `_template.en.json`
  the mod also writes one template per shipped language - e.g. `_template.de.json` with
  the complete German text - into `UserData/DooDesch/Localization/RVRepairVan/`. Want to
  tweak a line? Copy the template to `de.json`, keep the lines you change, done. The
  templates refresh on every game start, so they always match the installed version.

## [2.5.0] - 2026-07-08

### Added
- Translation mods: translations can now also be installed as their own code-less
  mod packages shipping `Mods/Localization/RVRepairVan/<language code>.json` - so a
  community translation is one mod-manager click away instead of manual file copying.
  Per line, your own file in `UserData/DooDesch/Localization/` still wins over an
  installed translation mod, which wins over the built-in texts. How to publish one:
  https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-L10n/wiki

## [2.4.0] - 2026-07-08

### Added
- Bring your own translation: the mod now also loads translation files from
  `UserData/DooDesch/Localization/RVRepairVan/<language code>.json`. A few lines are
  enough to fix wording you don't like, and a full file adds a whole language the mod
  never shipped. Your entries always win over the built-in English/German.
- To make that easy, the mod writes `_template.en.json` into that folder on startup,
  listing every translatable string. Copy it, rename it to e.g. `fr.json`, translate
  the values, restart - done. Full guide:
  https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-L10n/wiki
- The localization layer now lives in its own open-source project,
  [ScheduleOne-L10n](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-L10n), so other mods
  can use the same system (and share the same `Language` setting).

## [2.3.0] - 2026-07-08

### Added
- German translation. The whole questline - journal entries, objectives, all of
  Donna's/Mrs. Ming's/Marco's dialogue and the quest items - is now available in German.
- Automatic language pick: German systems get German, everything else gets English
  (the game itself has no language setting, so the OS language decides).
- A shared `Language` setting (under `DooDesch` in `MelonPreferences.cfg` / the Mod
  Manager UI) to force a language: `auto`, `en` or `de`. Other DooDesch mods will use
  the same setting as they pick up translations.

## [2.2.1] - 2026-07-01

### Fixed
- The quest marker now tracks Marco, Mrs. Ming and Donna as they move around town, instead of
  freezing at wherever the target happened to be standing when the objective updated. Following
  the marker now leads you straight to the right person even while they walk their daily route.

## [2.2.0] - 2026-06-24

### Fixed
- Multiplayer co-op now works end to end and has been verified in a real two-player session:
  both players can play through the entire repair questline together. The previous build shipped
  co-op as experimental; this release fixes the issues that kept it from working.
- The joining player now gets the repair quest from Donna and sees the same quest progress as
  the host, instead of having no dialogue option or a different quest state.
- Both players can see, pick up, carry and hand in the errand items (Ming's crate, Marco's
  package). The quest advances no matter which player makes the delivery, and the pay-instead
  fallback still applies if the item is lost.
- The dead-drop marker now points to a valid drop for the joining player; previously the marker
  could lead to nothing on the client.
- Giving Marco samples to lower the price works for the joining player too, and the discount
  stays in sync for both players.
- Quest items are now reliably removed from the joining player's inventory once they are
  handed in.

## [2.1.0] - 2026-06-24

### Fixed
- Giving Marco a packaged sample no longer fails with "That ain't packaged" while you are
  holding sealed product. The check now reads your inventory instead of the in-hand item,
  which the game empties while a conversation is open.
- Each sample's discount is now based on the value of the single package you hand over,
  rather than scaling with how many were left in the stack.
- The quest marker (the wrench) could end up pointing nowhere after returning to the main
  menu and reloading a save; it now re-points to the right target once the world finishes
  loading.

### Added
- You can now choose which packaged product to give Marco: the dialogue lists each packaged
  product you are carrying together with the discount it would give.
- Marco actually consumes the sample you hand him now (the matching smoke/snort/eat
  animation and effects), instead of just taking it.
- Marco pays more for cleaner product and less for junk: the per-sample discount is scaled
  by quality (Trash 0.6x up to Heavenly 2.0x).
- Experimental host-authoritative co-op support. Single-player is unaffected; co-op has
  only had limited testing, so please report any multiplayer issues.

## [2.0.1] - 2026-06-17

### Added
- Marco now shows a persistent "What can I bring to lower the price?" reminder once you
  have earned his trust (after the package favour). It explains that bringing packaged
  product lowers the bill, so players who skipped the dialogue still know how to keep
  progressing and afford the repair. It appears whenever you are not currently holding
  product to hand over (when you are, the "give a sample" action is shown instead).

## [2.0.0] - 2026-06-17

A ground-up rebuild on S1API with a full story questline, real items, save-bound
persistence and a repair cinematic.

### Added
- "Back on the Road" questline (default `QuestMode = Questline`): the RV is wrecked in
  the intro, then Donna points you to Mrs. Ming, who sends you on a dead-drop crate
  errand, who refers you to Marco the mechanic at the docks.
- Native S1API dialogue: real in-conversation choices and replies (no more floating
  worldspace-only bubbles).
- Referral pricing: Marco charges $50,000 up front, dropping to $10,000 once you tell
  him "Mrs. Ming sent me". Optional packaged-sample discounts cut the bill further,
  down to the repair-price floor.
- Real carried items in dead drops (Ming's Crate, Marco's Package) cloned from in-game
  items so they have a proper inventory icon and in-hand model. Lose one and the NPC
  charges a $500 recovery fee to continue.
- Repair cinematic when you pay: the screen fades to black, repair sounds play, Marco
  grunts as he works, then it fades back and he tells you it is done. Plays in both
  Questline and Simple mode.
- A wrench quest icon in the journal/HUD tracker.
- Settings: `QuestMode`, `BasePriceNoReferral`, `BasePriceWithReferral`,
  `MinSampleDiscount`, `MaxSampleDiscount` (plus the existing `Enabled`, `RepairPrice`).

### Changed
- Persistence is now bound to the game save (via the S1API save system): progress is
  written when the game saves and read on load, so it stays in sync with the world.
  Finishing the quest without saving (or after a crash) correctly reverts, instead of
  leaving the quest stuck or the RV unrepairable.
- "Simple" mode (`QuestMode = Simple`) repairs directly at Marco for the flat
  `RepairPrice` and now also plays the repair cinematic.
- Repair sounds route through the game audio mixer, so they respect the in-game volume
  settings.

### Fixed
- Delivered quest items now correctly leave the inventory.
- The quest reliably starts once the RV is actually wrecked and the intro has passed,
  and never flickers on an intact RV.

pages.title: RVRepairVan
pages.description: Repair your wrecked RV in Schedule I through a tracked questline, with referral haggling and a repair cinematic.
pages.markdown:
| | |
|---|---|
| Latest release | `4.2.0` |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-RVRepairVan) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/RVRepairVan/) |
| Requires | MelonLoader 0.7.3, S1API Forked 3.2.1, Chassis 1.8.0, MarcosBodyshop 1.1.0, Sideload 1.35.0 |
| Help | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/rvrepairvan) |

> Your RV got blown up in the intro? Now you can fix it. A tracked side quest sends you
> from Donna at the motel to Mrs. Ming to Marco the mechanic, with dead-drop errands, a
> haggled price and a repair cinematic. After that, Marco turns the RV into a workshop. Built on
> [S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API).



![The RV driving through town at dusk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-RVRepairVan/main/docs/img/header.jpg)

## Features

- **"Back on the Road" questline** (default). After the RV is wrecked in the intro, the
  quest starts on its own. Donna at the motel sends you to **Mrs. Ming**. She wants a crate
  from a **dead drop** first, then she calls **Marco** at the docks.
- **Native dialogue** via S1API: choices inside the normal conversation, plus journal
  entries and the on-screen quest tracker.
- **Haggling.** Marco normally charges **$50,000**. Tell him Mrs. Ming sent you and it is
  **$10,000**. Ask *"Can you go any lower?"* and he sends you for a package of his. After
  that, every packaged product you hold out to him takes up to $500 off, down to a floor.
- **Carried quest items.** The crate and the package are items with an icon and an in-hand
  model. Lose one and the owner wants **$500** before the quest goes on.
- **Repair cinematic.** You pay, the screen goes black, Marco works on the RV, and it fades
  back in repaired. Plays in both modes.
- **Marco's build-outs.** Once the RV stands again, he sells three upgrades in his dialogue,
  each with its own short cinematic:
  - **Get the engine running** ($10,000): take the wheel and drive the RV anywhere. Parked
    away, it keeps its stations; the crew and deliveries wait until it is back on its spot.
    The roof hatch opens with E from inside. It shuts while you drive and opens again when you get up.
  - **Make room for a crew** ($15,000): three employees work inside. Put a locker in. Needs
    the workshop floor.
  - **Build a loading dock** ($25,000): your supplier delivers to the RV.
- **Marco's Bodyshop.** Drive the RV onto the lot in front of his garage and ask him
  to modify your vehicle:
  - **Paint**: Marco's metallic, matte and chrome colours, and the trim in a second colour.
    It stays after the trip home and a reload.
  - **Interior, part by part**: bed, kitchen bench, upper and lower cabinets, both walls,
    bedside table and the decor. Each part is paid once ($150 to $450); after that, taking
    it out or putting it back is free. A part goes back only on an empty floor.
  - **Workshop floor** ($7,500): build on every bit of floor the furniture leaves free.
  - **Engine parts** from Chassis, as for every car.
- **Save intercom.** The repaired RV has the wall intercom every property has. Press E on it
  to save.
- **Save-bound progress.** Quest progress and the repaired RV live in the game save. Quit
  without saving and they go back with the world.
- **Simple mode** (`QuestMode = Simple`): skip the story, talk to Marco, pay the flat price.
- **Live settings.** Change a price and Marco's offer updates without a restart.
- **English and German, and your language.** German on a German system, English
  everywhere else. Add or fix a translation with a JSON file, see Configuration.

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


| Component | Version / Source |
|-----------|------------------|
| Schedule I | `0.4.7f12` (IL2CPP, current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+` |
| S1API | [ifBars/S1API_Forked](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ifBars/S1API_Forked/) **3.2.1+** (dialogue, items, dead drops, money, save system) |
| Chassis | [DooDesch/Chassis](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Chassis/) **1.8.0+** (driver in the seat, first person, horn, indicators) |
| Marco's Bodyshop | [DooDesch/MarcosBodyshop](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/MarcosBodyshop/) **1.1.0+** (the garage menu for the interior and the workshop floor) |
| Sideload | [DooDesch/Sideload](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Sideload/) **1.35.0+** (draws the garage menu) |


</details>

<details><summary>Installation</summary>


### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

Install with a mod manager (r2modman / Gale) from the Schedule I community; the
dependencies (MelonLoader, S1API, Chassis, Marco's Bodyshop, Sideload) are pulled in automatically.

### Manual

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **S1API** (its DLLs go in `Mods/` and `Plugins/` per its own instructions).
3. Install **Chassis**, **Sideload** and **Marco's Bodyshop** per their own instructions.
4. Drop **`RVRepairVan.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.


</details>

## Configuration

Settings live in
`UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `RVRepairVan_01_Main`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `true` | Master on/off for the repair feature. |
| `QuestMode` | `Questline` | `Questline` = the full Donna -> Ming -> Marco story. `Simple` = just talk to Marco and pay. |
| `RepairPrice` | `1500` | Simple-mode price, and the price floor the questline can never go below. |
| `BasePriceNoReferral` | `50000` | Questline price if you walk straight to Marco. |
| `BasePriceWithReferral` | `10000` | Questline price after you drop Mrs. Ming's name. |
| `MinSampleDiscount` | `100` | Smallest price cut a single packaged sample can give. |
| `MaxSampleDiscount` | `500` | Largest price cut a single packaged sample can give. |
| `UpgradesEnabled` | `true` | Marco's build-outs. Off = the RV stays a plain shell. |
| `PriceInteriorBed` | `450` | Bodyshop: unlock the bed once. |
| `PriceInteriorKitchen` | `400` | Bodyshop: unlock the kitchen bench once. |
| `PriceInteriorUpperCabinets` | `300` | Bodyshop: unlock the upper cabinets once. |
| `PriceInteriorLowerCabinets` | `350` | Bodyshop: unlock the lower cabinets once. |
| `PriceInteriorBedroomWall` | `250` | Bodyshop: unlock the bedroom wall once. |
| `PriceInteriorCabWall` | `250` | Bodyshop: unlock the wall behind the driver once. |
| `PriceInteriorBedsideTable` | `150` | Bodyshop: unlock the bedside table once. |
| `PriceInteriorDecor` | `350` | Bodyshop: unlock the decor once. |
| `PriceWorkshopFloor` | `7500` | Bodyshop: the build grid covers the free floor. |
| `PriceCrewQuarters` | `15000` | Lets employees be stationed at the RV. Needs the workshop floor. |
| `PriceLoadingDock` | `25000` | Adds a delivery dock. |
| `PriceEngine` | `10000` | Makes the RV drivable. Away from its spot, the crew and deliveries wait. |
| `CrewSize` | `3` | How many employees the RV holds once the crew quarters are built. |
| `BuildGridExtraTiles` | `96` | Upper limit for the tiles the workshop floor lays on top of the RV's own 32. |
| `InstantRepair` | `false` | Repairs the RV free of charge as soon as it is wrecked. |
| `RepairTakesADay` | `false` | Marco keeps the RV for 24 in-game hours and texts you when it is done. |

The language lives in its own shared section (`DooDesch` - all DooDesch mods with
translations read the same value):

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Language` | `auto` | `auto` = follow the OS language (German -> German, otherwise English), or force a code like `en` / `de` / `fr`. Takes effect after a restart. |

### Add your own translation

Want the quest in a language the mod doesn't ship, or prefer different wording? After
one game start you'll find templates in `UserData/DooDesch/Localization/RVRepairVan/` -
`_template.en.json` with every translatable line, plus one per shipped language (e.g.
`_template.de.json` with the built-in German). Copy one, rename the copy to your
language code (e.g. `fr.json`), translate or tweak the values, restart. Your file wins
over the built-in texts.

Translations can also be installed as their own mods (a code-less package shipping
`Mods/Localization/RVRepairVan/<code>.json`) - and you can publish yours the same way.
Step-by-step guides: the [ScheduleOne-L10n wiki](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/l10n/).

Debug-only toggles (Destroy RV, Add $10,000, Dump state, Play repair cinematic) exist only
in development builds and are not shipped in the release.

## Usage

1. Play through the intro until the RV is wrecked and the early quests have begun.
2. The **"Back on the Road"** quest appears and points you to the **motel manager**.
3. Follow it: Donna -> **Mrs. Ming** (fetch her crate from the dead drop) -> **Marco** at
   the docks. Tell him Mrs. Ming sent you.
4. Optional: ask him to go lower, fetch his package, then hold out packaged product to
   him for more off the bill.
5. **Pay**, watch the repair, then go **see your RV**. Marco texts you about his build-outs.
6. For the interior and the workshop floor: buy the engine, drive the RV onto the lot
   in front of Marco's garage, get out and ask him to modify your vehicle.

Prefer no story? Set `QuestMode = Simple` and just pay Marco directly.

## Screenshots

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Wrecked RV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-RVRepairVan/main/docs/img/wreck.jpg) | ![Repaired RV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-RVRepairVan/main/docs/img/repaired.jpg) |
| ![Crew at work in the RV](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-RVRepairVan/main/docs/img/crew.jpg) | ![Gutted interior with the dash kept](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-RVRepairVan/main/docs/img/interior.jpg) |

<details><summary>Compatibility</summary>


- Disable other RV-repair or Marco-dialogue mods to avoid duplicate or conflicting choices.
- IL2CPP build only (current Steam public branch). A Mono build for the alternate branch is
  planned.


</details>

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


- **DooDesch** - mod author.
- **[ifBars/S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API)** - the modding API this is built on.


</details>

pages.title: API
pages.description: Public, stable entry point for mods that want to appear as a gamemode in Side Hustle's main-menu list.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public static class API
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Public, stable entry point for mods that want to appear as a gamemode in Side Hustle's main-menu list. Register early (e.g. in your mod's OnInitializeMelon). Registration is load-order independent, so it does not matter whether Side Hustle or your mod loads first. Reference SideHustle.dll and declare `[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]` so the hub loads first and your mod still loads cleanly if it is absent.

A gamemode id is the [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id) you registered, e.g. "doodesch.example". Ids are compared exactly, case included. A Steam id is the id64 number, the same value as [`SessionPlayer.SteamId`](../sessionplayer/#steamid).

**Example**

A singleplayer menu gamemode that shows a notice and returns to the hub:

```csharp
API.Register(new GamemodeDescriptor
{
    Id = "you.yourmode",
    DisplayName = "Your Mode",
    Description = "One line under the name.",
    Support = GamemodeSupport.Singleplayer,
    Surface = GamemodeSurface.MenuSpace,
    OnLaunchSingleplayer = ctx => { API.ShowNotice("Started."); ctx.ReturnToHub(); }
});
```

## Properties

### ApiVersion

```csharp
public static int ApiVersion { get; }
```

Added in `3.0.0`

The version of this API surface. Rule: it goes up by one with every release that ADDS public API, and never for a fix. 1 = the 1.x hub (Register, descriptor basics), 2 = the 2.x additions (host settings, presets, mod policy, world hygiene flags, KickPlayer), 3 = Side Hustle 3.0.0 (validation, lifecycle events, players, notices, gamemode messages, [`Has`](#has)).

A property, not a const: a const is copied into the consumer at ITS compile time and would report the version the consumer was built against instead of the one running. Reading this on a Side Hustle older than 3.0.0 throws `MissingMethodException`; the copy-in `SideHustleLink` shim reads it by reflection and returns 0 there.

### IsReady

```csharp
public static bool IsReady { get; internal set; }
```

True once Side Hustle's own OnInitializeMelon has run. `Ready` fires at the same moment.

### Registered

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<GamemodeDescriptor> Registered { get; }
```

Type: [`GamemodeDescriptor`](../gamemodedescriptor/)

A snapshot of the registered gamemodes. Since 3.0.0 this is a copy: registering or removing a gamemode later does not change a list you already hold.

### CurrentSession

```csharp
public static LaunchContext CurrentSession { get; }
```

Type: [`LaunchContext`](../launchcontext/)

Added in `3.0.0`

The running gamemode session, or null. Set just before `SessionStarted` and cleared just before `SessionEnded`. Since 3.0.0.

### Players

```csharp
public static IReadOnlyList<SessionPlayer> Players { get; }
```

Type: [`SessionPlayer`](../sessionplayer/)

Added in `3.0.0`

The players in the current session as a snapshot copy (empty outside a session). A singleplayer session holds only the local player. Display names follow the session alias where one is known. Since 3.0.0.

### MaxMessageBytes

```csharp
public static int MaxMessageBytes { get; }
```

Added in `3.0.0`

The largest payload [`SendToAll`](#sendtoallstring-string-byte) and [`SendTo`](#sendtoulong-string-string-byte) accept, in bytes. Since 3.0.0.

**Value** 8192 (8 KB).

## Methods

### Has

```csharp
public static bool Has(string feature)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

True when this Side Hustle supports the named feature. Use the constants on [`ApiFeatures`](../apifeatures/); matching is case-insensitive and an unknown name is false. Exists since 3.0.0 (API version 3): on an older Side Hustle the method itself is missing, so call it through the `SideHustleLink` shim or guard it.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `feature` | A constant from [`ApiFeatures`](../apifeatures/), e.g. [`ApiFeatures.Messages`](../apifeatures/#messages) ("messages"). Leading and trailing spaces are ignored. Null or empty is false. |

### Register

```csharp
public static void Register(GamemodeDescriptor descriptor)
```

Types: [`GamemodeDescriptor`](../gamemodedescriptor/)

Register (or replace, by [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id)) a gamemode. Replacing an existing id is allowed and makes hot-reload / double-registration safe. Since 3.0.0 the descriptor is checked here and every problem is logged with the gamemode id and the field name; nothing is rejected that worked before. A second registration of the same id from a DIFFERENT mod is logged as a warning and still replaces the first.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `descriptor` | The gamemode to list. Null throws `ArgumentNullException`. An empty [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id) throws `ArgumentException`. An empty [`GamemodeDescriptor.DisplayName`](../gamemodedescriptor/#displayname) is set to the id. |

### Unregister

```csharp
public static bool Unregister(string id)
```

Remove a previously registered gamemode. Returns true if one was removed.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | The [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id) it registered with, e.g. "doodesch.example". Matched exactly, case included. Null or empty returns false. |

### KickPlayer

```csharp
public static bool KickPlayer(
    ulong steamId64,
    string reason = "Kicked by host")
```

Added in `1.5.3`

Host-only: kick the connected player with this Steam id (id64) from the current session. A no-op on a client or if no such player is connected, and never kicks the host itself. Returns true if a player was kicked. Reusable by any gamemode that manages a Side Hustle lobby.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `steamId64` | The player's Steam id64, the same value as [`SessionPlayer.SteamId`](../sessionplayer/#steamid). It is matched against the player's `Player.PlayerCode`. |
| `reason` | The reason passed to the kick and written to the log. Null or empty uses "Kicked by host". |

### ShowNotice

```csharp
public static void ShowNotice(string text, float seconds = 4f)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Show a short notice to the local player. In the world it is the game's own notification popup (titled with the running gamemode's name) and stays `seconds`; in the menu it is the hub's toast, whose duration is fixed. Safe from any thread: calls off the main thread are queued to the next frame. Since 3.0.0.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `text` | The notice text, e.g. "Round starts in 10 seconds". |
| `seconds` | How long the world popup stays, in seconds. 0, a negative value or NaN uses 4. The menu toast ignores it. |

### SendToAll(string, string, byte[])

```csharp
public static bool SendToAll(
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    byte[] payload)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send bytes to every other player in the current session (not to yourself). Reliable, over Steam P2P on Side Hustle's own channel; at most [`MaxMessageBytes`](#maxmessagebytes) bytes. Returns false, with a log line, when there is no session lobby or the message is refused. Off the main thread it is queued and returns true. Since 3.0.0.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `gamemodeId` | Your [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id), e.g. "doodesch.example". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `channel` | Your own message name, e.g. "ping" or "state". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `payload` | The bytes to send, at most [`MaxMessageBytes`](#maxmessagebytes) (8192). Null sends an empty payload. |

**Returns** True when the message went out or was queued from another thread. False when it was refused; the log line says why.

### SendToAll(string, string, string)

```csharp
public static bool SendToAll(string gamemodeId, string channel, string text)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send UTF-8 text to every other player in the current session. Same rules as the byte overload. Since 3.0.0.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `gamemodeId` | Your [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id). Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `channel` | Your own message name, e.g. "ping". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `text` | The text, sent as UTF-8. The encoded bytes count against [`MaxMessageBytes`](#maxmessagebytes). Null sends an empty text. |

### SendTo(ulong, string, string, byte[])

```csharp
public static bool SendTo(
    ulong steamId,
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    byte[] payload)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send bytes to one player of the current session by Steam id. The target must be in the session's lobby; sending to yourself is refused. Same rules as [`SendToAll`](#sendtoallstring-string-byte). Since 3.0.0.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `steamId` | The target's [`SessionPlayer.SteamId`](../sessionplayer/#steamid), e.g. [`SessionMessage.SenderSteamId`](../sessionmessage/#sendersteamid) to answer a message. |
| `gamemodeId` | Your [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id). Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `channel` | Your own message name, e.g. "pong". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `payload` | The bytes to send, at most [`MaxMessageBytes`](#maxmessagebytes) (8192). Null sends an empty payload. |

### SendTo(ulong, string, string, string)

```csharp
public static bool SendTo(
    ulong steamId,
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    string text)
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Send UTF-8 text to one player of the current session. Same rules as the byte overload. Since 3.0.0.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `steamId` | The target's [`SessionPlayer.SteamId`](../sessionplayer/#steamid). |
| `gamemodeId` | Your [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id). Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `channel` | Your own message name, e.g. "pong". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8. |
| `text` | The text, sent as UTF-8. The encoded bytes count against [`MaxMessageBytes`](#maxmessagebytes). Null sends an empty text. |

### OnMessage

```csharp
public static void OnMessage(
    string gamemodeId,
    Action<SessionMessage> handler)
```

Types: [`SessionMessage`](../sessionmessage/)

Added in `3.0.0`

Receive the messages sent for `gamemodeId` (any channel - read [`SessionMessage.Channel`](../sessionmessage/#channel)). Handlers run on the main thread. Only packets from members of the current session's lobby are delivered; the sender id comes from Steam, never from the payload. Since 3.0.0.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `gamemodeId` | Your [`GamemodeDescriptor.Id`](../gamemodedescriptor/#id), the same id the senders pass. Matched exactly, case included. Null or empty is ignored with a warning. |
| `handler` | Called once per received message. Null is ignored with a warning. |

**Example**

Answer a "ping" with a "pong" to the sender:

```csharp
API.OnMessage("you.yourmode", m =>
{
    if (m.Channel == "ping") API.SendTo(m.SenderSteamId, "you.yourmode", "pong", "hi " + m.Text);
});
API.SendToAll("you.yourmode", "ping", "hello");
```

### OffMessage

```csharp
public static bool OffMessage(
    string gamemodeId,
    Action<SessionMessage> handler)
```

Types: [`SessionMessage`](../sessionmessage/)

Added in `3.0.0`

Remove a handler added with [`OnMessage`](#onmessage). Returns true if it was registered. Since 3.0.0.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `gamemodeId` | The id the handler was added with. |
| `handler` | The same delegate instance passed to [`OnMessage`](#onmessage). |

pages.title: GamemodeDescriptor
pages.description: Everything a gamemode mod tells Side Hustle about itself.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class GamemodeDescriptor
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Everything a gamemode mod tells Side Hustle about itself. Pass one of these to [`API.Register`](../api/#register) (usually from your mod's OnInitializeMelon). Only [`Id`](#id), [`DisplayName`](#displayname) and the launch callback for your [`Support`](#support) mode are required; every multiplayer field is optional so a singleplayer-only mod registers minimally.

**Example**

A multiplayer World gamemode with one host setting:

```csharp
var d = new GamemodeDescriptor
{
    Id = "you.yourmode",
    DisplayName = "Your Mode",
    Support = GamemodeSupport.Multiplayer,
    Surface = GamemodeSurface.World,
    DownloadUrl = "https://github.com/you/yourmode",
    OnHostMultiplayer = Start,
    OnJoinMultiplayer = Start,
    OnExitToHub = Stop,
    HostSettings = new[]
    {
        new SettingDescriptor { Key = "len", Label = "Round length", Type = SettingType.Slider,
                                Min = 10, Max = 120, Step = 10, WholeNumbers = true, Default = "30", Unit = "s" }
    }
};
API.Register(WorldHygiene.CleanWorld(d));
```

## Fields

### Id

```csharp
public string Id
```

Stable, unique key (e.g. "doodesch.inkubator"). Used for de-duplication and, later, lobby filtering.

**Value** 3-48 characters of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' or '-', e.g. "doodesch.prophunt". Another form logs a warning and still registers. Compared exactly, case included. Required: null or empty makes [`API.Register`](../api/#register) throw.

### DisplayName

```csharp
public string DisplayName
```

Name shown in the gamemode list.

**Value** E.g. "PropHunt". Null or empty shows [`Id`](#id) instead.

### Description

```csharp
public string Description
```

Short one-line description shown under the name.

### Author

```csharp
public string Author
```

Author shown in the list (optional).

### Icon

```csharp
public Sprite Icon
```

Icon sprite for the list row. If null, Side Hustle builds one from [`IconTex`](#icontex).

### IconTex

```csharp
public Texture2D IconTex
```

Icon texture; Side Hustle wraps it in a Sprite when [`Icon`](#icon) is null.

### IconResource

```csharp
public string IconResource
```

Added in `3.0.0`

Name of a PNG embedded in your mod's assembly (the manifest resource name, e.g. "YourMod.icon.png"). Used only when [`Icon`](#icon) and [`IconTex`](#icontex) are both null: the hub loads it into [`IconTex`](#icontex) the first time it draws the row, so you need no Unity image code. A name that does not resolve is logged together with the resource names the assembly does have. Since 3.0.0.

Embed the PNG as `<AssemblyName>.hub-icon.png` (csproj: `<EmbeddedResource Include="icon.png"
LogicalName="YourMod.hub-icon.png" />`) and the hub finds it without this field, and also while the boot gate holds your mod back, when none of your code has run yet.

### Support

```csharp
public GamemodeSupport Support = GamemodeSupport.Singleplayer
```

Type: [`GamemodeSupport`](../gamemodesupport/)

Which play modes this gamemode supports.

### Surface

```csharp
public GamemodeSurface Surface = GamemodeSurface.MenuSpace
```

Type: [`GamemodeSurface`](../gamemodesurface/)

Whether the gamemode runs as a menu overlay or needs the game world.

### DownloadUrl

```csharp
public string DownloadUrl
```

Added in `2.0.0`

Where to get this mod (its Thunderstore/Nexus/GitHub page). When set, Side Hustle advertises this gamemode's live public lobbies to players who do NOT have it installed, with a "Download Mod" button that opens this page. Null = still advertised by name (see [`Advertise`](#advertise)) but with no download link. Only links on known mod hosts (Thunderstore, Nexus, GitHub) are opened.

**Value** An absolute https link on thunderstore.io, nexusmods.com, github.com or doodesch.de, or a subdomain of one, e.g. "https://github.com/you/yourmode". Any other link is shown but never opened.

### Advertise

```csharp
public bool Advertise = true
```

Added in `2.0.0`

When true (default), this gamemode's PUBLIC lobbies are advertised in the Side Hustle menu of players who do not have it installed, so they can discover it. Set false to stay invisible to non-installers - e.g. a work-in-progress gamemode you do not want discovered during development. This only affects that discovery listing; the gamemode is always fully hostable and joinable by people who have it.

### BlockVanillaQuests

```csharp
public bool BlockVanillaQuests = false
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle blocks every vanilla quest from starting for the duration of the session (a Harmony prefix on Quest.Begin). Keeps a clean slate - no tutorial/dealer quest chains, phone prompts, or NPC waypoints fighting the gamemode. Quests are host-authoritative so this matters on the host. Default false.

### AllowedQuestTitles

```csharp
public string[] AllowedQuestTitles
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Quest titles EXEMPT from [`BlockVanillaQuests`](#blockvanillaquests) - e.g. a gamemode's own guide quest. Their `Quest.Begin` is allowed through even while vanilla quests are blocked. Default none.

**Value** Each entry is compared exactly, case included, with the quest's `title`, e.g. "PropHunt" for PropHunt's guide quest. Null or empty entries are skipped.

### SkipIntro

```csharp
public bool SkipIntro = false
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle skips the new-game intro cutscene + character-creator (sets the player's HasCompletedIntro before the intro gate runs), so players drop straight into the world. Default false.

### ForceNewGame

```csharp
public bool ForceNewGame = false
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Has no effect. Side Hustle boots a clean scratch world (clears the scratch folder and copies DefaultSave) on every World launch anyway, and never touches a real save slot. Kept so mods that set it still load. Default false.

### BlockSaveDuringSession

```csharp
public bool BlockSaveDuringSession = false
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle blocks every vanilla save (both SaveManager.Save overloads) for the duration of the session. A gamemode runs on a throwaway scratch world and mutates transient state (teleports, locked doors, swapped appearances); persisting that to disk would corrupt the save. The Save button still appears but does nothing. Saving works normally again once the session ends. Default false.

### SuppressNpcCombatReactions

```csharp
public bool SuppressNpcCombatReactions = false
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle stops NPCs from reacting to hunter/player GUNFIRE for the session (no panic/flee/cover, no civilian police-call, no WANTED pursuit, no bystander weapon-impact) - so a gamemode can fire weapons without derailing the NPC schedule. Purely subtractive (prefixes on NPCAwareness NoiseEvent/VisionEvent for the gunshot/discharge cases, NPC.SendImpact, and the ranged-weapon aim scan); every other NPC awareness (footsteps, deals, vandalism) is untouched. Default false.

### DisableVanillaPlayerDeath

```csharp
public bool DisableVanillaPlayerDeath = false
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true, Side Hustle cancels all vanilla PLAYER death for the session (prefix on PlayerHealth.TakeDamage + SendDie) - players cannot die to real weapon damage while the session runs. Use this when elimination is the gamemode's own concern (e.g. a host-validated catch) and vanilla death + medical-centre respawn would eject a player from the play area. Damage to NPCs/props is untouched. Default false.

### OnLaunchSingleplayer

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnLaunchSingleplayer
```

Type: [`LaunchContext`](../launchcontext/)

Invoked to start singleplayer. Required for Singleplayer/Hybrid gamemodes.

### OnHostMultiplayer

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnHostMultiplayer
```

Type: [`LaunchContext`](../launchcontext/)

Invoked to start hosting a multiplayer session. Optional.

### OnJoinMultiplayer

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnJoinMultiplayer
```

Type: [`LaunchContext`](../launchcontext/)

Invoked to join a multiplayer session. Optional.

### OnExitToHub

```csharp
public Action<LaunchContext> OnExitToHub
```

Type: [`LaunchContext`](../launchcontext/)

Invoked when Side Hustle tears the gamemode down (e.g. the player backs out). Optional.

### Policy

```csharp
public ModPolicy Policy
```

Type: [`ModPolicy`](../modpolicy/)

Added in `1.2.0`

Optional policy controlling which other mods may stay loaded while this gamemode runs. Null = no restriction (default). See [`ModPolicy`](../modpolicy/).

### DefaultRequiredModsOnly

```csharp
public bool DefaultRequiredModsOnly = false
```

Added in `1.5.3`

When true, the Host form defaults the mod-set choice to "Required mods only" (an isolated profile with just this gamemode's mods) instead of "Current installed mods" - e.g. a multiplayer gamemode that wants everyone on an identical, clean set. The host can still switch it before starting. Only takes effect when [`Policy`](#policy) is declared and would actually change the set (and is not blocked). Default false.

### HostSettings

```csharp
public SettingDescriptor[] HostSettings
```

Type: [`SettingDescriptor`](../settingdescriptor/)

Added in `1.4.0`

Optional host-configurable settings. Side Hustle renders these as a form on the Host screen and ships the chosen values to your launch callbacks via [`LaunchContext.Multiplayer`](../launchcontext/#multiplayer)'s config blob. Null = none. See [`SettingDescriptor`](../settingdescriptor/).

**Value** Shown in array order. Each [`SettingDescriptor.Key`](../settingdescriptor/#key) must be unique; a repeated key logs a warning and both controls write the same value.

### Presets

```csharp
public SettingPreset[] Presets
```

Type: [`SettingPreset`](../settingpreset/)

Added in `1.5.0`

Optional one-click presets for [`HostSettings`](#hostsettings). Side Hustle shows a picker above the form; selecting a preset cascades its values into the matching controls (the host can still tweak after). Null/empty = no picker. See [`SettingPreset`](../settingpreset/).

**Value** The form opens on the preset marked [`SettingPreset.DefaultSelected`](../settingpreset/#defaultselected), else on the best fit for the lobby size, else on the first entry.

## Properties

### AllowsSingleplayer

```csharp
public bool AllowsSingleplayer { get; }
```

True when this descriptor can be launched in singleplayer.

### AllowsMultiplayer

```csharp
public bool AllowsMultiplayer { get; }
```

True when this descriptor exposes multiplayer (host/join).

pages.title: GamemodeSupport
pages.description: Which multiplayer modes a gamemode supports.
pages.markdown:
```csharp

```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Which multiplayer modes a gamemode supports. Side Hustle uses this to decide whether selecting the gamemode launches straight into singleplayer or first shows the Singleplayer / Host / Join choice.

## Fields

```csharp
Singleplayer
```

Singleplayer only. Selecting it launches immediately.

### Multiplayer

```csharp
Multiplayer
```

Multiplayer only. Selecting it shows Host / Join.

### Hybrid

```csharp
Hybrid
```

Both. Selecting it shows Singleplayer / Host / Join.

pages.title: GamemodeSurface
pages.description: Where a gamemode runs.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public enum GamemodeSurface
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Where a gamemode runs. [`MenuSpace`](#menuspace) gamemodes build their own overlay on top of the main menu and never load a save (e.g. the Inkubator tattoo editor). [`World`](#world) gamemodes need the actual game world, so Side Hustle boots a throwaway save before handing control over.

## Fields

### MenuSpace

```csharp
MenuSpace
```

Runs as an overlay in the menu scene; no save is loaded.

### World

```csharp
World
```

Needs the loaded game world; Side Hustle boots a throwaway save first.

pages.title: SideHustle API
pages.description: Look up every public type and member of SideHustle 3.3.0.
pages.markdown:
## Use this API

Reference `SideHustle.dll` from your Mods folder:

```xml
<Reference Include="SideHustle">
  <HintPath>$(ModsDirectory)\SideHustle.dll</HintPath>
  <Private>false</Private>
</Reference>
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]
```

Without SideHustle its types are missing too. Call it only after you know it loaded.

First steps: [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/).

Source: [`Api/API.cs`, `Api/ApiFeatures.cs`, `Api/GamemodeDescriptor.cs`, `Api/GamemodeTypes.cs`, `Api/LaunchContext.cs`, `Api/ModPolicy.cs`, `Api/Registry.cs`, `Api/SessionTypes.cs`, `Api/SettingDescriptor.cs`, `Api/WorldHygiene.cs`, `Multiplayer/MultiplayerInfo.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/blob/v3.3.0/Api/API.cs) at `v3.3.0`.

pages.title: LaunchContext
pages.description: Passed to a gamemode's launch callback.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class LaunchContext
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Passed to a gamemode's launch callback. Carries who is launching (host / client / singleplayer) and, for multiplayer, the lobby id. The gamemode calls [`ReturnToHub`](#returntohub) when it is finished so Side Hustle can restore the menu.

**Example**

One callback for every role, reading a host setting:

```csharp
static void Start(LaunchContext ctx)
{
    int seconds = ctx.Multiplayer?.GetInt("len", 30) ?? 30;   // null in singleplayer
    if (ctx.Role == SessionRole.Host) { /* start the round */ }
    // later, when the gamemode is done:
    ctx.ReturnToHub();
}
```

## Properties

### Descriptor

```csharp
public GamemodeDescriptor Descriptor { get; internal set; }
```

Type: [`GamemodeDescriptor`](../gamemodedescriptor/)

The descriptor being launched.

### IsHost

```csharp
public bool? IsHost { get; internal set; }
```

true = host, false = client, null = singleplayer.

### LobbyId

```csharp
public ulong LobbyId { get; internal set; }
```

Steam lobby id for multiplayer; 0 for singleplayer.

### IsSingleplayer

```csharp
public bool IsSingleplayer { get; }
```

True when this is a singleplayer launch.

### Role

```csharp
public SessionRole Role { get; }
```

Type: [`SessionRole`](../sessionrole/)

Added in `3.0.0`

Who the local player is in this session; the same information as [`IsHost`](#ishost) as an enum. Since 3.0.0.

### PlayerCount

```csharp
public int PlayerCount { get; internal set; }
```

Added in `1.1.0`

Players currently in the lobby (1 for singleplayer).

### HostName

```csharp
public string HostName { get; internal set; }
```

Added in `1.1.0`

The host's display name: their session alias when they set one on the Host form, else their Steam persona. On a client it is read from the lobby (`sh_host_name`), which the host writes the same way. Null for singleplayer.

### HasPassword

```csharp
public bool HasPassword { get; internal set; }
```

Added in `1.1.0`

True if the lobby was created with a password.

### Multiplayer

```csharp
public Multiplayer.MultiplayerInfo Multiplayer { get; internal set; }
```

Type: [`MultiplayerInfo`](../multiplayerinfo/)

Added in `1.1.0`

The full multiplayer payload (max players, gamemode name, the host's free-form config blob, ...). Null for singleplayer. Use this to pass gamemode-specific settings from host to clients.

## Methods

### ReturnToHub

```csharp
public void ReturnToHub()
```

Call this from your gamemode when it is done (e.g. the player clicks "Back"). Side Hustle restores the main menu and re-shows the hub. Only the first call counts: once the session was ended - by this call or by Side Hustle aborting it - later calls are ignored and logged.

pages.title: ModPolicy
pages.description: An optional per-gamemode policy that controls which OTHER mods are active while the gamemode runs.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class ModPolicy
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `1.2.0`

An optional per-gamemode policy that controls which OTHER mods are active while the gamemode runs. When a gamemode with a policy is launched, Side Hustle restarts the game into a temporary, isolated profile that loads ONLY the allowed mods, after a confirmation that lists exactly what changes, then continues into the gamemode; leaving the gamemode restarts back to your full mod set. Your installed mods are never renamed, moved or deleted - the profile is a throwaway sandbox - so mod managers stay in sync and a normal launch always loads everything.

Mods are matched by their MelonLoader display name OR their DLL file name (case-insensitive, ".dll" optional). You never need to list the essentials - they are always kept: MelonLoader, S1API, Side Hustle, this gamemode's own mod, the Mod Manager & Phone App, and (for multiplayer gamemodes) the multiplayer libraries. Mods that a kept mod depends on are kept too.

## Fields

### AllowedMods

```csharp
public string[] AllowedMods
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Extra mods that are allowed to remain loaded alongside this gamemode. Everything loaded that is neither allowed, required, nor an essential (or a dependency of a kept mod) gets disabled.

**Value** MelonLoader names or DLL file names, e.g. `new[] { "Snitch", "Inkorporated" }`. A name that is not installed is skipped. Null or empty allows no extra mods.

### RequiredMods

```csharp
public string[] RequiredMods
```

Added in `1.2.0`

Mods this gamemode needs. If present but disabled they are enabled; if a required mod is not installed at all the player is told to install it first. Required mods are implicitly allowed.

**Value** MelonLoader names or DLL file names, e.g. `new[] { "WhatsDab", "Sideload" }`. A required name that is not installed blocks a singleplayer launch, and hosting offers only the current mods. Null or empty requires nothing.

Namespace `SideHustle.Multiplayer`

Added in `1.1.0`

The multiplayer payload carried on [`LaunchContext.Multiplayer`](../launchcontext/#multiplayer). Populated by Side Hustle from the Steam lobby's namespaced metadata (the `sh_*` keys). The host fills it from its host options; a joining client reads it back from the lobby. [`ConfigBlob`](#configblob) is a free-form string the host writes (lobby key `sh_config`) so a gamemode can ship its own settings to clients with no extra netcode.

### MaxPlayers

```csharp

```

Added in `1.1.0`

Maximum players the host opened the lobby for.

**Value** The host form offers 2 up to the lobby cap. It starts at the host's last choice, else at 4 or the cap, whichever is lower.

### GamemodeName


Added in `1.1.0`

Display name of the gamemode (lobby key `sh_gamemode_name`).

### LobbyName


Added in `1.5.0`

Host-chosen lobby name (lobby key `sh_name`); may be empty.


Added in `1.5.0`

### HostName


Added in `1.1.0`

The host's name as other players see it: the display name the host chose for this gamemode, or their Steam persona name when none is set (lobby key `sh_host_name`).

### HasPassword


Added in `1.1.0`

True if the lobby is password-protected (lobby key `sh_pw` = "1").

### ConfigBlob

Added in `1.1.0`

Free-form per-gamemode payload the host published (lobby key `sh_config`); may be null.

Added in `1.5.0`

The host's gamemode build fingerprint (lobby key `sh_build`; the DLL's ModuleVersionId). Side Hustle compares this to the joining client's local build at join time and warns on mismatch. May be empty.

### GamemodeId


Added in `2.0.0`

The gamemode's stable id (lobby key `sh_gamemode`); used to match a lobby against the installed gamemodes and to group "not installed" advertisements by gamemode. May be empty.

### DownloadUrl

Added in `2.0.0`

Where to get the gamemode mod (lobby key `sh_url`), advertised by the host so a player who does not have it installed can open its download page. May be empty.


pages.title: SettingDescriptor
pages.description: One host-configurable setting a gamemode exposes.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class SettingDescriptor
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `1.4.0`

One host-configurable setting a gamemode exposes. Side Hustle renders these as a form on the Host screen, then ships the chosen values to the gamemode (host and clients) via the launch context's config blob - see [`GamemodeDescriptor.HostSettings`](../gamemodedescriptor/#hostsettings) and [`MultiplayerInfo`](../multiplayerinfo/)'s getters.

Every value is stored as a string under [`Key`](#key). Keep keys short (the whole blob rides on Steam lobby metadata) and stable (they are the wire format your gamemode reads back).

Stored form per [`Type`](#type): a Slider stores an integer such as "30" with [`WholeNumbers`](#wholenumbers), else a number with up to two decimals such as "0.25". Numbers use the invariant culture (a dot, no thousands separator). A Toggle stores "1" or "0". Segmented and Dropdown store the chosen entry of [`Values`](#values), or of [`Options`](#options) when Values is null. Text stores the typed text. The whole blob of all settings should stay under about 1500 bytes; a larger worst case logs a warning at [`API.Register`](../api/#register).

**Example**

One setting per type, read back in the launch callback:

```csharp
HostSettings = new[]
{
    new SettingDescriptor { Key = "len", Label = "Session length", Type = SettingType.Slider,
                            Min = 10, Max = 120, Step = 10, WholeNumbers = true, Default = "30", Unit = "s" },
    new SettingDescriptor { Key = "ping", Label = "Ping on start", Type = SettingType.Toggle, Default = "1" },
    new SettingDescriptor { Key = "pace", Label = "Pace", Type = SettingType.Segmented,
                            Options = new[] { "Slow", "Normal", "Fast" }, Values = new[] { "s", "n", "f" }, Default = "n" },
    new SettingDescriptor { Key = "motd", Label = "Welcome text", Type = SettingType.Text, Default = "Have fun" }
};
// in OnHostMultiplayer / OnJoinMultiplayer:
int seconds = ctx.Multiplayer?.GetInt("len", 30) ?? 30;
```

## Fields

### Key

```csharp
public string Key
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Stable, short id used to store/read the value (e.g. "round_time"). Required.

**Value** Unique within the gamemode, e.g. "len". Compared exactly, case included. Null or empty skips the setting on the form. Read it back with [`MultiplayerInfo.GetSetting`](../multiplayerinfo/#getsetting).

### Label

```csharp
public string Label
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Label shown to the host. Required.

### Hint

```csharp
public string Hint
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Optional one-line help shown under the label.

### Category

```csharp
public string Category
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Optional category name. The host form renders a section header whenever the category changes between consecutive settings, so order settings by category. Null/empty = no header for that setting.

### Type

```csharp
public SettingType Type = SettingType.Toggle
```

Type: [`SettingType`](../settingtype/)

Added in `1.4.0`

The control to render.

**Value** Default [`SettingType.Toggle`](../settingtype/#toggle).

### Default

```csharp
public string Default
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Default stored value (string form, parsed per [`Type`](#type)).

**Value** Slider: a number in the invariant culture, e.g. "30". Not a number starts at [`Min`](#min); a value outside Min..Max is clamped. Toggle: "1", "0", "true" or "false"; anything else starts off. Segmented and Dropdown: one of the stored values, e.g. "n"; anything else selects the first option. Text: the starting text. Null starts the slider at Min, the toggle off, the first option selected and the text empty.

### Unit

```csharp
public string Unit
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Optional unit suffix shown next to a slider value (e.g. "s", "m", "players").

### Min

```csharp
public float Min = 0f
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Slider minimum.

**Value** In the setting's own unit, e.g. 10. Default 0. Above [`Max`](#max) logs an error.

### Max

```csharp
public float Max = 1f
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Slider maximum.

**Value** In the setting's own unit, e.g. 120. Default 1. Leaving the range at 0..1 logs a warning.

### Step

```csharp
public float Step = 1f
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Slider step/granularity (0 = continuous).

**Value** In the setting's own unit, e.g. 10. Default 1. 0 or less means continuous, or steps of 1 with [`WholeNumbers`](#wholenumbers). A negative step logs a warning.

### WholeNumbers

```csharp
public bool WholeNumbers
```

Added in `1.4.0`

When true the slider snaps to whole numbers (integer setting).

### Options

```csharp
public string[] Options
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Segmented option labels (what the host sees).

**Value** Used by Segmented and Dropdown, e.g. `new[] { "Slow", "Normal", "Fast" }`. Null shows "Off" and "On". An empty array logs an error and shows nothing.

### Values

```csharp
public string[] Values
```

Added in `1.4.0`

Stored value per option, parallel to [`Options`](#options). When null the option label is stored.

**Value** Same length as Options, e.g. `new[] { "s", "n", "f" }`. Fewer entries store the label for the rest and log a warning. More entries log an error.

pages.title: SettingPreset
pages.description: A named bundle of host-setting values a gamemode can offer as a one-click preset (e.g.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public sealed class SettingPreset
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `1.5.0`

A named bundle of host-setting values a gamemode can offer as a one-click preset (e.g. "Classic Hunt"). Side Hustle shows a preset picker above the settings form; selecting one CASCADES its [`Values`](#values) into the matching controls (matched by [`SettingDescriptor.Key`](../settingdescriptor/#key)), which the host can then still tweak. Values use the same wire format as the controls: a Slider's number, a Toggle's "1"/"0", a Segmented's stored value. Keys with no matching control are ignored (forward-compatible with not-yet-built settings).

## Fields

### Name

```csharp
public string Name
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Display name shown in the picker (e.g. "Classic Hunt"). Required.

### Hint

```csharp
public string Hint
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Optional one-line description shown under the picker while this preset is selected.

### Values

```csharp
public System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary<string, string> Values
```

Added in `1.5.0`

The setting values this preset applies, keyed by [`SettingDescriptor.Key`](../settingdescriptor/#key).

**Value** Each value in the control's stored form, e.g. `{ "len", "10" }, { "pace", "f" }`. Keys with no matching setting log a warning and are ignored. Null applies nothing.

### Experimental

```csharp
public bool Experimental
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true the picker marks this preset as experimental (a badge + sorted to the back) - use it for presets whose headline mechanic is not fully built yet.

### Recommended

```csharp
public string Recommended
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Optional human-readable player-count recommendation shown in the picker (e.g. "Best for 2-6").

### MinPlayers

```csharp
public int MinPlayers
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Player-count range this preset suits best. When the lobby size falls in [[`MinPlayers`](#minplayers), [`MaxPlayers`](#maxplayers)] the form may auto-select it on open. 0 = unspecified.

**Value** Inclusive player count, e.g. 2. The auto-select needs both ends above 0 and skips experimental presets. Among several fits the narrowest range wins.

### MaxPlayers

```csharp
public int MaxPlayers
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Upper end of the player-count range, inclusive, e.g. 4. 0 = unspecified. See [`MinPlayers`](#minplayers).

### Mode

```csharp
public string Mode
```

Added in `1.5.0`

Canonical "mode" this preset represents (e.g. "Infection"). When the host tweaks a preset, the effective mode shown to joiners becomes "Custom - {Mode}". Defaults to [`Name`](#name) when null.

### DefaultSelected

```csharp
public bool DefaultSelected
```

Added in `1.5.0`

When true the form opens on this preset, overriding the player-count best-fit. Used for a saved "Custom" preset that should be pre-selected next time the host opens the form.

pages.title: WorldHygiene
pages.description: Ready-made sets of the world hygiene flags on `GamemodeDescriptor`, so a World gamemode does not have to know which five booleans belong together.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public static class WorldHygiene
```

Namespace `SideHustle`

Added in `3.0.0`

Ready-made sets of the world hygiene flags on [`GamemodeDescriptor`](../gamemodedescriptor/), so a World gamemode does not have to know which five booleans belong together. Each method sets the flags on the descriptor you pass and returns it, and only ever switches flags ON: anything you set yourself stays set. Since 3.0.0.

## Methods

### CleanWorld

```csharp
public static GamemodeDescriptor CleanWorld(
    GamemodeDescriptor descriptor,
    params string[] allowedQuestTitles)
```

Types: [`GamemodeDescriptor`](../gamemodedescriptor/)

Added in `3.0.0`

A clean scratch world: vanilla quests blocked (except `allowedQuestTitles`), the intro skipped and saving blocked for the session. Fits most World gamemodes.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `descriptor` | The descriptor to change. Null logs a warning and returns null. |
| `allowedQuestTitles` | Quest titles that may still start, e.g. "PropHunt"; see [`GamemodeDescriptor.AllowedQuestTitles`](../gamemodedescriptor/#allowedquesttitles). None keeps the titles already set. |

**Returns** The same descriptor, so the call fits inside [`API.Register`](../api/#register).

### Arena

```csharp
public static GamemodeDescriptor Arena(
    GamemodeDescriptor descriptor,
    params string[] allowedQuestTitles)
```

Types: [`GamemodeDescriptor`](../gamemodedescriptor/)

Added in `3.0.0`

[`CleanWorld`](#cleanworld) plus no NPC reactions to gunfire and no vanilla player death - for a gamemode whose players shoot and whose eliminations are its own (the set PropHunt uses).

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `descriptor` | The descriptor to change. Null logs a warning and returns null. |
| `allowedQuestTitles` | Quest titles that may still start, e.g. "PropHunt"; see [`GamemodeDescriptor.AllowedQuestTitles`](../gamemodedescriptor/#allowedquesttitles). None keeps the titles already set. |

**Returns** The same descriptor, so the call fits inside [`API.Register`](../api/#register).

All notable changes to Side Hustle are documented here. This project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [3.3.0] - 2026-10-31

## [2.0.0] - 2026-07-26

Play modded multiplayer with anyone - mods sync themselves, join a gamemode you don't even have installed, and chat in-game.

### Added
- **Join a gamemode you don't have installed.** A public gamemode lobby now advertises the exact mod files a joiner
  needs (the gamemode's own mod, whatever its policy requires, with version and hash). In the Side Hustle menu such a
  lobby is no longer a dead "not installed" entry: pick "Join (installs the mods)", confirm, and Side Hustle fetches
  them from Thunderstore - anything it can't fetch gets the same checklist with a direct Nexus link - installs them
  into a session profile, restarts and drops you into that lobby. Your own mods stay exactly where they are.
- **Mod Profiles - an in-game mod manager.** A new "Mod Profiles" entry on the main menu lets you keep separate,
  isolated sets of mods and switch between them (the game restarts into the one you pick). Build a profile from
  your installed mods, or browse and install straight from Thunderstore - dependencies included. Your real Mods
  folder is never touched, so external managers like r2modman keep working exactly as before. Side Hustle picks
  which profile to load at startup (a short prompt you can skip); pick "Full mod set" any time to go back to
  everything.
- **Vanilla Co-op with mod sync.** Host your own normal savegame as a public lobby (from the menu, or when you
  click Continue), and anyone can find it and join. When they do, Side Hustle compares their mods to yours and, if
  they differ, offers to set up a matching profile automatically - download from Thunderstore, restart, and drop
  straight back into your game. Mods that can't be fetched automatically get a simple checklist with a download
  link and an "open folder" button. You choose per-session whether to require synced mods.
- **Sync your mod settings too (optional).** As a host you can pick which mods' settings to apply to everyone who
  joins - it only affects the session, never their real settings, and anything that looks like a secret is left
  off by default.
- **Side Hustle Messenger.** A new phone app for chatting with the other players in your lobby - a shared lobby
  chat and private one-to-one conversations, with unread badges and native message notifications.
- **GitHub mods download themselves too.** Mods whose download link points at a GitHub repository are fetched
  automatically from the repo's releases (hash-verified against the host's exact file), so fewer mods end up on
  the manual checklist.
- **Hands-free manual installs.** For mods that still need a browser download (e.g. Nexus), the checklist now
  watches your Downloads folder (and Vortex's download folder, if you use Vortex): click the link, download the
  file, done - Side Hustle spots it, verifies it and installs it on its own. An "Open next link" button walks you
  through the list, each mod ticks off live with a toast, and if you grab the wrong version the row tells you
  exactly which one the host runs. Files with the right content are also reused across rejoins.
- **See what's being played right now.** The Side Hustle menu now also lists gamemodes you do NOT have installed
  that have live public lobbies, so you can discover new things to play. Opening one shows a "Download Mod" button
  (Host and Join stay greyed out until you install the mod). You can turn this off under "Show gamemodes you don't
  have" in the settings.
- **For gamemode authors:** a gamemode can declare a `DownloadUrl` (shown as the "Download Mod" link, opened in the
  Steam overlay) and set `Advertise = false` to keep its public lobbies out of that discovery list - e.g. while a
  mode is still in development. Advertising is on by default and only ever lists public lobbies.

### Changed
- **Manual downloads land on the mod's own Nexus page.** For a mod the host could not give a download link for,
  Side Hustle now looks the name up on Nexus: when it identifies exactly one published Schedule I mod, the
  checklist button opens that mod's page directly ("Open Nexus") instead of a search results list. Ambiguous
  names ("Mod Manager") and mods that aren't on Nexus still open the search, exactly as before. The same lookup
  gives a gamemode you don't have installed a working "Find it on Nexus" button when its host advertised no link.

### Fixed
- **Gamemode sessions show up on the public lobby list.** A hosted gamemode lobby now also lists itself on the Side
  Hustle website (public lobbies only - a friends-only session stays off it), with its gamemode, player count and
  what mods a joiner would need. Only vanilla co-op lobbies did that before.
- **Your lobby name survives the "Required mods only" restart.** Hosting a gamemode that curates its mod set restarts
  the game first, and the name (and the chosen preset label) you typed on the host form was dropped in the process -
  the lobby then showed up as just your player name, in the browser and on the website.
- **Synced mods no longer arrive without their shared libraries.** A mod whose Thunderstore package ships (or depends
  on) a shared library - PropHunt needs SteamNetworkLib, for example - was installed as a lone DLL, so the joiner
  ended up with a mod that could not load and an error every frame. The sync now fetches those library packages too
  and puts them into the session profile's own `Plugins`/`UserLibs`, seeded from your global ones, so your real
  install is still never written to.

### Notes
- Side Hustle now ships a small startup helper (`SideHustle.Boot`) that it installs into your `Plugins` folder on
  first run. To fully remove Side Hustle, delete that file and the `SideHustle_Profiles` folder alongside the game.
- Downloads only ever come from Thunderstore's official CDN or a mod's own GitHub releases, and every downloaded
  file is verified against the host's manifest hash before it is used. Mods are never sent between players directly.
- Side Hustle only ever reads your Downloads and Vortex folders - nothing there is moved or deleted.

## [1.5.3] - 2026-07-08

A multiplayer-focused update - public lobbies work with anyone, plus host controls, friend invites and smoother
mod-set switching.

### Added
- **Play with anyone, not just friends.** Schedule I normally kicks a joining player who isn't on the host's Steam
  friends list a few seconds after they connect - so public sessions were effectively friends-only. While you host a
  Side Hustle gamemode that kick is lifted, so friends and non-friends alike can join your public (or
  password-protected) lobbies. Normal co-op outside Side Hustle is unaffected.
- **Kick players.** The host can remove a player from the session from the gamemode's UI (a reusable framework
  control, so any gamemode can offer it).
- **Clients can invite friends too.** The Steam friend-invite (+) button in the pause-menu lobby panel now shows for
  everyone in the lobby, not just the host, and works past four seats (with BiggerLobbies).
- **A heads-up before a "Required mods only" host restarts the game.** Instead of restarting instantly, a short
  countdown appears (Restart now / Cancel) and restarts on its own when the timer runs out - so the restart is never
  a surprise.
- **Gamemodes can default to "Required mods only".** A gamemode can ask the Host form to pre-select the isolated
  "required mods only" set (the host can still switch it), so a mode that wants everyone on an identical set gets it
  by default.

### Fixed
- **"Required mods only" re-hosting is now solid.** Hosting a gamemode with only its required mods, returning to the
  menu, then hosting again now works reliably: each launch builds a fresh isolated profile (a locked leftover can
  never block it), the gamemode list comes back on its own, and a quick re-host no longer times out.

### Changed
- **Better connection routing for public lobbies.** Public P2P connections now allow all connection routes and warm
  up Steam's relay, so a join picks the best available path instead of falling back to relay-only.
