### Added
- **Gamemode presets.** Gamemodes can now ship named presets (like "Classic Hunt") that show up as a picker at
  the top of the host setup form. Pick one and it fills in all the settings for you - you can still tweak anything
  afterwards. The form auto-selects whichever preset best fits your lobby size, a preset can suggest a player
  count, and one whose headline mechanic isn't finished yet is flagged EXPERIMENTAL so you know what you're getting.
- **Name your lobby.** The host form has a lobby name field now, and that name (plus the mode you picked) shows on
  the server-browser cards, so joiners can tell sessions apart at a glance.
- **Session-hygiene flags for gamemode authors.** A gamemode can opt into a handful of world-cleanup switches
  instead of reinventing them: skip the new-game intro and character creator, stop vanilla quests from
  auto-starting (with an allow-list for your own guide quest), block saving for the session so a throwaway world
  never overwrites a real save, keep NPCs from reacting to gunfire, and turn off vanilla player death when the
  gamemode runs its own elimination. All opt-in, all off by default.
- **A heads-up when versions don't match.** When you join a session, Side Hustle compares your build of the
  gamemode against the host's and warns you - in the log and right on the browser card - if they differ. It's the
  classic "we're all on different versions" bug, now easy to spot. It only warns; it never stops you joining.

### Changed
- **Host form polish.** Settings can be grouped under section headers, there's a new compact dropdown for
  one-of-many choices, and the settings list scrolls with a smooth mouse-wheel glide.

## [1.4.0] - 2026-06-26

### Added
- **Host configuration screen.** Hosting a multiplayer gamemode now opens a native-style setup form: pick the
  exact player count (up to the lobby cap), a public or private (friends-only) lobby with an optional password,
  and any settings the gamemode itself exposes - sliders, toggles, choices and text fields - all handed to the
  gamemode at launch.
- **Restyled server browser.** The Join screen lists open lobbies as cards (host, player count, gamemode, and a
  lock for password-protected lobbies); a locked lobby asks for the password before joining.

### Changed
- **The mod policy is now a per-session choice on the host form.** When you host a gamemode that declares which
  other mods it works with, the setup form offers "Current installed mods" (the default - keep your full set) or
  "Required mods only" (run just the gamemode's mods in an isolated profile, after a confirmation listing the
  changes). Nothing in your real Mods folder is ever renamed, moved or deleted (junctions/hardlinks, no admin
  needed), so your mod manager stays in sync. Joining a session never changes your mods - that is the host's choice.

## [1.3.0] - 2026-06-26

### Changed
- **Conflict-free mod sets are now fully non-destructive.** When a gamemode declares which other mods it works
  with, Side Hustle launches it in a temporary, isolated profile that loads only those mods - your installed mods
  are never disabled, renamed, moved or deleted, so your mod manager stays in sync and a normal launch always
  loads everything. Leaving the gamemode restarts back to your full set. The confirmation still lists exactly what
  changes before anything happens, and a "Restore my mods" entry returns you to your full set at any time.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-06-25

### Added
- **Conflict-free mod sets.** A gamemode can declare which other mods it works with (a mod policy). When you
  launch it, Side Hustle shows exactly which mods it will pause and enable, then - on your confirmation -
  launches the gamemode in its own mod set. When you leave the gamemode your normal mods are restored. A
  "Restore my mods" entry is there if you ever need to put everything back yourself.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-06-25

### Added
- **Multiplayer launch.** Multiplayer and hybrid gamemodes now show a Singleplayer / Host / Join
  choice in the menu. Hosting opens a public lobby (with a player-count picker); bigger lobbies are
  supported with BiggerLobbies.
- **Public server browser.** Browse and join open sessions for a gamemode, filtered so each gamemode
  only lists its own lobbies.
- **World gamemodes.** Gamemodes that need the actual game world get a throwaway session booted for
  them, outside your five save slots - your real saves are never created or touched.
- **Richer launch context.** Gamemodes receive the host/client role, lobby id, player count, host name
  and the host's settings when they launch.
- Play-mode badge (Singleplayer / Multiplayer / SP + MP) on each gamemode in the list, optional
  per-gamemode icons, and a recently-played ordering so your last gamemodes appear first.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-06-24

### Fixed
- The "Side Hustle" menu entry could be added more than once (showing duplicate entries) when the
  main menu re-initialised during loading. Injection is now idempotent, so exactly one entry appears.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-06-24

Initial release.

### Added
- A "Side Hustle" entry on the main menu that lists every installed gamemode mod (name,
  description, author) and launches the selected one without loading a savegame.
- Public, load-order-independent registration API (`SideHustle.API.Register` with
  `GamemodeDescriptor` / `LaunchContext`) for mods to appear as gamemodes.
- Singleplayer launch flow with a clean return to the menu (`LaunchContext.ReturnToHub`).
- Multiplayer host/join and a server browser are shown but disabled, ready for a later update.
- `Enabled` setting (MelonPreferences) to hide the menu entry without uninstalling.

pages.title: Add a gamemode
pages.description: Register your mod as a gamemode so it shows in the Side Hustle hub with its own Host, Join and Solo buttons.
pages.markdown:
Register your mod as a gamemode. It then shows as a row in the Side Hustle hub, and the player starts it from there.

**You need:** Side Hustle 3.0, a MelonLoader mod project.

## Steps

1. Reference `SideHustle.dll` from your game's `Mods` folder. Do not copy it into your output.

   ```xml
   <Reference Include="SideHustle">
     <HintPath>path\to\Schedule I\Mods\SideHustle.dll</HintPath>
     <Private>false</Private>
   </Reference>
   ```

   Your project also needs `UnityEngine.CoreModule`, because the descriptor has `Sprite` and `Texture2D` fields.

2. Copy [`SideHustleLink.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/blob/main/Examples/SideHustleLink.cs) into your project. It keeps your mod working when Side Hustle is not installed.

3. Mark Side Hustle as an optional dependency, once in any file:

   ```csharp
   [assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]
   ```

4. Put every Side Hustle type in its own class. Your `MelonMod` class must not mention one.

   ```csharp
   using SideHustle;

   internal static class Gamemode
   {
       internal static GamemodeDescriptor Build() => new GamemodeDescriptor
       {
           Id = "you.yourmode",                     // stable and unique
           DisplayName = "Your Mode",
           Description = "What your gamemode does.",
           Author = "You",
           Support = GamemodeSupport.Singleplayer,  // or Multiplayer, Hybrid
           Surface = GamemodeSurface.MenuSpace,     // MenuSpace = overlay on the menu, World = loads a world
           OnLaunchSingleplayer = Start,
           OnExitToHub = ctx => CleanUp(),
       };

       private static void Start(LaunchContext ctx) { /* build your overlay or start your mode */ }
       private static void CleanUp() { /* remove everything you built */ }
   }
   ```

   A method that names a Side Hustle type fails before its first line when `SideHustle.dll` is missing. A `try`/`catch` inside that method does not help.

5. Register from `OnInitializeMelon`:

   ```csharp
   public override void OnInitializeMelon()
   {
       SideHustleLink.TryRegister(() => Gamemode.Build(), LoggerInstance);
   }
   ```

6. Call `ctx.ReturnToHub()` when your mode ends, for example on a Back button. Side Hustle then shows the menu and the hub again.

## Add an icon

Embed a PNG as `<AssemblyName>.hub-icon.png`. The hub finds it without any code:

```xml
<EmbeddedResource Include="icon.png" LogicalName="YourMod.hub-icon.png" />
```

The hub shows this icon also while the boot gate holds your mod back and none of your code has run.
For another resource name, set `IconResource` on the descriptor. `Icon` (a `Sprite`) and `IconTex` (a `Texture2D`) win over both.

## Check it works

The log shows:

```
Gamemode registered: 'Your Mode' (you.yourmode).
```

Your row is in the hub. Click Solo, and `OnLaunchSingleplayer` runs.

![The Side Hustle hub with the "Your Mode" row selected: icon, name, author and the Host, Join and Solo buttons](/img/guides/sidehustle/hub-your-mode.webp)

A problem in the descriptor is logged with the gamemode id and the field name.

## Next

- [Add host settings](/mods/sidehustle/guides/host-settings/)
- [React to players and send messages](/mods/sidehustle/guides/sessions-and-messages/)
- [Run your gamemode in the game world](/mods/sidehustle/guides/world-gamemodes/)
- [Example gamemode](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/tree/main/Examples/ExampleGamemode)
- [API reference](/mods/sidehustle/api/)

pages.title: Add host settings
pages.description: Let the host set round time, teams or any other value on the Host form and read it on every player.
pages.markdown:
Give the host a form with your settings. Side Hustle sends the chosen values to every player, so you write no netcode.

**You need:** a registered gamemode with `Support` set to `Multiplayer` or `Hybrid`. See [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/).

## Steps

1. Add `HostSettings` to your descriptor. Each entry is one control on the Host form.

   ```csharp
   HostSettings = new[]
   {
       new SettingDescriptor
       {
           Key = "round_time", Label = "Round time", Category = "Rounds",
           Type = SettingType.Slider, Min = 60, Max = 900, Step = 30, WholeNumbers = true,
           Unit = "s", Default = "300",
       },
       new SettingDescriptor
       {
           Key = "teams", Label = "Teams", Category = "Rounds",
           Type = SettingType.Segmented, Options = new[] { "Two", "Four" }, Values = new[] { "2", "4" },
           Default = "2",
       },
       new SettingDescriptor
       {
           Key = "friendly_fire", Label = "Friendly fire", Hint = "Team mates can hurt each other.",
           Type = SettingType.Toggle, Default = "0",
       },
   },
   ```

   - `Key` is the wire format. Keep it short and never rename it. All values travel in Steam lobby data, which has a size limit.
   - The form shows a section header each time `Category` changes. Sort your settings by category.
   - Every value is a string. A toggle stores `"1"` or `"0"`. A segmented or dropdown control stores the entry of `Values`, or the label when `Values` is null.

2. Optional: add `Presets`. The host picks one, and its values fill the matching controls.

   ```csharp
   Presets = new[]
   {
       new SettingPreset
       {
           Name = "Quick round", Hint = "Short rounds, two teams.", Recommended = "Best for 2-6",
           MinPlayers = 2, MaxPlayers = 6,
           Values = new Dictionary<string, string> { ["round_time"] = "120", ["teams"] = "2" },
       },
   },
   ```

   - A preset whose `MinPlayers` to `MaxPlayers` range fits the lobby size can be selected when the form opens. `DefaultSelected = true` always selects it.
   - When the host changes a value, joiners see the mode as "Custom - Quick round". Set `Mode` to use another name.
   - `Experimental = true` adds a badge and sorts the preset to the end.
   - A key without a matching setting is ignored.

3. Read the values in your launch callbacks. Host and clients get the same values.

   ```csharp
   OnHostMultiplayer = ctx => StartRound(ctx),
   OnJoinMultiplayer = ctx => StartRound(ctx),

   static void StartRound(LaunchContext ctx)
   {
       var mp = ctx.Multiplayer;
       int roundTime = mp.GetInt("round_time", 300);
       int teams = mp.GetInt("teams", 2);
       bool friendlyFire = mp.GetBool("friendly_fire");
       string mode = mp.Mode;   // "Quick round", "Custom - Quick round" or null
   }
   ```

   `GetInt` and `GetFloat` parse with the invariant culture. `GetBool` reads `"1"` and `"true"` as true.

## Check it works

1. Click Host on your row and open the full form.
2. Your settings show under their category headers. With `Presets`, the preset picker is above them.

   ![The full Host form with a Rounds section: a Round time slider at 300 s, a Two/Four Teams choice and a Friendly fire toggle with its hint](/img/guides/sidehustle/host-form.webp)

3. Host, then join with a second instance. Log `roundTime` on both: the values are the same.

## Next

- [React to players and send messages](/mods/sidehustle/guides/sessions-and-messages/)
- [`SettingDescriptor` in the API reference](/mods/sidehustle/api/)

pages.title: Make your mod sync to other players
pages.description: Publish your mod so Side Hustle can install it on a joining player automatically and find it from a lobby.
pages.markdown:
Give your mod a download source Side Hustle can use. A player who joins a lobby without your mod then gets it installed, or gets a direct link.

**You need:** a released mod. For the gamemode fields, a registered gamemode.

## How Side Hustle finds your mod

The host lists every loaded mod with its version and SHA256 hash. For each mod it picks one source:

| Source | What the joining player gets |
|---|---|
| Thunderstore has a package with the installed version | Automatic install |
| `downloadLink` points at a GitHub repository | Automatic download from its releases |
| `downloadLink` points at Nexus, Thunderstore or doodesch.de | A checklist entry with that link |
| No usable source | Nothing. The player joins without your mod. |

Every download is checked against the host's hash. A file with a different hash is never installed.
The Thunderstore build of Side Hustle downloads no code. There, every mod is a checklist entry.

## Steps

1. Set `downloadLink`, the fifth argument of `MelonInfo`. Use an `https` link.

   ```csharp
   [assembly: MelonInfo(typeof(Core), "Your Mod", "1.2.0", "You", "https://github.com/you/YourMod")]
   ```

2. Tag each GitHub release with the version from `MelonInfo`. `v1.2.0`, `1.2.0` and `1.2.0.0` all match.

3. Attach the DLL, or a zip with the DLL, as a release asset. Side Hustle reads up to 3 `.dll` or `.zip` assets of up to 50 MB.

4. Upload the same DLL file to every store. A rebuild has a different hash, and the download fails the check.

5. Keep secrets out of setting names you want synced. The host can sync mod settings to the session. A category with an entry name that contains `token`, `secret`, `password`, `webhook`, `apikey` or `api_key` is off by default, because lobby data is public.

## For a gamemode

Set these on your `GamemodeDescriptor`:

```csharp
DownloadUrl = "https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/You/YourMode/",
Advertise = true,
```

- Players without your gamemode see its public lobbies with a "Download the mod" button. The button opens `DownloadUrl`.
- Only links to Thunderstore, Nexus, GitHub and doodesch.de open. Other links show but do not open.
- `Advertise = false` hides your lobbies from players without your gamemode. Use it while your gamemode is in development.

## Check it works

1. Open the classic host form for a vanilla co-op lobby with your mod loaded.
2. The "Mod sync" note counts your mod: "install automatically", "need a download link" or "cannot sync".

   ![The Mod sync note on the host form: "Joiners get your mod set: 9 of 11 install automatically, 2 cannot sync."](/img/guides/sidehustle/mod-sync-note.webp)

3. For a gamemode lobby, the host log shows `[mp] join mod set published: N file(s) (A auto, G github, L link, U unsourced).`
4. Join from a second instance without your mod. Your mod shows as an automatic install or as a checklist entry with your link.

   ![The Manual installs checklist: one row per mod with its version, the reason it needs a manual install, and an Open Nexus or Find online button](/img/guides/sidehustle/manual-checklist.webp)

## Next

- [Troubleshoot Side Hustle](/mods/sidehustle/guides/troubleshooting/)

pages.title: React to players and send messages
pages.description: Know when your session starts and ends, who is in it, and send your own messages between players.
pages.markdown:
Use the session events, the player list, notices and messages. Side Hustle runs the Steam lobby, so you need no netcode of your own.

**You need:** a registered gamemode. See [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/).

## Steps

1. Subscribe to the session events once, in the same class as your descriptor.

   ```csharp
   API.SessionStarted += ctx =>
   {
       if (ctx.Descriptor.Id != "you.yourmode") return;   // fires for every gamemode
       Log.Msg($"started as {ctx.Role} with {API.Players.Count} player(s)");
   };
   API.SessionEnded += id => { if (id == "you.yourmode") Log.Msg("ended"); };
   ```

   - `SessionStarted` fires after your launch callback returns. `API.CurrentSession` and `API.Players` are set by then.
   - `SessionEnded` fires once, right after `OnExitToHub`. It also fires for a failed or aborted session.
   - `ctx.Role` is `Host`, `Client` or `Singleplayer`.

2. Track players.

   ```csharp
   API.PlayerJoined += p => Log.Msg($"joined: {p}");
   API.PlayerLeft += p => Log.Msg($"left: {p}");
   ```

   - Players who are in the lobby at the start are in `API.Players`. They do not raise `PlayerJoined`.
   - The list is polled about twice a second. In a World session, `PlayerJoined` fires before the character spawns.
   - `PlayerLeft` does not fire for the remaining players when the session ends.
   - `SessionPlayer` has `SteamId`, `DisplayName`, `IsHost` and `IsLocal`.

3. Show a notice to the local player.

   ```csharp
   API.ShowNotice("Round 2 starts in 10 seconds.", 5f);
   ```

   In the world this is the game's notification popup. In the menu it is the hub's toast, with a fixed duration.

4. Send messages to the other players.

   ```csharp
   API.SendToAll("you.yourmode", "score", "red:3,blue:1");
   API.SendTo(steamId, "you.yourmode", "role", "seeker");
   ```

   - Messages go to the other players only, never to yourself.
   - Delivery is reliable. A payload is at most `API.MaxMessageBytes` bytes.
   - `false` means no session lobby or a refused message. The reason is in the log.

5. Receive messages.

   ```csharp
   API.OnMessage("you.yourmode", msg =>
   {
       if (msg.Channel == "score") ApplyScore(msg.Text);
   });
   ```

   Handlers run on the main thread. Only members of the session lobby can send to you. `SenderSteamId` comes from Steam, not from the payload.

6. Optional, host only: remove a player.

   ```csharp
   API.KickPlayer(steamId, "Too many players");
   ```

   It never kicks the host. On a client it does nothing.

All calls are safe from any thread. Calls off the main thread run on the next frame.

## Check it works

1. Host your gamemode and join with a second instance.
2. The host log shows `joined:` with the client's name.
3. Send a message from the client. The host's handler runs with the client's `SenderSteamId`.

## Run on Side Hustle 2.x too

These members need Side Hustle 3.0. On an older Side Hustle they are missing, and a call fails.
Ask for each feature by name before you use it:

```csharp
if (SideHustleLink.Has("session-events") && SideHustleLink.Has("messages"))
    SideHustleLink.TryCall(() => Gamemode.Subscribe(), "lifecycle events", LoggerInstance);
```

The names are the constants on `ApiFeatures`, for example `players`, `notices` and `messages`.

## Next

- [Run your gamemode in the game world](/mods/sidehustle/guides/world-gamemodes/)
- [`API` in the API reference](/mods/sidehustle/api/)

pages.title: Troubleshoot Side Hustle
pages.description: Find the cause and fix when the hub, your gamemode row or a multiplayer join does not work.
pages.markdown:
Find your symptom below. Check `MelonLoader/Latest.log` first.

## The hub does not open in the main menu

- Side Hustle did not load. The log must show `Side Hustle <version> ready - N gamemode(s) registered so far.` If not, put `SideHustle.dll` in `Mods` and install MelonLoader and S1API.
- The hub page needs Sideload. Without a Sideload that can mount surfaces, the classic hub shows instead.
- `Enabled` is off. Set it to `true` under `[SideHustle_01_Main]` in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg`.
- You pressed Esc on the hub. The plain menu keeps a "Side Hustle" entry that opens it again.

## My gamemode is not in the list

- No `Gamemode registered: '<Name>' (<id>).` line in the log. Call `API.Register` in `OnInitializeMelon`.
- The log shows a JIT or `TypeLoadException` error from your `MelonMod` class. Move every Side Hustle type out of that class. See [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/).
- Two gamemodes use the same `Id`. The second one replaces the first. Give each gamemode its own `Id`.

## Clicking Host, Join or Solo does nothing

- The callback for that button is null. Solo needs `OnLaunchSingleplayer`. Host and Join need `OnHostMultiplayer` and `OnJoinMultiplayer`.
- Your callback throws. The exception is in the log.

## The menu does not come back after my gamemode

Call `ctx.ReturnToHub()` when your mode ends. Remove your own overlay in `OnExitToHub`.

## My icon does not show

- The resource name is wrong. The log lists the resource names your assembly has.
- Name the resource `<AssemblyName>.hub-icon.png`. Set `LogicalName` in the csproj, or the build adds the folder to the name.

## A joiner times out while the world loads

- Builds differ. Everyone must run the same build of the gamemode. Side Hustle warns on the lobby card and in the log.
- Mod sets differ. A mod that adds networked objects on one side only can stall the world sync. Host with "Required mods only" when the gamemode has a mod policy.

## A joiner never gets my mod installed

See [Make your mod sync to other players](/mods/sidehustle/guides/mod-sync/). The usual causes:

- `downloadLink` is not set, or it is not an `https` link.
- No GitHub release has a tag that matches the `MelonInfo` version.
- The released DLL is not the same file the host runs. The hash check refuses it.

## A non-friend drops out about ten seconds after joining

The game kicks players who are not on the host's friends list. Side Hustle removes this kick while you host a Side Hustle lobby.
On the host, the log shows `[mp] public-lobby access installed (non-friends may join a hosted lobby).`
Co-op that you start outside Side Hustle keeps the friends-only rule.

pages.title: Run your gamemode in the game world
pages.description: Start your gamemode in a clean scratch world, block vanilla quests and saves, and choose which mods stay loaded.
pages.markdown:
Set `Surface = GamemodeSurface.World`. Side Hustle then boots a scratch world before it calls your launch callback.

**You need:** a registered gamemode. See [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/).

The scratch world is a fresh copy of the default save on every launch. Side Hustle never touches a real save slot.

## Steps

1. Set the surface:

   ```csharp
   Surface = GamemodeSurface.World,
   ```

2. Turn on the world rules you need with a preset. Each preset only switches flags on.

   ```csharp
   WorldHygiene.CleanWorld(descriptor, "My Guide Quest");   // quests blocked except the named ones, no intro, no saving
   WorldHygiene.Arena(descriptor);                         // CleanWorld, plus no NPC reaction to gunfire and no player death
   ```

   Or set the flags yourself:

   | Flag | Effect for the session |
   |---|---|
   | `BlockVanillaQuests` | No vanilla quest starts. `AllowedQuestTitles` lists the exceptions. Matters on the host. |
   | `SkipIntro` | No intro cutscene and no character creator. |
   | `BlockSaveDuringSession` | Every vanilla save does nothing. The Save button stays visible. |
   | `SuppressNpcCombatReactions` | NPCs ignore gunfire: no panic, no police call, no wanted level. |
   | `DisableVanillaPlayerDeath` | Players cannot die from weapon damage. Damage to NPCs is unchanged. |

3. Optional: limit which other mods stay loaded with a `ModPolicy`.

   ```csharp
   Policy = new ModPolicy
   {
       RequiredMods = new[] { "S1API" },
       AllowedMods = new[] { "Hotline" },
   },
   DefaultRequiredModsOnly = true,
   ```

   - With a policy, Side Hustle restarts the game into a temporary profile that loads only the kept mods. Leaving the gamemode restarts into the full mod set.
   - The player confirms the change first. Installed mod files are never moved or deleted.
   - Names match the MelonLoader name or the DLL file name, case-insensitive.
   - Always kept: MelonLoader, S1API, Side Hustle, your own mod, the multiplayer libraries, and every dependency of a kept mod.
   - A required mod that is not installed blocks the launch with a message to install it.
   - `DefaultRequiredModsOnly` preselects "Required mods only" on the Host form. The host can change it.

## Check it works

1. Start your gamemode. The loading screen shows, then your launch callback runs in the world.
2. With `BlockSaveDuringSession`, press Save. Nothing is written.
3. End the session with `ctx.ReturnToHub()`. The menu and the hub come back.

## Next

- [Make your mod sync to other players](/mods/sidehustle/guides/mod-sync/)
- [`WorldHygiene` and `ModPolicy` in the API reference](/mods/sidehustle/api/)

pages.title: SideHustle
pages.description: A main-menu hub that lists installed gamemode mods and launches them without a savegame.
pages.markdown:
| | |
|---|---|
| Latest release | `3.3.0` |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/SideHustle/) |
| Requires | MelonLoader 0.7.3, S1API Forked 3.1.15, Sideload 1.33.1, WhatsDab 1.0.2 |
| Start here | [Add a gamemode](/mods/sidehustle/guides/getting-started/) |
| API | [Reference](/mods/sidehustle/api/) |
| Help | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/sidehustle) |

> Side Hustle adds a single entry to the Schedule I main menu that lists every installed
> "gamemode" mod and launches it straight from the menu - no savegame required. It is the
> shared entry point that gamemode mods (like an in-game tattoo editor) plug into. Built on
> [S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API).

> 🌐 **Is anyone playing right now?** Every public lobby is listed live at
> **[SideHustle.doodesch.de](https://sidehustle.doodesch.de)** - who is hosting, which gamemode, how full it is,
> and the exact mods that session runs. Check before you launch; you still join from inside the game.



![Side Hustle 3.0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/main/docs/img/header.jpg)

## What it is

Side Hustle is a **hub**, not a gamemode by itself. It opens beside the vanilla main menu, so Continue stays
one click away. Install gamemode mods that build on it and they appear in the list;
pick one and it launches immediately in its own self-contained session. Gamemodes never load or
touch a normal savegame, so they stay cleanly separated from your real playthrough.

If you installed Side Hustle as a dependency of another mod, you do not have to do anything - that
mod registers itself and shows up under the Side Hustle entry.

## New in 3.0: the hub

- **One page beside the vanilla menu.** Your last gamemode with Host again, public co-op for your own save, every
  gamemode with its actions, and a Lobbies tab, all on one screen over its own 3D scene.
- **Fewer clicks.** Host again and Host with defaults skip the form, a solo gamemode starts with one click, and
  after a session the hub opens on that gamemode for a rematch.
- **One lobby board** for every gamemode and vanilla co-op: search, filters, seats and what happens before you join.
- **A live status for every launch**: each step from lobby found to loading the world, with Cancel and the reason
  when something fails.

## Features

- **Every gamemode on one page.** The hub beside the main menu lists all installed gamemode mods with their
  name, description, author and a Singleplayer / Multiplayer badge.
- **No savegame.** Gamemodes launch in their own session and never load or alter your saves.
- **Singleplayer, host or join.** Singleplayer gamemodes launch with one click; multiplayer gamemodes carry
  Host and Join right on their row.
- **Configure before you host.** Hosting opens a native-style setup form: set the exact player count (up to the
  lobby cap), choose a public or private (friends-only) lobby with an optional password, and adjust any settings
  the gamemode exposes (sliders, toggles, choices, text) - all handed to the gamemode when it starts.
- **Lobby browser.** Find and join open lobbies for a gamemode, shown as cards with the host, player count and a
  lock for password-protected lobbies. Search by name, sort, and hide full, locked or other-version lobbies; the
  list refreshes itself every few seconds. Bigger lobbies (well past the vanilla 4 players) come built in - no extra
  lobby mod needed.
- **The host form remembers.** Player count, visibility, lobby name and Discord invite come back the next time you
  host, per gamemode and for vanilla co-op. "Host again" skips the form. Passwords are never stored.
- **Discord invite.** A host can put a Discord invite on the lobby; guests see a Discord button on the lobby card
  and in the Lobby app on the phone.
- **Play with anyone, not just friends.** Schedule I normally kicks joiners who aren't on the host's Steam friends
  list. While you host a Side Hustle gamemode that kick is lifted, so anyone can join your public or
  password-protected lobbies. Normal co-op outside Side Hustle is unaffected.
- **Custom display name.** Each gamemode has its own "Your name" field on its Host / Join screen. Fill it in and
  other players see that name - the in-game nametag over your character, scoreboards and the server browser -
  instead of your Steam name. A privacy option for public matches, remembered per gamemode.
- **Discover gamemodes.** The menu also lists released gamemodes you don't have installed, and any gamemode with a
  live public lobby right now, with a "Download Mod" button or a one-click install into a mod profile. Toggle it off
  in the settings; gamemode authors can opt their gamemode out of being advertised.
- **No dead ends.** Every download, search and wait has a Cancel or a Try again. If a session cannot start, the hub
  says why.
- **Host controls + friend invites.** The host can kick a player from the session, and every lobby member - not just
  the host - can invite Steam friends from the pause-menu panel.
- **World gamemodes.** Gamemodes that need the actual game world get a throwaway session booted for them,
  outside your save slots, so your real saves are never touched.
- **Conflict-free mod sets (optional, the host's choice).** A gamemode can declare which other mods it works with.
  When you host it, the setup form lets you keep your full set ("Current installed mods", the default) or run only
  the gamemode's mods ("Required mods only") in a temporary, isolated profile - after a confirmation that lists
  exactly what changes. Nothing in your real Mods folder is ever disabled, renamed, moved or deleted (it uses
  junctions/hardlinks, no admin needed), so your mod manager stays in sync; leaving the gamemode restarts back to
  your full set, and a normal launch always loads everything.
- **Load-order independent API.** Gamemode mods register themselves whether they load before or after
  Side Hustle.
- **Stays out of the way.** A single toggle hides the entry without uninstalling.

## New in 2.0: Profiles and Sync

- **Join a gamemode you don't have installed.** A public gamemode lobby lists the mod files a joiner needs. Pick
  "Join (installs the mods)", choose a session, and Side Hustle installs the gamemode (Thunderstore automatically,
  anything else via the checklist with a direct Nexus link), restarts and joins that lobby. Your own mods stay put.
- **Mod Profiles (in-game mod manager).** A separate "Mod Profiles" main-menu entry keeps isolated sets of mods you
  can switch between (the game restarts into the one you pick). Build a profile from your installed mods or browse
  and install straight from Thunderstore with dependencies resolved. Your real Mods folder is never managed, so
  external managers keep working. A short startup prompt lets you pick the profile to load (or the full set).
- **Vanilla Co-op with mod sync.** Host your own savegame as a public lobby (from the menu, or when you click
  Continue). When someone joins, Side Hustle compares mods and offers to set up a matching profile automatically -
  download from Thunderstore or a mod's GitHub releases, restart, rejoin - so you can play modded co-op with anyone
  without hand-matching mod lists. Mods that still need a browser download (e.g. Nexus) get a guided checklist:
  open the link, download the file, and Side Hustle picks it up from your Downloads folder (or Vortex's), verifies
  it and installs it on its own. Optionally require synced clients. Downloads only ever come from Thunderstore's
  CDN or GitHub releases, every file is hash-verified, and mods are never sent between players directly.
  **The build published on Thunderstore downloads nothing** (`-p:StoreBuild=thunderstore`), because Thunderstore
  does not allow a package to fetch executable code - not from GitHub and not from Thunderstore either. There,
  every mod takes the checklist route, and "Add from Thunderstore" is absent from Mod Profiles; the package
  index and mod icons are still fetched, being JSON and PNGs. The GitHub and Nexus builds are unchanged.
- **Lobby browser on the web** - see every open public lobby at [SideHustle.doodesch.de](https://sidehustle.doodesch.de) without starting the game.
- **Sync mod settings (optional).** A host can apply chosen mods' settings to everyone in the session only, never
  touching their real settings; anything that looks like a secret is off by default.
- **Lobby chat on the phone.** Side Hustle carried its own messenger until 2.1; that app is now
  [WhatsDab](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-WhatsDab), a mod of its own and a requirement of this
  one. Same idea, more of it: group and one-to-one threads, unread badges, notifications, and both orientations.
  Nothing to set up - install and it is on the phone.

## Screenshots

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Play tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/main/docs/img/play.jpg) | ![Lobby board](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/main/docs/img/lobbies.jpg) |
| ![Host form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/main/docs/img/host.jpg) | ![Joining](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/main/docs/img/join.jpg) |

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


| Component | Version / Source |
|-----------|------------------|
| Schedule I | IL2CPP (current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+` |
| S1API | [ifBars/S1API_Forked](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ifBars/S1API_Forked/) `3.1.15+` |
| [Sideload](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload) | `1.33.1+` - draws the hub |
| [WhatsDab](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-WhatsDab) | `1.0.2+` - the lobby chat app, pulled in as a dependency |


</details>

<details><summary>Installation</summary>


### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

Install with a mod manager (r2modman / Gale) from the Schedule I community; the dependencies
(MelonLoader, S1API) are pulled in automatically.

### Manual

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **S1API** (its DLLs go in `Mods/` and `Plugins/` per its own instructions).
3. Drop **`SideHustle.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.
4. Install one or more gamemode mods that use Side Hustle.


</details>

## Configuration

Open the **Settings** tab in the hub to change these in game. They are stored in
`UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `SideHustle_01_Main`.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `true` | Show the Side Hustle menu entry. Off hides it without uninstalling (only in the cfg). |
| `ShowUninstalledGamemodes` | `true` | Also list gamemodes you don't have installed. |
| `AskHostOnContinue` | `true` | Clicking Continue or a save slot offers to open it as a public lobby. |
| `AcceptStrangerMessages` | `true` | Anyone looking at your public lobby can send you a short message. |
| `MenuStatePanel` | `true` | Info column on the right of the main menu (needs Sideload 1.13.0+). |
| `JoinChatPanel` | `true` | Chat column on the screens you pass through while joining. |
| `DeferModsUntilLobby` | `false` | Load only Side Hustle and Sideload at startup; the rest loads when you host or join. Takes effect after a restart. |
| `AlwaysLoadMods` | `""` | File names that load at startup even with `DeferModsUntilLobby` on, comma-separated. |

## For mod authors

Make your mod show up as a gamemode in a few lines. Reference `SideHustle.dll`, declare it as an
optional dependency so your mod still loads if Side Hustle is absent, and register from your
`OnInitializeMelon`:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]

SideHustle.API.Register(new GamemodeDescriptor
{
    Id = "you.yourmode",                 // stable, unique
    DisplayName = "Your Mode",
    Description = "What your gamemode does.",
    Author = "You",
    Support = GamemodeSupport.Singleplayer,   // or Multiplayer / Hybrid
    Surface = GamemodeSurface.MenuSpace,      // overlay on the menu (no save), or World
    OnLaunchSingleplayer = ctx => { /* start your gamemode */ },
    OnExitToHub = ctx => { /* clean up when the player backs out */ }
});
```

For a multiplayer gamemode set `Support` to `Multiplayer` or `Hybrid` and add `OnHostMultiplayer` /
`OnJoinMultiplayer`. Side Hustle creates and tracks the lobby and (for `World` gamemodes) boots the
session, then hands you a `LaunchContext` with the role (`Host`, `Client` or `Singleplayer`), lobby id,
player count and the host's settings. Re-registering your own `Id` is safe; `Register` logs every problem
it finds in a descriptor. Call `ctx.ReturnToHub()` from your gamemode when it finishes to return to the menu.

Since API version 3 (`API.ApiVersion`, `API.Has(...)`) a gamemode can also:

- listen to `SessionStarted` / `SessionEnded` and `PlayerJoined` / `PlayerLeft`, and read `API.Players`;
- show a short message on screen with `API.ShowNotice`;
- send its own messages to the other players with `API.SendToAll` / `API.SendTo` and receive them with
  `API.OnMessage`, without its own networking code.

`OnExitToHub` runs exactly once per session, also when Side Hustle aborts a session that failed to start.
`Examples/SideHustleLink.cs` is a copy-in file that keeps Side Hustle optional, and `Examples/ExampleGamemode`
is a complete gamemode to start from. The full reference is on the
[docs site](https://docs.doodesch.de/mods/sidehustle/).

<details><summary>Compatibility</summary>


- IL2CPP build only (current Steam public branch).
- Works alongside any other MelonLoader/S1API mod. Side Hustle only adds a main-menu entry and the
  registration API; it does not touch gameplay or saves.


</details>

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


- **DooDesch** - mod author.
- **[ifBars/S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API)** - the modding API this is built on.


</details>

pages.title: AppHandle
pages.description: Handle to a registered app: the two-way channel between your C# and the app's JavaScript.
pages.markdown: ```csharp public sealed class AppHandle ``` Namespace `Sideload.Api` Handle to a registered app: the two-way channel between your C# and the app's JavaScript. Kept deliberately thin; every method stays a no-op when Sideload is absent. Strings cross the boundary in both directions. Send JSON for anything structured. Every call is queued until Sideload binds, except [`Icon`](#icon) and [`Show`](#show). **Example** ```csharp AppHandle app = Apps.Register("mystash", "MyMod.Assets.mystash", "Stash") .Orientation("landscape", "portrait") .OnCall("items.list", _ => string.Join("\n", Items)); // Later, when the game changes something the page did not ask for: app.Emit("items.changed", Items.Count.ToString()); app.Badge(Items.Count); if (!app.IsOnScreen) app.Notify("Stash", "New item"); ``` ## Properties ### Id ```csharp public string Id { get; } ``` The id this app was registered under. ### IsOnScreen ```csharp public bool IsOnScreen { get; } ``` Whether this app is the one the phone is showing right now. Ask before interrupting: an event the player is already watching happen does not deserve a notification, and the same event with the phone in their pocket does. False when Sideload is absent or the app is not on a phone yet. ```csharp if (!app.IsOnScreen) app.Notify(sender, text); ``` ### IsOpen ```csharp public bool IsOpen { get; } ``` Added in `1.1.0` Whether this app is the one the phone has open - true even with the phone in the player's pocket. For "can they actually see it", use [`IsOnScreen`](#isonscreen). ### CanOpenProgrammatically ```csharp public static bool CanOpenProgrammatically { get; } ``` Added in `1.1.0` Whether the installed Sideload understands [`NoIcon`](#noicon) and [`Open`](#open). False against an older host, where both are silent no-ops. A mod that provides its own entry point must check this before registering anything: on an older host it would hide nothing, open nothing, and leave the player with apps they cannot reach. Refuse to set up and say which version is needed - that is a fixable message, an unreachable app is not. ```csharp if (!AppHandle.CanOpenProgrammatically) { Log.Error("needs Sideload 1.1.0 or newer"); return; } ``` ### CanClaimKeys ```csharp public static bool CanClaimKeys { get; } ``` Added in `1.10.0` Whether the installed Sideload can hand an app a key. False against anything older than 1.10.0, where [`OnKey`](#onkey) is a silent no-op. Worth checking only when the key is the ONLY way into your app - pair it with [`NoIcon`](#noicon) and a host that ignores both leaves the player with an app they can neither see nor reach. ### CanEditLive ```csharp public static bool CanEditLive { get; } ``` Added in `1.35.0` Whether the installed Sideload understands [`Reload`](#reload) and [`Unregister`](#unregister), and puts an app registered while the game runs on the phone at once. False against an older host, where an app registered after the home screen was built waits for the next scene load. ## Methods ### OnCall ```csharp public AppHandle OnCall(string name, Func handler) ``` Answer `s1.call("", arg)` from this app's page. The handler runs on the Unity main thread in the same frame as the call, so it may touch game state directly; whatever it returns is the call's value. Strings cross the boundary - send JSON for anything structured. ```csharp app.OnCall("chat.threads", _ => Json.Of(Chat.Threads)); app.OnCall("chat.send", text => { Chat.Send(text); return "ok"; }); ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `name` | The name the page passes to `s1.call`, e.g. "chat.send". Compared case-insensitively. Null or blank registers nothing. The same name again replaces the handler. | | `handler` | Gets the page's argument, or an empty string when it passed none. Its return value is what `s1.call` returns; null returns an empty string. An exception is logged and the page gets an empty string. | ### Emit ```csharp public void Emit(string name, string payload = "") ``` Push an event at this app's page, where `s1.on("", fn)` is waiting for it. Use it when the game changes something the page did not ask for - a message arriving, a timer expiring. | Parameter | | |---|---| | `name` | The name the page listens on with `s1.on`, e.g. "chat.message". Compared case-insensitively. Null or blank sends nothing. | | `payload` | The string the page's listener receives, e.g. JSON. Null sends an empty string. | ### AllowHost ```csharp public AppHandle AllowHost(string host) ``` Let this app's page reach one host with `fetch`. Without at least one of these the page reaches nothing: the allowlist starts empty and only the app's own mod can add to it, so a web bundle edited in the Mods folder can never talk to somewhere you did not name here. Give a bare host name. `*.example.com` covers any single label under it, but not `example.com` itself. Ports are ignored, and the scheme must be https unless the host is `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`. ```csharp Apps.Register("mystash", "MyMod.Assets.mystash") .AllowHost("api.example.com") .AllowHost("*.cdn.example.com"); ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `host` | A bare host name such as "api.example.com", or `*.example.com` for any single label under it. A full URL is accepted and only its host is kept. A port is ignored. | ### Orientation ```csharp public AppHandle Orientation(params string[] supported) ``` Which ways round the phone may hold this app, in preference order. The FIRST one is what the app opens in; naming a second is what lets the player turn it, with the rotate keys the game already binds. Say nothing and the app is landscape only, which is the only safe reading of silence - an app that never styled portrait must not be turned into it. Both are worth styling. Sideload evaluates `@media (orientation: portrait|landscape)` against the real viewport shape, so one stylesheet covers both without any script. The player's choice is remembered per app; you do not have to store it. ```csharp .Orientation("landscape") // landscape only, the phone never turns .Orientation("portrait") // portrait only .Orientation("landscape", "portrait") // both, opens landscape .Orientation("portrait", "landscape") // both, opens portrait ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `supported` | "landscape", "portrait" or both, in preference order. Case-insensitive. Any other value is logged as a warning and ignored. Nothing recognisable keeps the previous setting, landscape only by default. | ### Badge ```csharp public AppHandle Badge(int count) ``` The unread count on this app's home-screen icon - the same red badge the vanilla apps use. Zero clears it. Counts above 99 read as "99+". Set it whenever your own count changes, not on a timer: the value is remembered across a phone rebuild, so setting it once is enough and setting it again is cheap. ```csharp app.Badge(unreadMessages); ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `count` | The unread count. 0 clears the badge. A negative value counts as 0. | ### Notify ```csharp public AppHandle Notify( string title, string subtitle = "", float seconds = 0f) ``` Added in `1.4.0` Raise one of the game's own phone notifications - the slide-in the vanilla apps use, carrying this app's icon. Nothing happens if the app is not on a phone yet. This interrupts whatever the player is doing, so spend it on what they would want to be interrupted for. A count that can wait belongs in [`Badge`](#badge). ```csharp app.Notify("Jessi Waters", "on my way"); ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `title` | The headline, e.g. a sender name like "Jessi Waters". Null counts as empty. | | `subtitle` | The line under it, e.g. "on my way". Empty by default. | | `seconds` | How long it stays up. Leave it at zero for Sideload's own timing (9 seconds), which suits a headline plus a sentence. Raise it for something the player has to act on, lower it for a passing remark. Clamped to between 2 and 30 seconds - the slide-in cannot be dismissed, so an app does not get to hold the corner of the screen. Zero or below means Sideload's own timing. Ignored, without failing, on a Sideload too old to have it. | ### Image ```csharp public AppHandle Image(string name, byte[] png) ``` Hand a picture your mod produced at runtime to the page, which draws it with ``. Null or empty bytes remove it, which is how you say "there is no picture for this one" and let the page fall back to whatever it draws without one. PNG bytes rather than a texture, because this file references no Unity type and is not going to start. Supplying the same name again replaces the picture. ```csharp app.Image("avatar/" + steamId, pngBytes); ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `name` | The name after `s1://` in the page, e.g. "avatar/76561198". Trimmed. Null or blank does nothing. | | `png` | PNG file bytes. Null or empty removes the picture. | ### Icon ```csharp public AppHandle Icon(bool visible) ``` Added in `1.6.0` Show or hide this app's home-screen icon while the game is running. For an app whose way in is a key rather than a square, but only sometimes: hash puts an icon there exactly while the game's console is switched on, because that is the only time it can run anything, and that setting is a live toggle. Safe to call with the same value repeatedly. Unlike [`NoIcon`](#noicon) this is NOT queued until Sideload binds. A caller polling a condition would otherwise pile up one queued call per check against a host that never arrives; an unbound host simply ignores it, which is the right answer for a decision that is re-stated anyway. | Parameter | | |---|---| | `visible` | True shows the icon, false hides it. | ### NoIcon ```csharp public AppHandle NoIcon() ``` Added in `1.1.0` Give this app no home-screen icon. For an app whose way in already exists somewhere else - a vanilla icon your mod has taken over, a world object, another app handing off. With no icon, [`Open`](#open) is the ONLY way in: call it from wherever your entry point is, or the app is unreachable. Check [`CanOpenProgrammatically`](#canopenprogrammatically) first - against an older Sideload this is a no-op and the app would get an icon you did not plan for. ```csharp Apps.Register("reflash-messages", "Reflash.Assets.reflash-messages", "Messages").NoIcon(); ``` ### Open ```csharp public AppHandle Open() ``` Added in `1.1.0` Open this app as if the player had pressed its icon: whatever else is open closes first, and the phone turns to this app's orientation. Does nothing while the app is not on a phone - before the home screen exists there is nothing to open. ```csharp if (playerPressedTheHijackedIcon) app.Open(); ``` ### Close ```csharp public AppHandle Close() ``` Added in `1.1.0` Close this app, returning the phone to its home screen. Does nothing if it is not the open one. ### Show ```csharp public bool Show() ``` Added in `1.5.0` Take the phone out AND open this app - what a key that opens an app has to mean, because [`Open`](#open) on its own opens it on a phone that is still in the player's pocket. The order matters and is why this exists rather than two calls at the call site: the page is built the first time it is opened, and a page built while its panel is hidden measures every line about ten times too short. Raising first means the very first frame is laid out against the real viewport. Returns false when the game refused the phone - paused, asleep, dead, arrested - in which case nothing was opened either. ```csharp if (consoleKeyPressed) app.Show(); ``` ### OnKey ```csharp public AppHandle OnKey(string keys, Func handler) ``` Added in `1.10.0` Ask for a key that reaches this app with the phone still in the player's pocket - the way IN, as opposed to `data-keys`, which only ever reaches a focused field in an already-open page. Spell keys the way the DOM does, several separated by spaces or commas: `Enter`, `F8`, `Ctrl+Shift+K`. Modifiers match exactly, so `Enter` does not fire for Shift+Enter. `Escape` is refused - it is the game's own exit action. **Your handler returns whether it TOOK the press.** Return false and the key goes to the next app that wants it, which is how you decline a key you cannot use right now - a chat with no lobby behind it should not open, and should not swallow the key on its way past. The argument is the key that fired, so one handler can serve several. **When two apps want the same key, the one that notified most recently gets it.** Two messengers installed together then behave the way a phone should: the key answers the conversation that is actually waiting. An app that has never notified still wins a key nobody else claimed - it simply sorts last. Sideload only reads the key where the game would let the player take their phone out anyway: never while they are typing, paused, asleep, arrested, or standing at a station, a shop or the developer console. While one of your apps is on screen it owns every key it claimed, and no other app is offered them. ```csharp app.OnKey("Enter", _ => { if (!Online) return false; return app.Show(); }); ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `keys` | One or more key declarations, separated by whitespace or commas, e.g. "Enter F8". A declaration is optional modifiers `Ctrl` (or `Control`), `Shift` and `Alt`, joined by `+` to one key name. Key names: the letters a to z, the digits 0 to 9, `F1` to `F12`, `Enter` (or `Return`), `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Insert`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` and `Space`. Case-insensitive. Punctuation keys are not accepted. A declaration that does not parse is logged as a warning and dropped; the rest still count. | | `handler` | Runs on the Unity main thread. Gets the key that fired in its canonical spelling, e.g. "Enter", "Ctrl+Shift+k" or "F8"; letters come back lower-case. Returns whether it took the press. Null gives back every key this app holds. | ### Reload ```csharp public AppHandle Reload() ``` Added in `1.35.0` Rebuild this app's page from disk, script engine included - what saving a file in `Mods//` means to someone editing it. For a tool that writes the bundle itself and wants the change on screen now, without DevTools attached. A page that was never opened is left alone: it builds from disk the first time. ### Unregister ```csharp public void Unregister() ``` Added in `1.35.0` Take this app off the phone and forget it while the game runs. For an app that only exists for a while; a mod's own apps live as long as the game and never need this. Registering the same id again brings it back, handlers included - they are kept by id. ### AllowGameWrites ```csharp public AppHandle AllowGameWrites(string scope) ``` Added in `1.35.0` Let this app's page CHANGE the game through `s1api`, for one area. Without it every `s1api` write is refused: a page is a file anyone can edit, so the permission has to come from the mod's own code, the same rule as [`AllowHost`](#allowhost). Reading needs no permission. ```csharp app.AllowGameWrites("money"); // s1api.money.change(amount) now works on this app's page ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `scope` | The area, e.g. "money". "*" allows every area, which is rarely what you mean. | ### Hide ```csharp public AppHandle Hide() ``` Added in `1.5.0` Close this app and put the phone away. The mirror of [`Show`](#show).

pages.title: Apps
pages.description: The Sideload framework's modder API.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public static class Apps
```

Namespace `Sideload.Api`

The Sideload framework's modder API. Reference Sideload.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod. Register an app and Sideload renders your HTML/CSS/JS bundle as a real phone app - no uGUI assembly by hand, no layout arithmetic, hot-reloadable while the game runs.

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when Sideload is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so you can ship this unconditionally with no hard dependency. Check [`Available`](#available) only if you want to fall back to your own UI.

```csharp
using Sideload.Api;
Apps.Register("prophunt", "PropHunt.App", title: "PropHunt", iconLabel: "PropHunt");
```

The bundle prefix is the embedded-resource prefix of your web files inside your own assembly, so `PropHunt/App/index.html` embedded as `PropHunt.App.index.html` is reached with prefix `"PropHunt.App"`. A file at `Mods/<id>/index.html` overrides the embedded copy.

All calls MUST be made from the Unity main thread.

Ids are compared case-insensitively and trimmed. Call and event names are compared case-insensitively. A bundle path is resolved in two places, and the file on disk wins: `Mods/<id>/<path>`, then the embedded resource `<bundlePrefix>.<path with / turned into .>`. So `css/app.css` with prefix `"MyMod.Assets.mystash"` is the resource `MyMod.Assets.mystash.css.app.css`.

**Example**

The csproj embeds the web files under the prefix you pass to [`Register`](#register):

```csharp
<EmbeddedResource Include="Assets/mystash/*">
  <LogicalName>MyMod.Assets.mystash.%(Filename)%(Extension)</LogicalName>
</EmbeddedResource>
```

Then in `OnInitializeMelon`:

```csharp
Apps.Register("mystash", "MyMod.Assets.mystash", title: "Stash", iconLabel: "Stash")
    .OnCall("items.list", _ => string.Join("\n", Items))
    .OnCall("items.add", text => { Items.Add(text.Trim()); return "ok"; });
```

## Properties

### Available

```csharp
public static bool Available { get; }
```

True only when the Sideload host is installed AND bound. You rarely need this - the API is a safe no-op when absent; use it to decide whether to build a fallback UI instead.

## Methods

### Register

```csharp
public static AppHandle Register(
    string id,
    string bundlePrefix,
    string title = null,
    string iconLabel = null,
    Assembly hostAssembly = null)
```

Types: [`AppHandle`](../apphandle/)

Declare an app. It appears on the in-game phone with its own icon and renders `index.html` from your bundle. Load-order-proof: registering before Sideload has loaded is fine, the call is replayed once the host appears.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | Stable, unique id, e.g. "mystash". Also the folder name under Mods/ that overrides the embedded files. Compared case-insensitively. Registering the same id again replaces the earlier app. Null or empty registers nothing and returns a handle whose calls do nothing. |
| `bundlePrefix` | Embedded-resource prefix of your web files inside the calling assembly, e.g. "MyMod.Assets.mystash" for `MyMod.Assets.mystash.index.html`. It is the `LogicalName` prefix in your csproj. Null means no prefix. |
| `title` | App title, e.g. "Stash". Null or blank uses `id`. |
| `iconLabel` | Caption under the home-screen icon. Null or blank uses the title. |
| `hostAssembly` | The assembly holding the embedded bundle. Defaults to the caller's assembly; pass it explicitly if you wrap this call in a helper of your own. |

**Returns** The handle for the app's calls, events, badge and notifications. Every method on it chains.

pages.description: Look up every public type and member of Sideload 1.36.1.
pages.markdown:
## Use this API

Copy [`Sideload.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload/blob/v1.36.1/Sideload.Api/Sideload.cs) into your project. That one file is the whole API.

```xml
<Compile Include="path\to\Sideload.cs" />
```

Mark it optional, so your mod still loads without it:

```csharp
[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Sideload")]
```

Without Sideload every call does nothing and returns a default. Calls made before Sideload loads run once it does.

First steps: [Build your first app](/mods/sideload/guides/your-first-app/).

Source: [`Sideload.Api/Sideload.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload/blob/v1.36.1/Sideload.Api/Sideload.cs) at `v1.36.1`.

pages.title: SurfaceHandle
pages.description: Handle to a mounted surface: the same call and event channel an app has, minus everything that only makes sense on a phone.
pages.markdown: ```csharp public sealed class SurfaceHandle ``` Namespace `Sideload.Api` Added in `1.13.0` Handle to a mounted surface: the same call and event channel an app has, minus everything that only makes sense on a phone. ## Properties ### Id ```csharp public string Id { get; } ``` Added in `1.13.0` The id this surface was mounted under. ## Methods ### OnCall ```csharp public SurfaceHandle OnCall(string name, Func handler) ``` Added in `1.13.0` Answer `s1.call(name, arg)` from this surface's page. Same rules as an app's handler: it runs on the Unity main thread in the same frame, and returns a string. | Parameter | | |---|---| | `name` | The name the page passes to `s1.call`, e.g. "chat.send". Compared case-insensitively. Null or blank registers nothing. The same name again replaces the handler. | | `handler` | Gets the page's argument, or an empty string when it passed none. Its return value is what `s1.call` returns; null returns an empty string. An exception is logged and the page gets an empty string. | ### Emit ```csharp public SurfaceHandle Emit(string name, string payload = "") ``` Added in `1.13.0` Push an event at this surface's page - `s1.on(name, fn)`. Nothing happens when the surface is not mounted; the page picks the state up when it next builds. | Parameter | | |---|---| | `name` | The name the page listens on with `s1.on`, e.g. "chat.message". Compared case-insensitively. Null or blank sends nothing. | | `payload` | The string the page's listener receives, e.g. JSON. Null sends an empty string. | ### AllowHost ```csharp public SurfaceHandle AllowHost(string host) ``` Added in `1.13.0` Let this surface's page reach one host with `fetch`. The allowlist starts empty. | Parameter | | |---|---| | `host` | A bare host name such as "api.example.com", or `*.example.com` for any single label under it. A full URL is accepted and only its host is kept. A port is ignored. | ### Image ```csharp public SurfaceHandle Image(string name, byte[] png) ``` Added in `1.32.0` Publish a picture this surface's page can draw with ``, exactly as an app does. Null or empty bytes remove it. It was missing, and the store never cared: pictures are held by (id, name) and nothing asks whether the id belongs to an app or a surface. So a surface could always have them - it just had no supported way to say so, and the one mod that needed it reached past this file into the internals because it compiles the shim in as source. A mod that references the DLL could not have done that at all. PNG bytes rather than a texture, for the reason the whole file gives: nothing here references a Unity type and nothing here is going to start. ```csharp surface.Image("icon/" + itemId, pngBytes); ``` | Parameter | | |---|---| | `name` | The name after `s1://` in the page, e.g. "avatar/76561198". Trimmed. Null or blank does nothing. | | `png` | PNG file bytes. Null or empty removes the picture. | ### Unmount ```csharp public void Unmount() ``` Added in `1.13.0` Take this surface down.

pages.title: Surfaces
pages.description: HTML somewhere other than the phone: a column in the main menu, a panel on a machine, a board on a wall.
pages.markdown:
```csharp
public static class Surfaces
```

Namespace `Sideload.Api`

Added in `1.13.0`

HTML somewhere other than the phone: a column in the main menu, a panel on a machine, a board on a wall.

The renderer never cared about the phone - it draws into any RectTransform - so a surface is the same engine, the same CSS subset and the same `s1.call` / `s1.on` channel, only mounted somewhere else. What it does not have is everything that belongs to the phone: no home-screen icon, no orientation the player can turn, no badge, no notification.

```csharp
Surfaces.Mount(myPanelRectTransform, "sidehustle-menu", "SideHustle.Assets.menu")
        .OnCall("menu.state", _ => StateJson());
```

Needs Sideload 1.13.0. Against anything older [`Mount`](#mount) answers a handle whose calls are no-ops and [`Available`](#available) is false, so a mod ships this without a hard version pin and keeps its own UI as the fallback.

**Example**

A panel survives no scene reload, so mount again whenever it is gone:

```csharp
if (Surfaces.Available && !Surfaces.IsMounted("sidehustle-menu"))
    Surfaces.Mount(myPanelRectTransform, "sidehustle-menu", "SideHustle.Assets.menu");
```

## Properties

### Available

```csharp
public static bool Available { get; }
```

Added in `1.13.0`

Whether the installed Sideload can render outside the phone at all.

## Methods

### Mount

```csharp
public static SurfaceHandle Mount(
    object hostRect,
    string id,
    string bundlePrefix,
    float designShortSide = 0f,
    Assembly hostAssembly = null)
```

Types: [`SurfaceHandle`](../surfacehandle/)

Added in `1.13.0`

Render a bundle into a panel of your own.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `hostRect` | Your `UnityEngine.RectTransform`. Typed as object only so this file stays compilable in a mod with no Unity reference; pass the RectTransform straight in. |
| `id` | Stable id, unique across apps AND surfaces - they share one namespace, so a surface cannot take an app's `s1.call` handlers. Also the folder under Mods/ that overrides the bundle. E.g. "sidehustle-menu". Compared case-insensitively and trimmed. Mounting the same id again replaces the old surface. Null or empty mounts nothing. |
| `bundlePrefix` | Embedded-resource prefix of the web files inside the calling assembly, e.g. "SideHustle.Assets.menu". Null means no prefix. |
| `designShortSide` | What the panel's short side is worth in CSS pixels. 0 (the default) maps one CSS pixel to one device unit, which is what a panel uGUI has already laid out wants. Give a number instead to get the phone's contract: the page is written for that width and scales with the panel. The phone uses 400. |
| `hostAssembly` | The assembly holding the bundle. Defaults to the caller's. |

**Returns** The handle for the surface's calls and events. It is returned even when nothing was mounted; check [`IsMounted`](#ismounted) to know.

### Unmount

```csharp
public static void Unmount(string id)
```

Added in `1.13.0`

Take a surface down. Safe for an id that was never mounted.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | The id passed to [`Mount`](#mount). Compared case-insensitively. |

### IsMounted

```csharp
public static bool IsMounted(string id)
```

Added in `1.13.0`

Whether a surface under this id is on screen. False once its panel is destroyed - a scene reload does that - so this is the check to remount on.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `id` | The id passed to [`Mount`](#mount). Compared case-insensitively. |

pages.title: Sideload changelog
pages.description: Every released version of Sideload and what changed in it.
pages.markdown:
All notable changes to Sideload are documented here. This project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). ## [Unreleased] ## [1.36.1] - 2026-10-31 ### Fixed - A surface mounted with `designShortSide` redraws when its rect changes size with the same aspect ratio. The page used to stay at the old scale and overflow the rect. ## [1.36.0] - 2026-10-29 ### Added - `` drags by its thumb and jumps on a track click: `input` per step, `change` on release. `accent-color` and `::-webkit-slider-thumb` style it. - `` opens a picker with a colour field, a hue strip and a hex field. Value is `#rrggbb`, `change` fires when it closes. - `` text and placeholder sit on the vertical middle of the field instead of its top edge. - A `transform` set from script lands where it says after another app has built. It used to add onto the box's previous translate. ### Changed - Phone app pages build while the loading screen is up. The first open of an app no longer stalls. ## [1.33.5] - 2026-10-16 ### Fixed - `box-shadow` no longer flickers between soft and hard edges from frame to frame on a page that does not change. ## [1.33.4] - 2026-10-16 ### Fixed - `opacity` fades the box with its text and children, as in a browser. It used to fade only the box's own fill and picture. - Text in a column box with `justify-content: center` sits in the middle; it stayed on the top edge. - `font-style: italic` at weight 400 and 300 draws slanted instead of upright. - Text in a box shorter than its line plus a thick border no longer disappears. - Borders keep their width and colour on a scaled page; a 1.8px frame came out 2.9px and tinted yellow. ### Added - `scrollbar-color` sets the scrollbar thumb colour. `overflow-y: scroll` keeps the bar visible while the content fits. ### Changed - `overflow: hidden` clips content inside the border instead of on top of it. ## [1.33.3] - 2026-10-16 ### Fixed - Dark fills on the phone show their declared colour instead of a washed-out grey (`#0b0c0e` arrived as `#3b3d42`). Drop any CSS you darkened to make up for it. ## [1.33.2] - 2026-10-16 ### Fixed - A text field the page removes no longer stays on screen as an empty bar until the next rebuild. ## [1.33.1] - 2026-10-15 ### Fixed - `setAttribute(name, '')` now adds the attribute. React switches `disabled`, `checked` and `hidden` on that way, so a disabled button was still pressable and `disabled:` styles never showed. ## [1.33.0] - 2026-09-01 ### Fixed - Escape and right-click keep working after you return to the menu and load back in. Every app left a dead listener behind on each load, one per app per cycle. - A fresh install no longer warns that AngleSharp, Jint and Esprima are missing. They are inside `Sideload.dll` and always were; MelonLoader was looking for them on disk. ### For mod authors - `sideloadgamma` prints per mounted page: the canvas and its render mode, its camera, whether that camera has a target texture, and what `WantsLinearColors()` returned. Debug builds. ## [1.32.0] - 2026-08-19 ### Added - A scrolling box has a bar down its right edge now, so a long list shows where you are in it. `scrollbar-width: none` takes it away. - A surface can publish pictures for its page, the same way an app does: `surface.Image(name, png)`, drawn with ``. ## [1.31.1] - 2026-08-16 ### Fixed - The stylesheet report no longer flags `display: inline-flex` as lost. It maps onto flex exactly, keeping the shrink behaviour, so only the report was wrong. ## [1.31.0] - 2026-08-10 ### Added - Changing only the text of a box no longer rebuilds the page. A clock that ticks once a second rebuilt every element on screen with it. ### Fixed - A scrolling area inside a plain `
` keeps its height. It was squeezed to nothing, so the one part of a page meant to scroll was the part that disappeared. - A box only shrinks its children if it says `display: flex`, `flex-direction`, `flex-wrap` or `flex-flow`. Anything else overflows, as a block does. - `transform` turns a box around its `transform-origin` without dragging its contents along. A button growing on hover left its own label behind. - `:hover` survives a page rebuild. A page that redraws on a timer flickered once a second, and a text field lost its hover for good. ## [1.30.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - Elements look like they do in a browser before your CSS says anything: heading sizes, paragraph spacing, list indent, bold, italic, monospace. - Only with ``, and every rule you write beats it. - Lists have bullets and numbers. `list-style-type` picks between `disc`, `circle`, `square`, `decimal` and `none`, and `start` on an `
    ` counts from there. - `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` reach the same store as `s1.storage`, so a library that calls `getItem` works. ## [1.29.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - `outline` draws a focus ring, outside the box and without moving it. Width, colour, offset and `auto` are all read. - `vertical-align` puts an icon or a badge on the line it sits in: `top`, `middle`, `bottom` and `baseline`. - `touch-action: none` says a box handles its own drag, so a map pans instead of scrolling the page around it. - `tab-size` fills a tab to the next stop in preserved text, counted from the line start. Default 8, as in CSS. - `FormData` exists, including `new FormData(form)`, iteration and posting it as a `fetch` body. ### Fixed - A rounded box with a border and no background draws its border. It drew nothing at all, so an outlined chip was an empty rectangle. - A drag listener no longer takes scrolling away from the list underneath. Claim the gesture with `preventDefault()` or `touch-action: none`. - `el.value = x` no longer reports itself as typing. A field whose page wrote its value back could loop. - A page that needs longer than 250 ms to start now gets it: loading has a 5 s budget, a handler still has 250 ms. - `mousemove` fires while a page listens for it, and `createElementNS` puts the element in the namespace it names. ## [1.28.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Fixed - Boxes have their borders, corners and shadows back next to a mod that draws in the main menu. Only the fill was drawn, and no stylesheet could bring the rest back. ## [1.27.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Fixed - A styled `` inside a sentence keeps its background, padding and corners. The whole sentence used to collapse into one run of text, and a badge in the middle of it came out as coloured words. - The space before a bold or coloured word is there. "A paragraph with" and a bold "bold" were printed as "withbold", because the piece that carried the space was measured without it. ## [1.26.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - `::placeholder` styles the hint text in a field. Without a rule it stays the field's own type, faded, exactly as before. - The `lh` and `rlh` units, which is one line box tall - `min-height: 1lh` is how a stock Tailwind build sizes a one-line control. ## [1.25.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - `text-decoration` draws an underline or a strike, the `font` shorthand sets the whole type in one line, and `inherit` works on every property the cascade can carry down. - A font stack is read the way a browser reads it: `Inter, game-comic` reaches the comic face instead of falling back to the UI font on the first name it does not have. - An input's `type` is read at last: a checkbox and a radio are a box with a state, `hidden` is no box at all, and `button` draws its `value` as a label. - Clicking a checkbox flips it, clears its radio group and raises `input` and `change` - which is what React listens for, so a controlled checkbox finally moves. Clicking its label works too. - `sideloadwheel [notches] [appId]` turns the wheel over a page through the real raycast and names what took the notch. A screenshot cannot tell scrolling from cropping. Debug builds only. ### Changed - The log names only what is lost. A React and Tailwind build reported 128 dead declarations and now reports 28, and most of the difference was the report being wrong. ### Fixed - A page taller than the phone scrolls instead of drawing past it. The lower half used to be painted outside the phone, over the game world, out of reach. - A page whose script listens for the wheel still scrolls. React registers one on its root container, which took scrolling away from every React app. - A text field is as tall as a line of its own text. It used to be padding around one pixel of nothing, with the placeholder hanging out of the bottom. - A page that says `overflow-x: hidden` still scrolls downwards. It used to be cropped at the first screenful, with everything below it reachable by nothing. - `scrollToEnd()` works on a box that already had a scroll area. The position restore that follows a rebuild put it straight back where it was. ## [1.19.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - `align-items: baseline` works. It parsed and then did nothing, so a 13px name and a 12px amount in one row sat visibly off each other with no rule anywhere looking wrong. - `overflow-wrap`, `word-wrap` and `word-break` are implemented. `break-all` and `anywhere` bring back the old behaviour of cutting a long word to fit. ### Fixed - A word too long for its box hangs out of it instead of being cut in half. A stock count of 1073904864 printed as 10739048 over 64, which reads as two numbers. - A row that does not fit holds each label at its longest word instead of squeezing every box toward nothing. - An invalid `flex` value is named in the log. It used to vanish in silence, leaving the box at its default with nothing pointing at the line that caused it. ## [1.24.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - `align-content` moves the wrapped lines: `flex-end`, `center`, `space-between`, `space-around`, `space-evenly`. - `object-fit: fill` stretches the picture to its box, and `scale-down` leaves one alone that is already smaller. ### Changed - `align-content: flex-start` and `object-fit: contain` are taken in silence. Both are what the engine already did, and every use of them in the shipped apps was reported as unimplemented. ## [1.23.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Changed - The report about unusable CSS only names what is actually lost. `will-change`, `touch-action`, `user-select` and the other pure browser hints are accepted in silence. - A breakpoint wider than the phone now says so and names the screen, rather than reading as a missing feature. ### Fixed - `border-style: none` removes the border. It used to leave it drawn, and every value including `solid` was reported as doing nothing. ## [1.22.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - `line-height` reaches the text. It was read and then used only to size an empty box, so nine of the fourteen shipped apps set a line height that never appeared. - `pointer-events: none` lets the pointer through to whatever is behind. A scrim that only dims, a label over a map. Inherited, so one rule covers a whole overlay. - `text-transform` with `uppercase`, `lowercase` and `capitalize`. - `transform-origin`, in the keyword and length forms. ### Fixed - `scale` and `rotate` turn a box around its centre. They turned it around its top-left corner, which is not what any browser does and not what any page that scales was drawn against. ## [1.21.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Changed - A page that redraws is twice as fast again. The same 206-box React page went from 128 ms to 56 ms, and a state update from 116 ms to 48 ms. - The layout stopped asking for the same measurement over and over: 73600 requests per render became 20100, and the layout phase 95 ms became 19 ms. ### Fixed - A deeply nested box no longer costs exponentially more than a shallow one. One line of text eight levels down took 40963 measurements; it takes 154. ## [1.20.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - Eleven more events fire: `mousedown`, `mouseup`, `mouseover`, `mouseout`, `dblclick`, `contextmenu`, `focus`, `blur`, `focusin`, `focusout` and `change`. - `change` fires when a field gives the caret back with a different value than it took, so a page can save once instead of on every keystroke. - An event carries `clientX`, `clientY`, `button` and `detail` - which button, how many clicks, and where in the page it landed. ### Changed - A right click raises `contextmenu` instead of `click`. It still raises `back` at the document as well. - `mouseenter` and `mouseleave` do not bubble and `mouseover` and `mouseout` do, as in a browser. One rule, one place. ## [1.18.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Changed - A page that redraws is about six times faster. A 206-box page built by React went from 754 ms to 128 ms, and a state update from the same to 116 ms. - Text measurements are cached across renders. One render was asking TextMeshPro the same 599 questions 74000 times, and that was 720 of those 754 ms. - Every page build logs where its time went - `cascade / layout / paint / wire`, plus how many text measurements were taken and how many came from the cache. Turn it on with `LogPageBuilds`. ## [1.17.0] - 2026-08-09 ### Added - React runs. `createRoot(...).render(...)` draws, `onClick` fires, `useState` updates and a keyed list reorders - react-dom 18 unchanged. - A click reports the element it landed on, not the box that caught it.
