pages.description: Copy this single C# file into your mod project to call the TightBeam API.

pages.title: TightBeam
pages.description: A believable, limited-range handheld flashlight for Schedule I with a cross-mod control API.
pages.markdown:
| | |
|---|---|
| Latest release | `2.1.1` |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/TightBeam/) |
| Requires | MelonLoader 0.7.3 |
| Start here | [Control the flashlight](/mods/tightbeam/guides/modder-api/) |
| API | [Reference](/mods/tightbeam/api/) |
| Help | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/tightbeam) |

> A proper handheld flashlight for Schedule I. It upgrades the game's own flashlight - toggle it with your
> flashlight key, then hold **ALT + mouse wheel** to dial the beam from a wide near-flood to a tight,
> far-reaching throw. No map-wide floodlight, no blinding glare - just a light that feels like a flashlight.


## Features

- **A beam you can aim and shape.** Hold **ALT + mouse wheel** to slide a single Focus axis: the wide
  end is a short, broad flood right in front of you; the narrow end is a tight cone that throws far.
  Range and cone angle both follow the focus, so you get real control without ever washing out the map.
- **Velocity-sensitive focus.** Scroll slowly for fine steps; flick fast and the beam races to the
  nearest extreme. The displayed beam eases in smoothly instead of popping.
- **Fixed, sane brightness.** The beam holds a sensible brightness within a hard floor and ceiling - no
  accidental whiteout. Brightness is not a player control; mods can drive it through the API (e.g. dim it in a
  dark room).
- **Shadows and a cool-white tint by default**, so the beam is blocked by walls and reads against the
  game's warm lighting. Both are configurable (turn shadows off on low-end machines).
- **In perfect sync with the game.** TightBeam drives off the game's own flashlight state, so its on/off
  never falls out of step - your flashlight key toggles it, and it swaps the vanilla point light for its
  own clean cone.
- **Works in co-op.** Everyone else's flashlight becomes a TightBeam cone too, pointed where they are
  looking rather than sitting on their chest, with their own focus, brightness and colour. Players who
  join late see the lights that are already on - the base game never tells them about those. Capped,
  distance-culled and shadow-free by default so a full lobby stays smooth, and anyone without the mod
  still gets a cone instead of the vanilla dot.
- **Light-touch and update-resilient.** A spotlight that follows your camera - no gameplay rewired, and
  nothing written to the game's own state. In co-op your beam's shape goes on a noticeboard in the Steam
  lobby that the game itself never reads, so players without the mod are not touched by it at all. A tiny
  guard keeps ALT+scroll from cycling your hotbar.
- **Cross-mod API.** Other mods can drive the beam - dim it in a dark room, flicker it near power,
  blink it as an alert - through a drop-in `Beam` shim. See [For modders](#for-modders).

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| Flashlight key (your game bind) | Toggle the flashlight on/off |
| `ALT` + mouse wheel | Focus: wide near-flood to tight far-throw |

On/off uses your game's own flashlight key; the focus modifier is rebindable in TightBeam's config.

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


| Component | Version / Source |
|---|---|
| Schedule I | IL2CPP (current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+` |

No other dependencies - just MelonLoader. TightBeam reads the game's own flashlight state and renders its own light; no S1API. Co-op works with only some players having the mod, though everyone gets the best result if you all do.


</details>

<details><summary>Installation</summary>


### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

Install with r2modman / Gale from the Schedule I community; MelonLoader is pulled in automatically.

### Manual

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Drop **`TightBeam.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.


</details>

## Configuration

Settings live in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `[TightBeam]`. Highlights:

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `true` | Master on/off for the whole mod. |
| `FocusModifierKey` | `LeftAlt` | Hold this and scroll to change focus. |
| `DefaultFocus` | `0.5` | Starting focus. `1` = wide flood, `0` = tight throw. |
| `DefaultIntensity` | `7` | Base brightness (clamped to Min/Max). |
| `MinIntensity` / `MaxIntensity` | `1` / `20` | Hard floor / ceiling for brightness. |
| `RangeWide` / `RangeNarrow` | `8` / `34` | Beam range (m) at each focus extreme. |
| `AngleWide` / `AngleNarrow` | `66` / `16` | Cone angle (deg) at each focus extreme. |
| `ColorHex` | `#E6F2FF` | Beam colour (cool white). |
| `CastShadows` | `true` | Soft shadows (turn off on low-end machines). |

There are more fine-tuning knobs for the focus feel (sensitivity, easing, flick threshold) in the same
section if you want to dial it in. Editing the file takes effect on the next launch.

## For modders

TightBeam exposes a small cross-mod control API so your mod can drive the player's flashlight - on/off,
brightness, range, colour, plus Blink/Flicker/Pulse and scoped per-field overrides. Every call is a safe
no-op when TightBeam is not installed, so you can ship it with no hard dependency.

**Full reference: the [TightBeam Wiki](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/wiki)** - see the
[Modder API](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/wiki/Modder-API) page.

Copy the [Beam shim](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-TightBeam/wiki/The-Beam-Shim) (`TightBeam.cs`)
into your project (or reference `TightBeam.Api.dll`) and call it:

```csharp
using TightBeam.Api;

Beam.Blink(3);                                 // blink as an alert
using (var ov = Beam.BeginOverride("MyMod"))   // scoped, per-field override
{
    ov.SetIntensity(1f).SetSpotAngle(28f);     // dim + narrow while in a zone
}                                              // released -> back to the player's own settings
```

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


- **DooDesch** - mod author.


</details>

pages.title: WhatsDab changelog
pages.description: Every released version of WhatsDab and what changed in it.
pages.markdown:
All notable changes to WhatsDab are documented here. This project adheres to
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## [1.1.0] - 2026-08-07

### Added

- Press Enter and WhatsDab opens on the Everyone chat with the cursor already in the message box, so
  the next thing you type is the message. Your phone does not have to be out.
- With a conversation on screen, everything you type goes into the message box. It used to walk your
  character forward, crouch you and swap inventory slots unless you clicked the box first. Escape and
  right-click still leave, on the first press.
- Enter still belongs to the game where the game wants it: nothing happens while you are typing,
  paused, or at a station, a shop or the console, and nothing happens outside a lobby.
- Needs Sideload 1.10.0. On an older one WhatsDab works as before, just without the key.

## [1.0.5] - 2026-08-07

### Fixed

- Spamming the chat no longer freezes the game. Every message rebuilt the whole app, and a conversation was kept
  without end, so each rebuild cost more than the last. Redraws are collapsed into one per burst and a thread keeps
  its most recent 200 messages.
- The unread badge counts again. A thread you had open marked itself read whenever a message arrived, phone in your
  pocket or not - so nothing was ever unread.

## [1.0.4] - 2026-08-07

### Fixed

- One-to-one chats are back. The member list was never rebuilt, so there was nobody to write to and only the group
  thread worked. 1.0.3 fixed the same broken lobby lookup in the transport and missed a second copy of it here.
- A message cut at the 500 character limit can no longer be cut through the middle of an emoji.

## [1.0.3] - 2026-08-06

### Fixed

- Messages send again. WhatsDab read the lobby id from a game property that Schedule I stopped filling in 0.4.6,
  so every message was dropped before it left your machine - no error, no hint in the app. It now reads the id
  from where the game keeps it since that update.

## [1.0.2] - 2026-07-28

### Fixed

- A long player name no longer breaks the timestamp. The name and the time share one line, and the name could
  take all of it, so "02:55" wrapped onto two lines inside a row 58 pixels tall. The name is cut with an
  ellipsis instead and the time is never squeezed. The conversation header clamps the same way.

## [1.0.1] - 2026-07-27

### Fixed

- Opening the app could show a conversation header with nothing under it. WhatsDab reopens whichever thread you
  last read, and thread ids are the people you were in a lobby with - so the next lobby has different people and
  the stored id resolves to nothing. It now falls back to the group chat, which always exists, and the header no
  longer carries placeholder markup that made the empty pane look like a rendering failure.
- Notifications are back for the case that matters: a message arriving with the phone closed. Needs Sideload
  1.0.1, where the underlying check was fixed.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-07-27

First release, alongside Sideload 1.0.0. WhatsDab is the reference app: a complete chat client for the in
game phone, written as `index.html` / `app.css` / `app.js` and rendered by Sideload. It exists to prove that
somebody else can build with the framework without knowing its internals.

### Added

- **WhatsDab on the in game phone.** Contact list and conversation side by side in the phone's landscape
  panel, a search filter, unread counts per thread and in total, coloured avatars with an initial, day
  separators, bubbles carrying the sender's name in group threads, timestamps, a delivery tick, a typing
  indicator in both the conversation and the contact list, and a send bar.
- **Both orientations, one stylesheet.** The app declares both and the player turns the phone with the
  game's rotate keys - no button of its own. Landscape keeps the two pane split; portrait becomes push
  navigation - the list, then the conversation, with a back arrow - driven entirely by
  `@media (orientation: portrait)` in `app.css`. The choice outlives a reload.
- **Right-click goes back**, exactly as it does in the vanilla Messages app: out of a conversation first,
  and only from the list does it close WhatsDab. Two lines in `app.js`, on Sideload's cancellable `back`
  event, and the visible `<` button in the portrait header does the same thing.
- **Real messages between players**, over the Steam lobby chat the game already uses for its own control
  traffic. No FishNet, and nothing from any other mod - a lobby is a lobby, however it was opened. Messages
  are session-only and in memory; nothing is written to your save. One-to-one is filter-level privacy: the
  bytes reach every member and non-recipients drop them, which is the honest description of game chat.
- A scripted other side in development builds: a contact starts typing shortly after you send and answers
  shortly after that, so the whole app is exercisable from a single-player save.
- The whole mod as a worked example. `Core.cs` is one `Apps.Register` call plus data.
  `Chat/ChatBackend.cs` is the entire seam to the interface, five calls in and one event out, JSON strings
  both ways. `Chat/ChatModel.cs` is the only file holding sample data, so swapping in a real transport
  leaves the handlers and the whole interface untouched.
- No Unity assembly, no IL2CPP interop and no reference to Sideload itself. Only MelonLoader plus the
  single file `Sideload.Api` shim compiled in as source, so the mod ships as one DLL and does nothing rather
  than throwing when Sideload is absent.
- `preview.html` + `s1-mock.js` next to the app: the shipped `app.js` and `app.css` run in Chrome in a
  733x400 frame with a mock bridge, so layout and logic can be iterated without launching the game. Both are
  excluded from the embedded bundle.
- File overrides: anything under `Mods/whatsdab/` beats the copy embedded in the DLL, which is the same
  mechanism players use to reskin an app.

pages.title: WhatsDab
pages.description: Chat on the Schedule I phone. Threads, unread counts, group and one to one, in both orientations. Built on Sideload.
pages.markdown:
| | |
|---|---|
| Latest release | `1.1.0` |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-WhatsDab) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/WhatsDab/) |
| Requires | MelonLoader 0.7.3, Sideload 1.10.0 |
| Help | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/whatsdab) |

> Text the people in your lobby from the phone you already carry. Threads, unread counts, group chat and
> one-to-one, in both orientations.
>
> Built on [Sideload](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload), which is a hard requirement -
> the whole interface is three web files rather than hand-built panels, and the mod's own C# is one
> `Apps.Register` call plus the chat itself.



## What you get

WhatsDab appears on the in game phone as its own app, and it texts the people actually in your Steam lobby.
One thread per player plus a group thread for everyone, with a contact list and the conversation side by
side, a search filter, unread counts per thread and in total, coloured avatars, day separators, bubbles with
the sender's name in groups, timestamps, a delivery tick, a typing indicator in both the conversation and
the contact list, and a send bar.

Any lobby works - plain co-op, one a gamemode opened, one from the main menu. It rides the same Steam lobby
chat the game already uses for its own messages, so there is no server, no FishNet and no other mod in the
way. Side Hustle is not required.

The phone turns with the game's own rotate keys - the app has no button for it, and the key strip at the
bottom left says which key. Landscape keeps the two panes side by side; portrait switches to push
navigation - the list, then the conversation, with a back arrow. That is one `@media (orientation:
portrait)` block in `app.css`, not a second layout.

Right-click goes back the way it does everywhere else on the phone: out of a conversation first, and only
from the list does it close the app.

With a conversation on screen the keyboard belongs to the message box, so you can just type. Before that,
every letter was still a game binding: "hello" walked you forward, crouched you and swapped two inventory
slots unless you clicked the box first. Escape and right-click still leave, on the first press. Click the
search field and it keeps the keyboard for as long as you are searching.

Press **Enter** and WhatsDab opens on the Everyone chat with the cursor already in the message box, phone in
your pocket or not - so answering somebody is one key rather than a phone, a home screen, an app and a
click. Enter still belongs to the game where the game wants it: nothing happens while you are typing,
paused, or at a station, a shop or the console, and nothing happens outside a lobby. Sideload owns the key
and turns it off in one place (`AppKeys` in `MelonPreferences.cfg`); with a second messenger installed it
hands Enter to whichever app messaged you last.

Conversations live in memory for the session and are deliberately never written to disk: a chat log on
someone's drive is not what people expect from a lobby chat, and the name shown is whatever a player already
goes by in game, so a privacy mod that renames them is respected here too. Leave the lobby and the
conversations are gone.

A development build swaps the lobby for a scripted conversation, so the whole interface is exercisable from
a single player save without a second machine.

## Why it exists

To answer one question: can somebody else build with this framework without knowing its internals? The
project references **no** Unity assembly, **no** IL2CPP interop and **not Sideload itself** - only
MelonLoader plus the single file `Sideload.Api` shim, which finds the host by reflection. That is the whole
point. A mod author writes game logic in C# and the entire interface in web files, and ships one DLL.

The same screen exists in Side Hustle as hand built uGUI, which makes the comparison concrete:

| | uGUI (SideHustle Messenger) | Sideload (this mod) |
|---|---|---|
| Interface | 781 lines of C# | 518 lines of HTML/CSS/JS |
| Logic + data | 489 lines of C# | 475 lines of C# |
| Changing the layout | rebuild, restart the game | save the file |

What sits in those lines matters more than how many there are: the uGUI version spends 60 of them computing
a chat bubble's width, line count and height from text measurements. In CSS the same bubble is `align-self`,
`max-width` and `padding`.

## Layout of the mod

```
WhatsDab/
  Core.cs                 MelonMod: one Register call, then only data
  Chat/IChatSource.cs     where conversations come from - the seam between the two halves below
  Chat/ChatBackend.cs     the ENTIRE seam to the interface: 6 calls in, 1 event out
  Chat/DemoSource.cs      the scripted conversation, so the app works with no lobby running
  Chat/ChatModel.cs       threads, messages, unread counts, all in memory
  Chat/Json.cs            a tiny JSON writer (no parser needed on the C# side)
  Lobby/LobbySource.cs    the real one: everyone in your Steam lobby
  Lobby/ChatTransport.cs  send and receive over Steam lobby chat
  Lobby/ChatEnvelope.cs   the wire format
  Lobby/ChatStore.cs      conversations, unread counts, echo reconciliation
  Lobby/Contacts.cs       lobby members, resolved to display names
  Assets/whatsdab/        index.html, app.css, app.js, icon.png - the app itself
```

The two halves meet at `IChatSource`, and that seam has already paid off once: the lobby transport was added
under it without `ChatBackend` or a single line of the interface changing. `Chat/` compiles without any game
reference, which is what lets the headless suite run the page's JavaScript against the real handlers in a
second.

`Assets/whatsdab/` also carries `preview.html` and `s1-mock.js`. Those two are authoring tools, not part of
the app: open `preview.html` in Chrome and the shipped `app.js` and `app.css` run in a 733x400 frame without
launching the game. They are excluded from the embedded bundle rather than shipped as dead weight.

## The seam, in full

```csharp
AppHandle app = Apps.Register("whatsdab", "WhatsDab.Assets.whatsdab", title: "WhatsDab");

app.OnCall("chat.threads", _ => Threads())        // answers s1.call('chat.threads') in the page
   .OnCall("chat.thread", Conversation)
   .OnCall("chat.send", Send);

app.Emit("chat.changed", unread.ToString());      // reaches s1.on('chat.changed', fn) in the page
```

Strings both ways, JSON for anything structured. No CLR object reaches the script and no script object
reaches the mod, which is why `app.css` can be rewritten from scratch without touching `ChatBackend.cs`.

One detail worth stealing: the event is pushed from the update loop when a revision counter changes, not
from inside a handler. Emitting from inside an `OnCall` re-enters the script engine while it is still on the
stack.

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


| Component | Version / Source |
|-----------|------------------|
| Schedule I | IL2CPP (current Steam public build) |
| MelonLoader | `0.7.3+` |
| [Sideload](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload) | `1.10.0+` - the framework that renders the app, and the source of the Enter key |


</details>

<details><summary>Installation</summary>


### Recommended: a Thunderstore mod manager

Install with a mod manager (r2modman / Gale) from the Schedule I community; MelonLoader and Sideload are
pulled in automatically.

### Manual

1. Install **MelonLoader 0.7.3** for Schedule I.
2. Install **[Sideload](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload)** and its support libraries.
3. Drop **`WhatsDab.dll`** into your Schedule I `Mods/` folder.
4. Open the phone in game. WhatsDab is on the home screen.


</details>

## Configuration

None. This mod registers no MelonPreferences entries and has nothing to tune. The Enter key is Sideload's,
and `AppKeys` under `Sideload_01_Main` switches it off along with every other app key; see the
[Sideload README](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload#configuration).

## Editing the app without rebuilding

Any file under `Mods/whatsdab/` overrides the copy embedded in the DLL. Copy `index.html`, `app.css` and
`app.js` into that folder, edit them, and the changes are picked up the next time the page builds. With
Sideload's Chrome DevTools switched on, `Page.reload` in the inspector rebuilds from disk on the spot. That
is also the mechanism players use to reskin an app.

<details><summary>Compatibility</summary>


- IL2CPP build only (current Steam public branch).
- Nothing is added to the world and nothing is written to a save. What does travel between players is chat
  text, over the Steam lobby's own chat channel - so everyone in the lobby needs WhatsDab to take part, and
  players without it are unaffected.
- Without Sideload installed the shim binds nothing, every call is a no op and the mod simply does nothing
  rather than throwing.


</details>

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


- **DooDesch** - mod author.
- Built on **[Sideload](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Sideload)**.


</details>

![Yesla Assisted Driving](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Yesla/main/docs/img/header.jpg)

> An electric sedan for Schedule I that drives you where you send it.

## What it does

Jeremy at the dealership sells the **Yesla Model 3** for $60,000. It hums instead of running an engine, does
0-50 km/h in 3.4 seconds, takes paint like any other car, and is saved with the game.

**Yesla Assisted Driving.** Pick a destination in the Yesla phone app: a point on the map, one of your
properties, a customer, a dealer, a shop, or the target of your current quest or deal. Sit in the driver seat
and press **Y**. The car takes the fastest route and drives around active police checkpoints. It keeps to speed
limits, brakes early for bends, signals before it turns, stops at red lights, waits at zebra crossings and for
traffic. At the destination **Autopark** takes a free parking spot or pulls over at the kerb. Steering,
throttle or brake, or pressing **Y** again hands control back at once.

**Drive profiles** in the app: Chill, Standard and Mad Max. Mad Max ignores speed limits and red lights.
Autopark backs in by default; the app can switch it to nose in.

**First-person view** in the car with **C**: a detailed cabin, and the driving visualisation on the centre
screen.

**Driving visualisation.** **N** cycles panel, full screen and off. It shows the road lanes, the blue route,
cars, people, buildings, zebra crossings, parking spots, traffic lights with their colour, your speed, the speed
limit and the next turn.

**Phone app**, owner only:

- A map with search, your route on it, and **Send to car**.
- **Actual Super Summon** - the car drives itself to you and follows you while you walk. If you stand where no
  car can reach, it stops at the nearest road.
- **Go to target** - the empty car drives to your destination and parks there.
- **Honk and flash the lights.**
- **Lock** - nobody gets in, not even NPCs.
- **Sentry Mode** - the phone tells you when someone hits the car or stands next to it.
- **Frunk** and **Trunk** open and close the lids.
- **Paint** and **Plate** tabs change the colour and the licence plate.

The app shows your car in its own paint, turned the way your camera looks at it. The app icon shows once you
own a Yesla.

**The car itself.** Storage opens at the rear and at the nose (the frunk); both share one inventory. The
steering wheel turns with the wheels, the wipers run in the rain, and the bonnet and boot open with the
storage. Headlights switch on by themselves from 17:30 to 06:00 while the car drives, and stay on for a minute
after a night drive. Tail lamps glow at night, and the reverse light lights the ground behind the car.

**Sounds.** A recorded horn, a lock chirp, and a chime when Assisted Driving takes over and hands back. All
follow the game's volume sliders.

## Keys and settings

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| `Y` | Assisted Driving (driver seat, your own car) |
| `C` | First person |
| `N` | Visualisation |

Everything is in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `[Yesla]`:

- `EngageKey`, `ViewKey`, `VisualisationKey` - the three keys, as Unity KeyCode names.
- `DriveProfile` - `chill`, `standard` or `madmax`.
- `ParkDirection` - `auto`, `reverse` or `forward`. `auto` backs in unless the car already faces the spot.

The app sets the last two as well.

## Multiplayer

Everyone needs the mod. Every player can buy and own a Yesla. Remote controls and Assisted Driving answer only
the owner, and a client's own car drives on the client.

## Uninstalling

A save with a Yesla in it cannot load the car without the mod, because the game does not know the vehicle
code. Sell or leave the car before you remove the mod.

pages.title: Yoink
pages.description: A hand winch for Schedule I - hook anything at the exact point you aimed at and reel it out of wherever it is stuck.
pages.markdown:
| | |
|---|---|
| Latest release | `1.2.2` |
| Download | [GitHub](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Yoink) · [Thunderstore](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/DooDesch/Yoink/) |
| Requires | MelonLoader 0.7.3, S1API Forked 3.1.1 |
| Help | [Discord](https://mods.doodesch.de) · [Report a bug](https://support.doodesch.de/yoink) |

> A hand winch for Schedule I. Aim at anything with a rigidbody, fire the hook, and reel it in. Built for the
> case the game has no answer to: a van wedged between two walls, dropped through the world geometry, or
> parked somewhere it can never drive out of.



![Yoink in action: a car hauled in on the winch cable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-Yoink/main/media/yoink.gif)

*Hook the car, hold right click, walk backwards. The cable tightens as the winch takes the load.*

## What it does

The hook bites the spot under your crosshair, not the object's centre. Pull a van by its rear corner and it
swings round; pull it by the nose and it comes at you straight. On something wedged, that choice is usually
the difference between freeing it and grinding it further in.

It reels anything with a rigidbody: vehicles, barrels, crates, litter. A parked car gets its handbrake
released first, because the game leaves it permanently applied on anything nobody is driving, and without
that no amount of force moves it a centimetre. A car with an NPC at the wheel is held in neutral for as long
as the hook is in it, because an AI driver otherwise brakes against the cable every frame.

It bites people too. A shot that lands on somebody takes them off their feet and drags the whole body, and
they get back up by themselves once you let go - the same knockdown and the same recovery the game uses when
a car clips a pedestrian. Set `HookPeople` to false if you would rather it did not.

The cable is simulated rather than drawn. It sags under its own weight, rests on the ground instead of
hanging through it, takes about half a second to tighten when the winch bites, and snaps if you walk too far.

Co-op works. The host owns the physics and a client's pull travels as an intent, and if another player is
sitting in the vehicle you hooked, their machine applies the force, because that is who owns it.

## How to use it

1. Buy the Winch in the hardware store ($80 by default).
2. Equip it. **Left click** fires the hook at whatever you are looking at; click again to let go.
3. **Hold right click** to reel. Walk backwards while holding it and the load follows you out.

The rope breaks at 25 m, and reeling stops once the load is about 2.5 m away so it does not end up in your
face. Both are configurable.

## Settings

Everything lives in `UserData/MelonPreferences.cfg` under `[Yoink]`:

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `PullNewtons` | 40000 | Pull force, about a four-tonne recovery winch. Real mass applies - a loaded van moves slower than a bin. |
| `MaxSpeed` | 1.5 | How fast the hook point is reeled in, m/s. |
| `HookRange` | 15 | How far the hook can be fired, metres. |
| `BreakDistance` | 25 | The rope snaps past this, metres. |
| `StopDistance` | 2.5 | Reeling stops once the load is this close. |
| `RopeSegments` | 20 | Points in the rope simulation. More is smoother, slightly more expensive. |
| `RopeCollision` | true | Rope slack rests on the ground instead of hanging through it. |
| `ShopPrice` | 80 | What it costs on the shelf. Read once when the item is registered. |
| `HookPeople` | true | Whether the hook bites people and drags them. |
| `Knockdown` | 60 | How hard a hooked person is knocked over, in newton-seconds. |

## When it will not move

The mod says why in the console every time it refuses a hook: `nothing within Xm` (nothing hookable in
range), `has no rigidbody` (scenery), `is fixed in place` (kinematic, and no winch moves a building).

If it hooked but nothing happens, it is usually one of three things. Another player is sitting in the
vehicle, in which case their machine owns it. Or it is wedged hard and wants a different hook point - aim at
the corner that has somewhere to go. Or it is simply heavy: raise `PullNewtons`.

`PullNewtons` and `MaxSpeed` do different jobs. The force decides whether a heavy thing moves at all; the
speed caps how fast anything is allowed to arrive. Raising the force will not make a barrel come faster,
because the speed ceiling binds first. Raising the speed will not free a stuck van.

## Multiplayer

Everyone needs the mod. The machine that owns an object applies the force to it, so a pull on a networked
object goes through the host, and a pull on a vehicle another player is sitting in is handed to their machine,
which is the only one whose forces that vehicle accepts. A vehicle an NPC is driving stays the host's. The rope
is not networked and does not need to be.

Co-op is implemented and reviewed but has not been run with two players since the physics rework.

<details><summary>Requirements</summary>


- [MelonLoader](https://melonwiki.xyz/) 0.7.3 or newer
- [S1API](https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/p/ifBars/S1API_Forked/) 3.1.1 or newer


</details>

<details><summary>Credits</summary>


Built by DooDesch on [S1API](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API) by ifBars.
Winch sound effect by **fadestyle**.


</details>

pages.title: Call another mod's API
pages.description: Add another mod's API to your project and keep your mod working when that mod is not installed.
pages.markdown:
Add the API to your project, mark the mod optional, and call it. The "Use this API" block on each API reference page has the exact file and csproj lines.

## Pick your kind of API

| Kind | Mods | What you add |
|---|---|---|
| One source file | Snitch, Hotline, Sideload, TightBeam, Clipwise, Hash | Copy one `.cs` file into your project. Nothing extra to ship. |
| The mod's DLL | SideHustle, Personnel, Inkorporated | Reference the mod's DLL with `<Private>false</Private>`. |

## Steps for a source file

1. Copy the file into your project:

   ```xml
   <Compile Include="path\to\Snitch.cs" />
   ```

2. Mark the mod optional:

   ```csharp
   [assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("Snitch")]
   ```

3. Call it. Without the mod, every call does nothing and returns a default.

   ```csharp
   using Snitch.Api;

   using (Profiler.Sample("MyMod.Pathfinding"))
   {
       // runs the same with or without Snitch
   }
   ```

Calls made before the mod loads run when it loads. Load order does not matter.

## Steps for a DLL

1. Reference the DLL from your game's `Mods` folder:

   ```xml
   <Reference Include="SideHustle">
     <HintPath>path\to\Schedule I\Mods\SideHustle.dll</HintPath>
     <Private>false</Private>
   </Reference>
   ```

2. Mark the mod optional, as above.

3. Put every call into a separate class, and call that class only when the mod is loaded.

   A method that names a type from a missing DLL fails before its first line. A `try`/`catch` inside that method does not catch it. SideHustle ships [`SideHustleLink.cs`](https://github.com/DooDesch-Mods/ScheduleOne-SideHustle/blob/main/Examples/SideHustleLink.cs) for this.

## Rules for every API

- Call the API from Unity's main thread. Your callbacks also run on the main thread.
- In a hot path, check the API's `Enabled` or `Available` flag first. A call that does nothing still costs a call.

  ```csharp
  if (Profiler.Enabled)
  {
      using (Profiler.Sample("MyMod.Inner")) { }
  }
  ```

## Support an older version of the mod

The reference shows the latest release. A member that came later says **Added in `x.y.z`**. A member without that line exists in every release.
The **Changes by version** page lists what each release added and removed. Read "Removed" before you raise the version you require.

## Next

- [What do you want to build?](/build/)

chassis.Name: ChassisApi
chassis.Summary:
Public entry point for other mods: read and change the seat profiles Chassis uses per vehicle code.

Precedence, last one wins: a profile a mod registers with `Register`, the JSON file in UserData/Chassis/<code>.json. The file wins so a player or the debug console can always correct a mod's values. Changes take effect on the next seat change; `Changed` tells seated rigs to re-read now.

Members.Name: PoseAsPusher
Members.Signature:
public static bool PoseAsPusher(
    Player player,
    LandVehicle vehicle,
    bool glide = true)
Members.Summary: Poses a player's body behind a vehicle with the hands on the handles from `ChassisProfile.Push`. For the local player the key hints switch to the pusher's keys. Returns false with the reason logged when the vehicle has no push profile or the body cannot be posed.

Parameters.Name: glide
Parameters.Description: true eases the body into the pose over a moment, false puts it there at once.

Members.Name: ReleasePusher
Members.Summary: Lets go: the body of a player posed with `PoseAsPusher` moves on its own again.

Members.Name: PushedBy
Members.Summary: The vehicle a player is posed behind, or null.

Members.Name: LocalDriverThrottle
Members.Summary: The local driver's own throttle this physics step, before mods add to it in their own UpdateThrottle postfix. Chassis records it first; a pusher mod adds the pusher's input after that, so a seated body's hands follow only the driver's keys.

Members.Name: AddKeyHint
Members.Signature:
public static void AddKeyHint(
    string id,
    string label,
    Func<KeyHintContext, bool> show,
    params KeyCode[] keys)

A `Secondary` slot takes the second paint ("paint2") instead and keeps its own material without one. A `Flat` slot drops its colour texture while painted (the normal map stays), for a part whose texture is dark or two-toned: the paint multiplies the texture, so it would show darker than chosen.

Members.Name: PaintTarget
Members.Signature: public PaintTarget(Renderer renderer, int materialIndex, bool secondary)

chassis.Name: ChassisProfile
chassis.Summary:
Where occupants sit and hold on in one vehicle type, keyed by its vehicle code. Every point is in the space of the vehicle's model frame: the transform at `Frame` under the vehicle, or the vehicle root when that is empty. Left-side points are the mirror of the right-side values stored here, about the seat's own centre plane (through the seat root, turned by its yaw); in wheel mode the hands mirror about the steering column.

The same object backs the JSON file (UserData/Chassis/<code>.json) and the C# API, so a value set from code, from the file or from the debug console is the same value.
chassis.Remarks: Points are `Vector3` values in metres in the frame's own axes: x to the vehicle's right, y up, z forward. Angles are in degrees. Weights run from 0 (the animation decides) to 1 (the profile decides). In the JSON file a vector is `[x, y, z]` and a colour is `[r, g, b, a]` with each channel from 0 to 1.

Members.Name: Code
Members.Summary: Vehicle code (`LandVehicle.VehicleCode`) this profile belongs to.
Members.Value: Lower case, matched without case. The vanilla cars are "shitbox", "shitbox_police", "veeper", "bruiser", "bruiser_police", "dinkler", "hounddog", "cheetah" and "hotbox"; the wheelchair from the mod Rollin is "rollin_wheelchair". A mod vehicle can use a code of its own and get it with `ChassisApi.Assign`. `ChassisApi.Codes` lists every code that has a profile.

Members.Name: Frame
Members.Summary: Path of the model frame below the vehicle root, or empty for the root itself.
Members.Value: Transform names joined with "/", as `Transform.Find` takes them, e.g. "Body/Model". When that path does not exist, the first transform named like its last part is used. Rollin's wheelchair uses "ChassisModel"; the vanilla cars leave it empty.

Members.Name: Seats
Members.Summary: One entry per `LandVehicle.Seats` index that should show a seated body.

Members.Name: Push
Members.Summary: Where a second player stands and holds on to push, or null when the vehicle cannot be pushed.

Members.Name: Steering
Members.Summary: The steering wheel that turns with the road wheels, or null when the vehicle has none.

Members.Name: Parts
Members.Summary: Lids and wipers that move by themselves.

Members.Name: Lamps
Members.Summary: Indicator lamps, or null when the model has none.

Members.Name: Horn
Members.Summary: Horn and lock chirp sounds; null uses the built-in ones.

Members.Name: AutoLights
Members.Summary: Headlights switch on by themselves while the vehicle is driven between 17:30 and 06:00.

Members.Name: Interior
Members.Summary: The base interior Chassis builds into a vehicle without one, or null for none.

Members.Name: Gauges
Members.Summary: Needles, lamps and digit displays in the cockpit.

Members.Name: Controls
Members.Summary: Switches a seated player can use in first person.

Members.Name: Control
Members.Summary: The switch with this name (case ignored), or null.

Members.Name: Seat
Members.Summary: The seat entry for this `LandVehicle.Seats` index, or null when the seat shows no body.

Members.Name: Part
Members.Summary: The part with this name (case ignored), or null.

Members.Name: Clone
Members.Summary: A deep copy, made through the same JSON the profile file uses.

chassis.Name: SeatProfile
chassis.Summary: One seated body: where the avatar sits, where the first-person camera looks from, and how the hands and feet hold on.

Members.Name: Index
Members.Summary: Index into `LandVehicle.Seats`.
Members.Value: 0 up to the number of vanilla seats minus 1. The driver's seat is the one with `isDriverSeat` set.

Members.Name: Root
Members.Summary: Avatar root. The vanilla sit clip puts the hips 0.825 m above it.
Members.Value: A point in the frame, in metres. With the hips 0.5 m above the frame origin, y is -0.325.

Members.Name: Yaw
Members.Summary: Avatar yaw against the frame, in degrees.
Members.Value: 0 faces the frame's forward axis, 90 its right, 180 backwards.

Members.Name: Recline
Members.Summary: How far the whole body leans back, in degrees, turned about the hips; the back stays straight.
Members.Value: 0 sits upright as the sit clip does. 15 suits a low car roof. Hands and feet keep their own points.

Members.Name: Eyes
Members.Summary: Camera position for the first-person view.
Members.Value: A point in the frame, in metres; about 0.6 m above the hips looks from the avatar's eyes.

Members.Name: Pose
Members.Summary: Animator bool that holds the pose; vanilla has "Sitting".
Members.Value: "Sitting" is the only seated pose the vanilla avatar has.

Members.Name: Hands
Members.Summary: Hands, or null to leave the arms to the animation.

Members.Name: Feet
Members.Summary: Feet, or null to leave the legs to the animation.

chassis.Name: HandProfile
chassis.Summary: Hand targets of a seated body: on push rims, on the steering wheel or at a fixed grip. Right side; the left is mirrored.

Members.Name: Mode
Members.Summary: "rim": hands ride the push rims of two wheels. "fixed": hands stay at `GripStart`. "wheel": hands hold the steering wheel at `GripStart` and turn with it up to `FollowMax` degrees.

Members.Name: FollowMax
Members.Summary: Wheel mode: the hands follow the steering wheel this far either way, then stay.

Members.Name: LeftWheel
Members.Summary: Rim mode: name of the left wheel transform in the model.
Members.Value: A transform name below the frame, e.g. "RimPivot_L" on the wheelchair. Empty outside rim mode.

Members.Name: RightWheel
Members.Summary: Rim mode: name of the right wheel transform in the model.
Members.Value: A transform name below the frame, e.g. "RimPivot_R" on the wheelchair. Empty outside rim mode.

Members.Name: GripStart
Members.Summary: Right hand where a push stroke starts. Rim mode: from the wheel centre; fixed mode: in the frame.
Members.Value: In metres. Rim mode: offset from the right wheel's centre, e.g. (0.04, 0.26, 0.15) on the wheelchair. Fixed and wheel mode: a point in the frame; for the wheel, about 0.17 m right of its centre.

Members.Name: GripEnd
Members.Summary: Rim mode: right hand where the stroke ends and the hand lets go.
Members.Value: Offset from the right wheel's centre in metres, e.g. (0.04, 0.15, 0.27) on the wheelchair.

Members.Name: Recovery
Members.Summary: Seconds the hand takes from the end of a stroke back to its start.

Members.Name: RotationWeight
Members.Summary: How strongly the hands turn to the grip, 0 to 1; 0 leaves the wrists to the animation.

Members.Name: RimRadius
Members.Summary: Wheel mode: radius of the steering wheel's rim, from the steering pivot to the middle of the rim. Above 0 the hands close around the rim at `GripAngle`: palm on the rim, fingers around it, thumb on the inside, and `GripStart` and `RotationWeight` are not used. 0 keeps the wrists at `GripStart` with the fingers as the animation leaves them.
Members.Value: In metres, e.g. 0.18 on a car wheel 0.39 m across. `ChassisApi.FitSeat` measures it from the wheel's mesh.

Members.Name: RimThickness
Members.Summary: Wheel mode: thickness of the rim the fingers close around.
Members.Value: In metres, e.g. 0.03.

Members.Name: RimOffset
Members.Summary: Wheel mode: how far the rim's middle sits from the steering pivot along the column, towards the driver, in metres. 0 when the pivot is the rim's centre; set it when the pivot sits at the hub behind the rim.

Members.Name: GripAngle
Members.Summary: Wheel mode with a `RimRadius`: where the right hand holds the rim, the left one mirrored.
Members.Value: Degrees from level towards the top of the wheel: 0 holds it at quarter to three, 30 at ten to two, negative below.

Members.Name: Elbow
Members.Summary: Elbow bend goal (right side).
Members.Value: A point in the frame the elbow bends towards, in metres: right of and behind the hand points it outwards.

Members.Name: LeanStart
Members.Summary: Point the spine reaches for at the start of a stroke.

Members.Name: LeanStartWeight
Members.Summary: How strongly the spine reaches for `LeanStart`, 0 to 1.

Members.Name: LeanEnd
Members.Summary: Point the spine reaches for at the end of a stroke.

Members.Name: LeanEndWeight
Members.Summary: How strongly the spine reaches for `LeanEnd`, 0 to 1.

chassis.Name: FootProfile
chassis.Summary: Foot targets of a seated body. Right side; the left is mirrored.

Members.Name: Position
Members.Summary: Right foot target (left mirrored).
Members.Value: A point in the frame in metres, e.g. (0.165, 0.17, 0.46) puts the foot on the wheelchair's footrest.

Members.Name: Rotation
Members.Summary: Right foot bone rotation against the frame in degrees (yaw and roll mirrored for the left). The bone's Y axis runs to the toes and its X axis points to the body's left, so (-90, 180, 0) is a flat foot with the toes forward and the sole down. (90, 0, 0) points the toes forward too, but with the sole up.

Members.Name: RotationWeight
Members.Summary: How strongly the feet turn to `Rotation`, 0 to 1; 0 leaves the ankles to the animation.

Members.Name: Knee
Members.Summary: Knee bend goal (right side).

chassis.Name: PushProfile
chassis.Summary: Where a second player stands and holds on to push the vehicle. Right side; the left is mirrored.

Members.Name: Stand
Members.Summary: Where the pusher's feet stand.

Members.Name: Handle
Members.Summary: Right handle grip (left mirrored).

Members.Name: Elbow
Members.Summary: Elbow bend goal of the pusher (right side).

Members.Name: Reach
Members.Summary: Range in metres from the stand point within which a player can take the handles.

chassis.Name: SteeringProfile
chassis.Summary: A steering wheel in the model that turns with the road wheels.

Members.Name: Path
Members.Summary: Pivot of the steering wheel below the frame; a single name is searched in the whole frame.
Members.Value: A path like "Dashboard/SteeringWheel" or one name like "SteeringWheel". The base interior's wheel is "Chassis_Wheel".

Members.Name: Axis
Members.Summary: Column axis in the pivot's own space at rest.
Members.Value: A direction: (0, 0, 1) when the pivot's forward axis runs along the column, (0, 1, 0) when its up axis does.

Members.Name: Ratio
Members.Summary: Steering wheel degrees per degree of road wheel.

Members.Name: Max
Members.Summary: The wheel stops at this many degrees either way.

Members.Name: Sign
Members.Summary: +1 or -1 for the turning direction; 0 works it out so a right turn moves the top of the wheel right.

chassis.Name: PartProfile
chassis.Summary: A lid or a wiper in the model that Chassis moves.

Members.Name: Name
Members.Summary: Name the API and the debug console use, e.g. "bonnet", "boot", "wiper_l".

Members.Name: Kind
Members.Summary: "lid": opens on request or with the storage. "wiper": sweeps while it rains and the vehicle runs.

Members.Name: Path
Members.Summary: Pivot below the frame at the hinge or axle; a single name is searched in the whole frame.
Members.Value: A path like "Body/BootHinge" or one name like "BootHinge".

Members.Name: Axis
Members.Summary: Hinge or axle in the pivot's own space at rest.
Members.Value: A direction: on a pivot turned like the car, (1, 0, 0) for a bonnet or boot hinged across it and (0, 0, 1) for a wiper axle facing forward.

Members.Name: Angle
Members.Summary: Lid: open angle. Wiper: sweep. In degrees.

Members.Name: Seconds
Members.Summary: Lid: seconds to open or close. Wiper: seconds per stroke in light rain.

Members.Name: FastSeconds
Members.Summary: Wiper: seconds per stroke in heavy rain.

Members.Name: Sign
Members.Summary: +1 or -1 for the turning direction; 0 works it out so the part lifts.

Members.Name: Storage
Members.Summary: Lid: opens while the vehicle's storage is open from this end, "front" or "rear"; empty never.

chassis.Name: LampProfile
chassis.Summary: Indicator lamps in the model.

Members.Name: Left
Members.Summary: Names of the left indicator lamp objects. A name also matches "name.001" and every renderer below it.
Members.Value: Transform names in the model, for example ["Indicator_FL", "Indicator_RL"] for a front and a rear lamp.

Members.Name: Right
Members.Summary: Names of the right indicator lamp objects, matched as `Left`.

Members.Name: Color
Members.Summary: Glow colour while a lamp flashes.
Members.Value: Channels from 0 to 1; the default (1, 0.42, 0) is amber. In JSON: [1, 0.42, 0, 1].

Members.Name: UseTexture
Members.Summary: The glow takes the lamp's own texture as its pattern; off, the whole lamp glows in `Color`.

chassis.Name: HornProfile
chassis.Summary: Horn and lock chirp sounds of a vehicle.

Members.Name: Clip
Members.Summary: Sound name from `ChassisApi.RegisterSound`; empty is the built-in two-tone horn.
Members.Value: The name a mod passed to `ChassisApi.RegisterSound`, e.g. "mymod_horn".

Members.Name: Chirp
Members.Summary: Sound name of the lock chirp; empty is the built-in chirp.
Members.Value: The name a mod passed to `ChassisApi.RegisterSound`, e.g. "mymod_chirp".

Members.Name: Position
Members.Summary: Where the sound comes from, in the vehicle root's space.
Members.Value: A point in metres; the default (0, 0.6, 1.8) is at the front of a car.

Members.Name: Volume
Members.Summary: Volume of horn and chirp, 0 to 1.

chassis.Name: InteriorProfile
chassis.Summary: The base interior: seats, a dashboard and a steering wheel built from simple shapes, the inside of the body shell drawn as a dark lining, and see-through tinted windows. Points are in the profile's frame.

Members.Name: Parts
Members.Summary: Kit pieces: "seat", "bench", "dash", "gauges", "wheel".

Members.Name: Lining
Members.Summary: Draws the inside of the body shell, so the cabin is closed when seen through the glass.

Members.Name: LiningColor
Members.Summary: Lining colour.

Members.Name: OpenLid
Members.Summary: Cuts the flat lid some vanilla bodies close the cabin with at the belt line out of the body mesh.

Members.Name: Glass
Members.Summary: The windows, or null to keep them as they are.

chassis.Name: KitPart
chassis.Summary: One simple shape of the base interior.

Members.Name: Kind
Members.Summary: "seat" (cushion and backrest), "bench" (a seat across several places), "dash", "gauges" (the hood over the dials), "wheel", and the instrument pieces "needle", "rocker" (a switch that tips), "button" (a round push button facing back), "stalk" (a lever pointing left) and "lamp" (a small block a lamp gauge lights).

Members.Name: Name
Members.Summary: Name of the part's object, so gauges, switches and other parts can find it; empty names it by kind.
Members.Value: A transform name such as "Chassis_SpeedNeedle". The wheel is "Chassis_Wheel" unless named otherwise.

Members.Name: Parent
Members.Summary: Name of another kit part this one hangs below and moves with, or empty for none.
Members.Value: "Chassis_Wheel" puts a horn button on the steering wheel. `Position` stays in the frame either way.

Members.Name: Position
Members.Summary: Seat and bench: middle of the cushion top. Dash: middle of the top edge at the windscreen. Gauges: middle of the back bottom edge. Wheel: centre of the rim. Needle: its pivot. Rocker, lamp: its centre. Button: the middle of its back. Stalk: where it meets the column.

Members.Name: Rotation
Members.Summary: Euler angles in the frame. A wheel's column runs along its local forward axis.

Members.Name: Size
Members.Summary: Seat and bench: width, backrest height, cushion depth. Dash and gauges: width, height, depth. Wheel: rim radius, -, column length. Needle: width, length, thickness. Rocker and lamp: width, height, depth. Button: radius, -, depth. Stalk: length, thickness, -.

Members.Name: Color
Members.Summary: Colour of the shape.

chassis.Name: GlassProfile
chassis.Summary: Which materials are windows and how they are tinted.

Members.Name: Materials
Members.Summary: Window materials are the ones whose name starts with one of these.
Members.Value: Material name prefixes; the vanilla cars use "window_opaque".

Members.Name: Tint
Members.Summary: Glass colour; alpha is how much of the cabin it hides.
Members.Value: Channels from 0 to 1; alpha 0 is clear glass, 1 hides the cabin. In JSON: [0.2, 0.24, 0.28, 0.55].

chassis.Name: GaugeReading
chassis.Summary: One value of a gauge source, and whether this peer knows it.
chassis.Remarks: A value is not valid when this peer cannot know it: the throttle of a car an NPC drives on a client, the odometer before the host's first update, a mod source that threw. Gauges hold their last position while a value is not valid.

Members.Name: Value
Members.Summary: The value, in the unit of its source; 0 when not valid.

Members.Name: Valid
Members.Summary: True when this peer knows the value.

Members.Name: GaugeReading
Members.Summary: A reading with a value.

Members.Name: Invalid
Members.Summary: A reading this peer does not know.

Members.Name: ToString
Members.Summary: The value with two decimals, or "-" when not valid.

chassis.Name: VehicleTelemetry
chassis.Summary: Everything Chassis knows about a vehicle's driving state at one moment, from `ChassisApi.Telemetry`. Each value carries its own validity; see `GaugeReading`.

Members.Name: Vehicle
Members.Summary: The vehicle the snapshot is of.

Members.Name: At
Members.Summary: `Time.time` when the snapshot was taken.

Members.Name: Speed
Members.Summary: Speed in the player's unit (km/h or mph, `ChassisApi.UsesMph`), as the speedometer shows it.

Members.Name: SpeedKmh
Members.Summary: Speed in km/h as the speedometer shows it: vanilla's `Speed_Kmh` times 1.4, never negative.
Members.Value: On a passenger's peer it trails the driver's by about 0.4 s.

Members.Name: Rpm
Members.Summary: Estimated engine speed in revolutions per minute: 800 idle up to 6000 at top speed, 0 with nobody aboard.
Members.Value: Vanilla has no engine model; this follows speed and throttle as vanilla's engine sound does.

Members.Name: Throttle
Members.Summary: Throttle from -1 (reverse) to 1. Synced by Chassis from the driver's peer, up to 10 times a second.

Members.Name: Handbrake
Members.Summary: 1 while the handbrake is on, else 0. Synced like `Throttle`.

Members.Name: Brake
Members.Summary: 1 while the brakes are on, else 0.

Members.Name: Reverse
Members.Summary: 1 while the vehicle drives backwards, else 0.

Members.Name: Headlights
Members.Summary: 1 while the headlights are on, else 0.

Members.Name: Indicator
Members.Summary: -1 left, 0 off, 1 right; 0 while the hazard lights flash.

Members.Name: Hazard
Members.Summary: 1 while the hazard lights flash, else 0.

Members.Name: Steer
Members.Summary: Front wheel angle from -1 (full left) to 1 (full right).

Members.Name: Clock
Members.Summary: Game time as HHMM, e.g. 1730 for half past five in the afternoon.

Members.Name: OdometerKm
Members.Summary: Total distance in km, counted by the host with the speedometer's factor and saved with player-owned vehicles.

Members.Name: TripKm
Members.Summary: Distance in km since the last trip reset.

Members.Name: Occupied
Members.Summary: 1 when anyone is aboard (players or NPCs), else 0.

Members.Name: Driver
Members.Summary: 1 when someone is at the wheel (a player or an NPC), else 0.

Members.Name: Get
Members.Summary: Any source by name, read now; also the ones mods registered.

Parameters.Name: source
Parameters.Description: A name from `ChassisApi.GaugeSources`.

chassis.Name: ControlUse
chassis.Summary: A switch in a cockpit was used, from `ChassisApi.ControlUsed` and the handlers of `ChassisApi.RegisterControlAction`.

Members.Name: Vehicle
Members.Signature: public LandVehicle Vehicle { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The vehicle the switch is in.

Members.Name: Control
Members.Signature: public ControlProfile Control { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The switch, from the vehicle's profile.

Members.Name: Action
Members.Signature: public string Action { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The switch's action, e.g. "lights" or "mymod.siren".

Members.Name: Value
Members.Signature: public float Value { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The new value: 1 for a button, 0 or 1 for a toggle, the knob's new position.

Members.Name: By
Members.Signature: public Player By { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The player who used it, or null when a mod called `ChassisApi.UseControl`.

Members.Name: IsHost
Members.Signature: public bool IsHost { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: True on the host. Do work that changes the world only where this is set; the handler runs on every peer.

chassis.Name: OccupantDown
chassis.Summary: A seated NPC that just died or was knocked out, as `ChassisApi.RegisterOccupantDown` hands it over.

Members.Name: Vehicle
Members.Summary: The vehicle the NPC sits in.

Members.Name: Npc
Members.Summary: The NPC, about to die or be knocked out; its health still reads the moment before.

Members.Name: Seat
Members.Summary: Index into `Vehicle.Seats`; 0 is the driver.

Members.Name: Dead
Members.Summary: True when the NPC died, false when it was knocked out.

chassis.Name: GaugeProfile
chassis.Summary: One display in the cockpit: a needle that turns with a value, a lamp that glows above a threshold, or digits. It reads a source by name (`ChassisApi.GaugeSources`) and moves a transform of the vehicle's model or interior. Chassis draws gauges on every peer, for vehicles near the camera.

Members.Name: Name
Members.Summary: Name the debug output and warnings use, e.g. "speedo".

Members.Name: Kind
Members.Summary: "needle", "lamp" or "digits".
Members.Value: "needle" turns the transform at `Path` from `From` to `To` degrees about `Axis`. "lamp" makes every renderer below it glow in `Color` while the value is above `Threshold`. "digits" puts a text below it that shows the value in `Format`.

Members.Name: Path
Members.Summary: The transform to move, light or write on, below the vehicle's frame.
Members.Value: A path like "Chassis_Interior/Dash/SpeedoNeedle", or one name like "SpeedoNeedle" that is searched in the whole frame. A needle's transform should sit at the pivot of the needle. Chassis logs one warning per vehicle code when the path is not found.

Members.Name: Source
Members.Summary: The value the gauge shows, by source name.
Members.Value: A built-in source such as "speed", "rpm", "lights" or "clock_hours", or a name a mod registered with `ChassisApi.RegisterGaugeSource`. The full list with units is on `ChassisApi.GaugeSources`.

Members.Name: Min
Members.Summary: Needle: the value at `From`. Values outside Min and Max stop at the end of the dial.
Members.Value: In the unit of the source, e.g. 0 for a speedometer.

Members.Name: Max
Members.Summary: Needle: the value at `To`.
Members.Value: In the unit of the source, e.g. 160 for a speedometer that ends at 160 km/h.

Members.Name: From
Members.Summary: Needle: angle at `Min`, in degrees about `Axis` from the needle's rest pose.
Members.Value: With the default axis (0, 0, -1) on a needle that points up at rest, -135 points to the lower left as the driver sees it.

Members.Name: To
Members.Summary: Needle: angle at `Max`, in degrees.
Members.Value: 135 points to the lower right with the default axis; From -135 to To 135 sweeps 270 degrees clockwise.

Members.Name: Axis
Members.Summary: Needle: the turning axis in the needle transform's own space.
Members.Value: A direction. (0, 0, -1) turns clockwise as seen by a driver who looks along the vehicle's forward axis at a dial that faces back towards them.

Members.Name: Smooth
Members.Summary: Needle and digits: seconds the shown value takes to follow the source; 0 follows at once.

Members.Name: Threshold
Members.Summary: Lamp: glows while the value is above this.
Members.Value: 0.5 suits the on/off sources, which read 0 or 1.

Members.Name: Color
Members.Summary: Lamp: glow colour. Digits: text colour.
Members.Value: Channels from 0 to 1. In JSON: [1, 0.42, 0, 1] for amber.

Members.Name: Format
Members.Summary: Digits: number format of the value.
Members.Value: A .NET numeric format in invariant culture: "0" for whole numbers, "0.0" for one decimal, "000000" for an odometer with leading zeros. The source "clock" formats as "00:00" by itself.

Members.Name: Size
Members.Summary: Digits: height of one line of text in metres.
Members.Value: 0.02 to 0.03 reads well on a dashboard at arm's length.

chassis.Example:
A speedometer needle that sweeps from 0 to 160 km/h across 270 degrees:

```csharp
profile.Gauges.Add(new GaugeProfile { Name = "speedo", Kind = "needle", Path = "Dash/SpeedoNeedle", Source = "speed_kmh", Min = 0f, Max = 160f });
```

chassis.Name: ControlProfile
chassis.Summary: One switch in the cockpit a seated player can use in first person: look at it and click, or turn a knob with the mouse wheel. Everyone within reach (about 0.9 m from the eyes) can use it; the click goes through the host to every peer, and Chassis keeps and saves the state of toggles and knobs.

Members.Name: Name
Members.Summary: Name of the switch, unique in the profile; the saved state and `ChassisApi.ControlValue` use it.

Members.Name: Label
Members.Summary: The name the player reads under the centre dot while looking at the switch.
Members.Value: For example "Hazard lights". Empty shows `Name` with a capital first letter and spaces for "_".

Members.Name: Kind
Members.Summary: "button", "toggle" or "knob".
Members.Value: "button" fires its action on a click and springs back. "toggle" flips between 0 and 1 on a click. "knob" steps between `Min` and `Max` with the mouse wheel; a click puts it back to `Default`.

Members.Name: Path
Members.Summary: The transform that moves and that the player aims at, below the vehicle's frame.
Members.Value: A path or one name, searched as `GaugeProfile.Path`. Its renderers give the area to aim at unless `BoxSize` is set.

Members.Name: Action
Members.Summary: What the switch does.
Members.Value: A built-in action: "lights" (headlights on/off), "hazard" (hazard lights on/off), "indicator" (a knob from -1 left to 1 right), "indicator_left", "indicator_right", "horn" or "trip_reset". Any other name is a mod's own action from `ChassisApi.RegisterControlAction`; empty does nothing but keep the state.

Members.Name: Source
Members.Summary: A source whose value the switch shows instead of its own state, or empty.
Members.Value: For switches whose state can change without them: "lights" for a light switch (the light key also switches), "hazard", "indicator". Any source from `ChassisApi.GaugeSources` works.

Members.Name: Axis
Members.Summary: The axis the switch turns about (toggle, knob) or moves along (button), in its own space.
Members.Value: A direction, e.g. (1, 0, 0) for a rocker switch that tips forward and back, (0, 0, 1) for a button pushed forward.

Members.Name: Angle
Members.Summary: Toggle: degrees between off and on. Knob: degrees from `Min` to `Max`.
Members.Value: The rest pose is the middle: a toggle stands at -Angle/2 off and +Angle/2 on.

Members.Name: Press
Members.Summary: Button: how far it moves along `Axis` while pressed, in metres.

Members.Name: Min
Members.Summary: Knob: lowest value.

Members.Name: Max
Members.Summary: Knob: highest value.

Members.Name: Step
Members.Summary: Knob: change per notch of the mouse wheel.

Members.Name: Default
Members.Summary: Toggle and knob: the value before anyone touched it, and a knob's value after a click.

Members.Name: BoxCenter
Members.Summary: Centre of the area to aim at, in the switch transform's own space; used when `BoxSize` is set.

Members.Name: BoxSize
Members.Summary: Size of the area to aim at in metres, in the switch transform's own space; zero uses its renderers.
Members.Value: Set it for a switch with no renderer of its own, or to make a small one easier to hit.

clipwise.Name: Clipboard
clipwise.Summary:
Clipwise's modder API. Reference Clipwise.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod.

The management clipboard shows every selectable item of a field in one flat, unscrollable icon grid. Clipwise replaces that with a searchable, tabbed picker. Tell it which category your items belong to and they get their own tab instead of being mixed into the vanilla ones.

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when Clipwise is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so this can ship unconditionally with no hard dependency. Registration order does not matter: calls made before Clipwise loads are queued and replayed on bind.

```csharp
using Clipwise.Api;
Clipboard.Category("doodesch.breedtoseed", "tier-1", "Bred - Tier 1", sortOrder: 100)
         .Item("headband", "b2s_headband_seed", sortKey: "Headband",
               tags: new[] { "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1" });
```

Tip: a class named `ClipwiseProbe` with a static `Register()` is auto-discovered and called on bind (see `AutoRegister`), so a mod's Core does not have to wire anything.

Identifiers: `source` is the reverse-DNS id of the registering mod (`"doodesch.breedtoseed"`). A category's canonical key is `"source:id"`. Tags MUST be namespaced the same way (`"doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1"`) - bare tags are rejected by the host so two unrelated mods cannot fight over a name like "tier3". The `clipwise:` namespace is reserved for the host.

All calls MUST be made from the Unity main thread.
clipwise.Remarks: A source and a category id must not be empty and must not contain ":" or whitespace; the host rejects them otherwise. The source "clipwise" is reserved for the host. An item id (`ItemDefinition.ID`) is matched without case. A tag is "namespace:path" with both parts non-empty, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1"; a tag without a namespace or in the "clipwise" namespace is dropped. Sort orders sort lower first.

Members.Name: Available
Members.Summary: True only when the Clipwise host is installed AND bound. Rarely needed - the API is a safe no-op when absent.

Members.Name: AbiVersion
Members.Summary: The host's ABI version: 0 when Clipwise is absent, 1 for the initial contract. Use this only to gate on capabilities added in a later ABI; everything below degrades to a no-op on its own.
Members.Value: 0 without Clipwise. 1 for the initial contract. 2 once `Facts` is available.

Members.Name: Category
Members.Signature:
public static CategoryRef Category(
    string source,
    string id,
    string label,
    int sortOrder = 0,
    string iconItemId = null)
Members.Summary: Declare a category - one tab in the picker. `sortOrder` orders the tabs (lower first; vanilla sits at 0). `iconItemId` optionally names an item whose icon represents the tab. Returns a fluent builder for the items in it. Load-order-proof.
Members.Returns: A handle that places items in this category.

Parameters.Description: The reverse-DNS id of the registering mod, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed". No ":" and no whitespace; "clipwise" is reserved.

Parameters.Name: id

Parameters.Name: label
Parameters.Description: The tab text, e.g. "Breed to Seed Strains". Null or blank shows the id.

Parameters.Name: sortOrder
Parameters.Description: Tab position, lower first. Vanilla sits at 0. Equal values sort by key.

Parameters.Name: iconItemId
Parameters.Description: An `ItemDefinition.ID`, e.g. "b2s_headband_seed". Null or blank sets no icon item.

Members.Name: RegisterItem
Members.Signature:
public static void RegisterItem(
    string source,
    string id,
    string itemId,
    string category,
    string[] tags = null,
    int sortOrder = 0,
    string sortKey = null,
    string description = null,
    int precedence = 0)
Members.Summary:
Place one item in a category. `id` is this mod's own stable key for the entry, unique within `source`; `itemId` is the game's `ItemDefinition.ID` the entry stands for; `category` is a canonical category key (`"source:id"`). `sortKey` orders entries inside the category (falls back to the item's display name); `description` shows up in the tooltip; `precedence` breaks ties when several sources claim the same item (higher wins).

Returns nothing on purpose: a call queued before Clipwise loaded cannot know whether the future host accepts it. Re-registering the same (source, id) is an idempotent upsert, so calling this twice is safe. Load-order-proof.

Parameters.Name: source
Parameters.Description: The reverse-DNS id of the registering mod, e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed". No ":" and no whitespace.

Parameters.Name: id
Parameters.Description: This mod's own key for the entry, e.g. "headband". Null or blank is rejected.

Parameters.Name: itemId
Parameters.Description: The game's `ItemDefinition.ID`, e.g. "b2s_headband_seed". Matched without case. Null or blank is rejected.

Parameters.Name: category
Parameters.Description: A category key "<source>:<id>", e.g. "doodesch.breedtoseed:bred". Null or blank places the item as if it were not registered. A key that was never declared shows as a tab with a label made from its id.

Parameters.Name: tags
Parameters.Description: Namespaced filter tags, e.g. `new[] { "doodesch.breedtoseed:tier/1" }`. Bare tags and tags in the "clipwise" namespace are dropped. Null adds no tags.

Parameters.Name: sortOrder
Parameters.Description: Position inside the category, lower first. Equal values fall back to `sortKey`.

Parameters.Name: sortKey
Parameters.Description: Text that orders entries inside the category without case, e.g. "Headband". Null uses the display name. It never changes the shown name.

Parameters.Name: description
Parameters.Description: Tooltip text. Null or blank shows none.

Parameters.Name: precedence
Parameters.Description: Higher wins when several sources claim the same item; default 0. A user override file beats every API claim. Equal precedence goes to the claim whose source, then id, sorts first.

Members.Key: Clipboard.RegisterItem(string, string, string, string, string[], int, string, string, int)

hash.Name: HashCommands
hash.Summary:
Tell the game's command list about a command your mod answers to itself.

A mod that handles console input with a Harmony prefix on `SubmitCommand` - the pattern for anything that wants subcommands or arguments the game's own `ConsoleCommand` cannot express - registers nothing. Its words run when typed and are invisible everywhere else: the in-game command list, an autocomplete, a help overlay, hash. There is nothing to enumerate, because the words only exist as string literals in a switch.

One call fixes that:

```csharp
HashCommands.Add("snitch", "profiler: start, stop, top, report", "snitch start");
```

Listing only. Your prefix keeps running the command exactly as it does now, and the entry this creates never dispatches - a second route would risk running the same line twice.

Reach it through `using Hash.Api;` and call `HashCommands.Add(...)`. Writing `Hash.Api.HashCommands` out in full inside a `MelonMod` does not compile: `MelonBase` has a string property called `Hash`, and the member wins over the namespace.

One file, no references, no hard dependency. Compile it into your mod (`<Compile Include="path\to\HashCommands.cs" />`). Every call is a no-op while hash is absent, and calls made before it loads are replayed once it appears, so load order does not matter.

Members.Name: Available
Members.Summary: True once hash is installed and listening. You rarely need this - `Add` is safe either way; use it to decide whether to log something to the player instead.

Members.Name: Add
Members.Signature:
public static void Add(
    string word,
    string description,
    string example = null)
Members.Summary:
Declare a command word your mod answers to.

The word goes into the game's own command list, which is what every tool reads - so this reaches the vanilla list and any autocomplete as well, not only hash.

Parameters.Name: word
Parameters.Description: The first token of the line, without arguments, e.g. "snitch". Case does not matter. Spaces around it are trimmed. Null, empty or blank declares nothing. A word that is already declared or already in the game's command list is not added again.

Parameters.Name: description
Parameters.Description: One line, lowercase, no trailing period - the way the game words its own, e.g. "profiler: start, stop, top, report". Line breaks become spaces. Longer than 200 characters is cut to 197 plus "...". Null lists no description.

Parameters.Name: example
Parameters.Description: A line that would work, e.g. `snitch top 10`. Optional but worth it: hash shows it as the argument shape while the player is typing. Line breaks and length are handled as in `description`. Null lists no example.

hotline.Name: Hud
hotline.Summary:
The Hotline framework's modder API. Reference Hotline.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod. Register a panel and you instantly get a ready-made, toggleable, draggable in-game window inside the one unified Hotline overlay - no custom hotkey, no custom uGUI, no per-mod debug window. One master key opens the overlay; every mod's controls live there as buttons. Optionally bind a central hotkey to an action and Hotline owns the polling and conflict detection for you.

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when Hotline is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so you can ship this unconditionally with no hard dependency.

```csharp
using Hotline.Api;
Hud.RegisterPanel("MyMod", "My Mod")
   .Text(() => "queue = " + _queue.Count)
   .Action("Reload", Reload)
   .Toggle("Verbose", () => _verbose, v => _verbose = v)
   .Hotkey("Reload", HotlineKey.F8, Reload);   // optional central hotkey
```

Tip: a class named `HotlineProbe` with a static `Register()` is auto-discovered and called on bind (see `AutoRegister`), so your mod's Core does not have to wire anything.

All calls MUST be made from the Unity main thread.

Members.Name: Available
Members.Summary: True only when the Hotline host is installed AND bound. You rarely need this - the API is a safe no-op when absent.

Members.Name: RegisterPanel
Members.Signature: public static Panel RegisterPanel(string id, string title = null)
Members.Summary: Declare a panel: a named, toggleable, movable window in the Hotline overlay that groups everything this mod exposes (text readouts, action buttons, toggles, a log channel). Returns a fluent builder. Load-order-proof; a no-op (the builder still works) if Hotline is absent.

Members.Summary: A clickable button in a mod's panel - the in-game replacement for a debug hotkey action. Runs on the main thread when clicked. Load-order-proof.

Members.Summary: An on/off control in a mod's panel - the in-game replacement for a toggle hotkey. `get` reports the current state, `set` applies it; both run on the main thread. Load-order-proof.

Members.Summary: A draggable value in a mod's panel - the in-game replacement for typing a number into a console to find it. `get` reports the current value, `set` applies it; both run on the main thread. The host clamps to [`min`, `max`] and snaps to `step` (0 = continuous), so a setter never sees a value outside its range. Load-order-proof; a no-op on an older Hotline host that predates slider support.

Polled by the host on the main thread and drawn Point-filtered. Kept as a raw int[] so this shim needs no Unity reference. Load-order-proof; a no-op on an older Hotline host that predates image support.

personnel.Name: API
personnel.Summary: Public, stable entry point for other mods (e.g. Backrooms) that want to consume user-authored NPC definitions. Reference Personnel.dll and declare `[MelonOptionalDependencies("Personnel")]`. The primitive most consumers need is `BuildAvatarSettings` / `ApplyAppearance` - realise a definition's look onto any live `Avatar`. Definitions are loaded from packs on startup; register your own programmatically via `Register`.
personnel.Remarks: A definition id is lower case: letters and digits, every other run of characters turned into "_". A pack entry uses its authored `id`, or else `<packId or folder name>_<npc name>`, e.g. "examples_pale". Packs load from UserData/Personnel/Packs/<pack>/manifest.json on startup.

Members.Name: All
Members.Summary: All loaded NPC definitions (pack-sourced + API-registered).
Members.Value: Pack-sourced and API-registered definitions together. Empty when no pack is installed and nothing was registered.

Members.Name: TryGet
Members.Signature: public static bool TryGet(string id, out NpcDef def)
Members.Summary: Look up a definition by id (case-insensitive).

Parameters.Description: A definition id such as "examples_pale", the same value as `Id`. Null or blank returns false.

Parameters.Name: def

Members.Summary: Register a definition programmatically (de-duplicated by Source/Id). Returns false on duplicate.

Members.Summary: Build the definition's `AvatarSettings` and load it onto a live avatar.
Members.Returns: false when the avatar or the definition is null or no settings could be built.

Parameters.Name: def
Parameters.Description: The definition, e.g. from `TryGet`.

Members.Name: ApplyDistortion
Members.Signature: public static void ApplyDistortion(Avatar avatar, NpcDef def)
Members.Summary: Apply a definition's extreme body distortion (Personify's Experimental tab: bone scale/hide, mesh hide) onto a live avatar. A separate pass from `ApplyAppearance` since vanilla AvatarSettings has no such concept - call this right after loading the normal appearance.

Parameters.Name: avatar
Parameters.Description: A live avatar, with its normal appearance already loaded.

Parameters.Name: def
Parameters.Description: The definition. Its `Appearance.Distortion` keys are the bones "HeadBone", "HipBone", "LeftFootBone", "RightFootBone", "LeftShoulder", "RightShoulder", "MiddleSpine", "LowerSpine" and "LowestSpine", which take a scale or a hide, plus "FaceMesh" and "BodyMesh0", "BodyMesh1" and so on, which only take a hide. A bone missing from the dictionary goes back to scale 1 and visible. Other keys are ignored.

Members.Summary: Configures an S1API `NPCPrefabBuilder` from a definition - identity + full appearance (+ the def's spawn position if it has one). This is the one call needed to turn a Personnel definition into a real, networked, save/load-safe S1API NPC. Prefer subclassing `PersonnelNpc` (which calls this for you); call this directly only if you keep your own `NPC` subclass and want to configure it inside its `ConfigurePrefab`.

Parameters.Description: The builder S1API passes to your NPC's `ConfigurePrefab`.
