Members.Summary: A small set of choices shown as a button group; stored as the chosen `SettingDescriptor.Values`.

Members.Name: Text
Members.Summary: A free-text field of up to 64 characters. On Start the form replaces ';', '=' and line breaks with spaces and trims the text.

Members.Name: Dropdown
Members.Summary: A single choice from `SettingDescriptor.Options`/`SettingDescriptor.Values`, rendered as a compact "< Name >" cycler (a dropdown selector). Stored as the chosen value.

sidehustle.Name: SettingDescriptor
sidehustle.Summary:
One host-configurable setting a gamemode exposes. Side Hustle renders these as a form on the Host screen, then ships the chosen values to the gamemode (host and clients) via the launch context's config blob - see `GamemodeDescriptor.HostSettings` and `MultiplayerInfo`'s getters.

Every value is stored as a string under `Key`. Keep keys short (the whole blob rides on Steam lobby metadata) and stable (they are the wire format your gamemode reads back).
sidehustle.Remarks: Stored form per `Type`: a Slider stores an integer such as "30" with `WholeNumbers`, else a number with up to two decimals such as "0.25". Numbers use the invariant culture (a dot, no thousands separator). A Toggle stores "1" or "0". Segmented and Dropdown store the chosen entry of `Values`, or of `Options` when Values is null. Text stores the typed text. The whole blob of all settings should stay under about 1500 bytes; a larger worst case logs a warning at `API.Register`.

Members.Name: Key
Members.Summary: Stable, short id used to store/read the value (e.g. "round_time"). Required.
Members.Value: Unique within the gamemode, e.g. "len". Compared exactly, case included. Null or empty skips the setting on the form. Read it back with `MultiplayerInfo.GetSetting`.

Members.Name: Label
Members.Summary: Label shown to the host. Required.

Members.Name: Hint
Members.Summary: Optional one-line help shown under the label.

Members.Name: Category
Members.Summary: Optional category name. The host form renders a section header whenever the category changes between consecutive settings, so order settings by category. Null/empty = no header for that setting.

Members.Name: Type
Members.Summary: The control to render.
Members.Value: Default `SettingType.Toggle`.

Members.Name: Default
Members.Summary: Default stored value (string form, parsed per `Type`).
Members.Value: Slider: a number in the invariant culture, e.g. "30". Not a number starts at `Min`; a value outside Min..Max is clamped. Toggle: "1", "0", "true" or "false"; anything else starts off. Segmented and Dropdown: one of the stored values, e.g. "n"; anything else selects the first option. Text: the starting text. Null starts the slider at Min, the toggle off, the first option selected and the text empty.

Members.Name: Unit
Members.Summary: Optional unit suffix shown next to a slider value (e.g. "s", "m", "players").

Members.Name: Min
Members.Summary: Slider minimum.
Members.Value: In the setting's own unit, e.g. 10. Default 0. Above `Max` logs an error.

Members.Name: Max
Members.Summary: Slider maximum.
Members.Value: In the setting's own unit, e.g. 120. Default 1. Leaving the range at 0..1 logs a warning.

Members.Name: Step
Members.Summary: Slider step/granularity (0 = continuous).
Members.Value: In the setting's own unit, e.g. 10. Default 1. 0 or less means continuous, or steps of 1 with `WholeNumbers`. A negative step logs a warning.

Members.Name: WholeNumbers
Members.Summary: When true the slider snaps to whole numbers (integer setting).

Members.Name: Options
Members.Summary: Segmented option labels (what the host sees).
Members.Value: Used by Segmented and Dropdown, e.g. `new[] { "Slow", "Normal", "Fast" }`. Null shows "Off" and "On". An empty array logs an error and shows nothing.

Members.Name: Values
Members.Summary: Stored value per option, parallel to `Options`. When null the option label is stored.
Members.Value: Same length as Options, e.g. `new[] { "s", "n", "f" }`. Fewer entries store the label for the rest and log a warning. More entries log an error.

sidehustle.Name: SettingPreset
sidehustle.Summary: A named bundle of host-setting values a gamemode can offer as a one-click preset (e.g. "Classic Hunt"). Side Hustle shows a preset picker above the settings form; selecting one CASCADES its `Values` into the matching controls (matched by `SettingDescriptor.Key`), which the host can then still tweak. Values use the same wire format as the controls: a Slider's number, a Toggle's "1"/"0", a Segmented's stored value. Keys with no matching control are ignored (forward-compatible with not-yet-built settings).

Members.Name: Name
Members.Summary: Display name shown in the picker (e.g. "Classic Hunt"). Required.

Members.Name: Hint
Members.Summary: Optional one-line description shown under the picker while this preset is selected.

Members.Name: Values
Members.Summary: The setting values this preset applies, keyed by `SettingDescriptor.Key`.
Members.Value: Each value in the control's stored form, e.g. `{ "len", "10" }, { "pace", "f" }`. Keys with no matching setting log a warning and are ignored. Null applies nothing.

Members.Name: Experimental
Members.Summary: When true the picker marks this preset as experimental (a badge + sorted to the back) - use it for presets whose headline mechanic is not fully built yet.

Members.Name: Recommended
Members.Summary: Optional human-readable player-count recommendation shown in the picker (e.g. "Best for 2-6").

Members.Name: MinPlayers
Members.Summary: Player-count range this preset suits best. When the lobby size falls in [`MinPlayers`, `MaxPlayers`] the form may auto-select it on open. 0 = unspecified.
Members.Value: Inclusive player count, e.g. 2. The auto-select needs both ends above 0 and skips experimental presets. Among several fits the narrowest range wins.

Members.Name: MaxPlayers
Members.Summary: Upper end of the player-count range, inclusive, e.g. 4. 0 = unspecified. See `MinPlayers`.

Members.Name: Mode
Members.Summary: Canonical "mode" this preset represents (e.g. "Infection"). When the host tweaks a preset, the effective mode shown to joiners becomes "Custom - {Mode}". Defaults to `Name` when null.

Members.Name: DefaultSelected
Members.Summary: When true the form opens on this preset, overriding the player-count best-fit. Used for a saved "Custom" preset that should be pre-selected next time the host opens the form.

sidehustle.Name: LaunchContext
sidehustle.Summary: Passed to a gamemode's launch callback. Carries who is launching (host / client / singleplayer) and, for multiplayer, the lobby id. The gamemode calls `ReturnToHub` when it is finished so Side Hustle can restore the menu.

Members.Name: Descriptor
Members.Signature: public GamemodeDescriptor Descriptor { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The descriptor being launched.

Members.Name: IsHost
Members.Signature: public bool? IsHost { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: true = host, false = client, null = singleplayer.

Members.Name: LobbyId
Members.Signature: public ulong LobbyId { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: Steam lobby id for multiplayer; 0 for singleplayer.

Members.Name: IsSingleplayer
Members.Summary: True when this is a singleplayer launch.

Members.Name: Role
Members.Summary: Who the local player is in this session; the same information as `IsHost` as an enum. Since 3.0.0.

Members.Name: PlayerCount
Members.Signature: public int PlayerCount { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: Players currently in the lobby (1 for singleplayer).

Members.Name: HostName
Members.Signature: public string HostName { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The host's display name: their session alias when they set one on the Host form, else their Steam persona. On a client it is read from the lobby (`sh_host_name`), which the host writes the same way. Null for singleplayer.

Members.Name: HasPassword
Members.Signature: public bool HasPassword { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: True if the lobby was created with a password.

Members.Name: Multiplayer
Members.Signature: public Multiplayer.MultiplayerInfo Multiplayer { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The full multiplayer payload (max players, gamemode name, the host's free-form config blob, ...). Null for singleplayer. Use this to pass gamemode-specific settings from host to clients.

Members.Name: ReturnToHub
Members.Summary: Call this from your gamemode when it is done (e.g. the player clicks "Back"). Side Hustle restores the main menu and re-shows the hub. Only the first call counts: once the session was ended - by this call or by Side Hustle aborting it - later calls are ignored and logged.

sidehustle.Name: API
sidehustle.Summary: Public, stable entry point for mods that want to appear as a gamemode in Side Hustle's main-menu list. Register early (e.g. in your mod's OnInitializeMelon). Registration is load-order independent, so it does not matter whether Side Hustle or your mod loads first. Reference SideHustle.dll and declare `[assembly: MelonOptionalDependencies("SideHustle")]` so the hub loads first and your mod still loads cleanly if it is absent.
sidehustle.Remarks: A gamemode id is the `GamemodeDescriptor.Id` you registered, e.g. "doodesch.example". Ids are compared exactly, case included. A Steam id is the id64 number, the same value as `SessionPlayer.SteamId`.

Members.Name: ApiVersion
Members.Summary:
The version of this API surface. Rule: it goes up by one with every release that ADDS public API, and never for a fix. 1 = the 1.x hub (Register, descriptor basics), 2 = the 2.x additions (host settings, presets, mod policy, world hygiene flags, KickPlayer), 3 = Side Hustle 3.0.0 (validation, lifecycle events, players, notices, gamemode messages, `Has`).

A property, not a const: a const is copied into the consumer at ITS compile time and would report the version the consumer was built against instead of the one running. Reading this on a Side Hustle older than 3.0.0 throws `MissingMethodException`; the copy-in `SideHustleLink` shim reads it by reflection and returns 0 there.

Members.Name: Has
Members.Summary: True when this Side Hustle supports the named feature. Use the constants on `ApiFeatures`; matching is case-insensitive and an unknown name is false. Exists since 3.0.0 (API version 3): on an older Side Hustle the method itself is missing, so call it through the `SideHustleLink` shim or guard it.

Parameters.Name: feature
Parameters.Description: A constant from `ApiFeatures`, e.g. `ApiFeatures.Messages` ("messages"). Leading and trailing spaces are ignored. Null or empty is false.

Members.Name: Register
Members.Summary: Register (or replace, by `GamemodeDescriptor.Id`) a gamemode. Replacing an existing id is allowed and makes hot-reload / double-registration safe. Since 3.0.0 the descriptor is checked here and every problem is logged with the gamemode id and the field name; nothing is rejected that worked before. A second registration of the same id from a DIFFERENT mod is logged as a warning and still replaces the first.

Parameters.Name: descriptor
Parameters.Description: The gamemode to list. Null throws `ArgumentNullException`. An empty `GamemodeDescriptor.Id` throws `ArgumentException`. An empty `GamemodeDescriptor.DisplayName` is set to the id.

Members.Name: Unregister
Members.Summary: Remove a previously registered gamemode. Returns true if one was removed.

Parameters.Name: id
Parameters.Description: The `GamemodeDescriptor.Id` it registered with, e.g. "doodesch.example". Matched exactly, case included. Null or empty returns false.

Members.Name: KickPlayer
Members.Summary: Host-only: kick the connected player with this Steam id (id64) from the current session. A no-op on a client or if no such player is connected, and never kicks the host itself. Returns true if a player was kicked. Reusable by any gamemode that manages a Side Hustle lobby.

Parameters.Name: steamId64
Parameters.Description: The player's Steam id64, the same value as `SessionPlayer.SteamId`. It is matched against the player's `Player.PlayerCode`.

Parameters.Name: reason
Parameters.Description: The reason passed to the kick and written to the log. Null or empty uses "Kicked by host".

Members.Name: IsReady
Members.Signature: public static bool IsReady { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: True once Side Hustle's own OnInitializeMelon has run. `Ready` fires at the same moment.

Members.Name: Registered
Members.Summary: A snapshot of the registered gamemodes. Since 3.0.0 this is a copy: registering or removing a gamemode later does not change a list you already hold.

Members.Name: CurrentSession
Members.Summary: The running gamemode session, or null. Set just before `SessionStarted` and cleared just before `SessionEnded`. Since 3.0.0.

Members.Name: Players
Members.Summary: The players in the current session as a snapshot copy (empty outside a session). A singleplayer session holds only the local player. Display names follow the session alias where one is known. Since 3.0.0.

Members.Name: ShowNotice
Members.Signature: public static void ShowNotice(string text, float seconds = 4f)
Members.Summary: Show a short notice to the local player. In the world it is the game's own notification popup (titled with the running gamemode's name) and stays `seconds`; in the menu it is the hub's toast, whose duration is fixed. Safe from any thread: calls off the main thread are queued to the next frame. Since 3.0.0.

Parameters.Name: text
Parameters.Description: The notice text, e.g. "Round starts in 10 seconds".

Parameters.Name: seconds
Parameters.Description: How long the world popup stays, in seconds. 0, a negative value or NaN uses 4. The menu toast ignores it.

Members.Name: SendToAll
Members.Signature:
public static bool SendToAll(
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    byte[] payload)
Members.Summary: Send bytes to every other player in the current session (not to yourself). Reliable, over Steam P2P on Side Hustle's own channel; at most `MaxMessageBytes` bytes. Returns false, with a log line, when there is no session lobby or the message is refused. Off the main thread it is queued and returns true. Since 3.0.0.
Members.Returns: True when the message went out or was queued from another thread. False when it was refused; the log line says why.

Parameters.Name: gamemodeId
Parameters.Description: Your `GamemodeDescriptor.Id`, e.g. "doodesch.example". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: channel
Parameters.Description: Your own message name, e.g. "ping" or "state". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: payload
Parameters.Description: The bytes to send, at most `MaxMessageBytes` (8192). Null sends an empty payload.

Members.Name: SendToAll
Members.Signature: public static bool SendToAll(string gamemodeId, string channel, string text)
Members.Summary: Send UTF-8 text to every other player in the current session. Same rules as the byte overload. Since 3.0.0.

Parameters.Name: gamemodeId
Parameters.Description: Your `GamemodeDescriptor.Id`. Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: channel
Parameters.Description: Your own message name, e.g. "ping". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: text
Parameters.Description: The text, sent as UTF-8. The encoded bytes count against `MaxMessageBytes`. Null sends an empty text.

Members.Name: SendTo
Members.Signature:
public static bool SendTo(
    ulong steamId,
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    byte[] payload)
Members.Summary: Send bytes to one player of the current session by Steam id. The target must be in the session's lobby; sending to yourself is refused. Same rules as `SendToAll`. Since 3.0.0.

Parameters.Name: steamId
Parameters.Description: The target's `SessionPlayer.SteamId`, e.g. `SessionMessage.SenderSteamId` to answer a message.

Parameters.Name: gamemodeId
Parameters.Description: Your `GamemodeDescriptor.Id`. Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: channel
Parameters.Description: Your own message name, e.g. "pong". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: payload
Parameters.Description: The bytes to send, at most `MaxMessageBytes` (8192). Null sends an empty payload.

Members.Name: SendTo
Members.Signature:
public static bool SendTo(
    ulong steamId,
    string gamemodeId,
    string channel,
    string text)
Members.Summary: Send UTF-8 text to one player of the current session. Same rules as the byte overload. Since 3.0.0.

Parameters.Name: steamId
Parameters.Description: The target's `SessionPlayer.SteamId`.

Parameters.Name: gamemodeId
Parameters.Description: Your `GamemodeDescriptor.Id`. Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: channel
Parameters.Description: Your own message name, e.g. "pong". Required. At most 64 bytes as UTF-8.

Parameters.Name: text
Parameters.Description: The text, sent as UTF-8. The encoded bytes count against `MaxMessageBytes`. Null sends an empty text.

Members.Name: OnMessage
Members.Summary: Receive the messages sent for `gamemodeId` (any channel - read `SessionMessage.Channel`). Handlers run on the main thread. Only packets from members of the current session's lobby are delivered; the sender id comes from Steam, never from the payload. Since 3.0.0.

Parameters.Name: gamemodeId
Parameters.Description: Your `GamemodeDescriptor.Id`, the same id the senders pass. Matched exactly, case included. Null or empty is ignored with a warning.

Parameters.Name: handler
Parameters.Description: Called once per received message. Null is ignored with a warning.

Members.Name: OffMessage
Members.Summary: Remove a handler added with `OnMessage`. Returns true if it was registered. Since 3.0.0.

Parameters.Name: gamemodeId
Parameters.Description: The id the handler was added with.

Parameters.Name: handler
Parameters.Description: The same delegate instance passed to `OnMessage`.

Members.Name: MaxMessageBytes
Members.Summary: The largest payload `SendToAll` and `SendTo` accept, in bytes. Since 3.0.0.

sidehustle.Name: SessionRole
sidehustle.Summary: Who the local player is in a session. Read it from `LaunchContext.Role`. Since 3.0.0.

Members.Name: Singleplayer
Members.Summary: A singleplayer launch; no lobby.

Members.Name: Host
Members.Summary: The local player opened the lobby and owns the session.

Members.Name: Client
Members.Summary: The local player joined someone else's lobby.

sidehustle.Name: SessionPlayer
sidehustle.Summary: One player in the current session (see `API.Players`, `API.PlayerJoined`, `API.PlayerLeft`). The same object stays in `API.Players` for as long as the player is in the session; `DisplayName` and `IsHost` are refreshed about twice a second. Since 3.0.0.

Members.Name: SteamId
Members.Summary: The player's Steam id (id64). 0 for the local player when Steam could not be read.

Members.Name: DisplayName
Members.Signature: public string DisplayName { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The name other players see. For the local player this is the session alias when one is set, else the Steam persona. For a remote player in a World session it is the replicated in-game name (which carries their alias) once their character has spawned; before that, and in a MenuSpace session, it is their Steam persona.

Members.Name: IsHost
Members.Signature: public bool IsHost { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: True for the lobby owner. In singleplayer the local player is not the host.

Members.Name: IsLocal
Members.Summary: True for the player on this machine.

Members.Name: ToString
Members.Summary: "Name (steamId)", for logs.

sidehustle.Name: SessionMessage
sidehustle.Summary: A gamemode message received over Side Hustle's P2P channel (see `API.OnMessage`). Since 3.0.0.

Members.Name: GamemodeId
Members.Summary: The gamemode id the sender addressed.

Members.Name: Channel
Members.Summary: The sender's channel name, free-form per gamemode (e.g. "ping", "state").

Members.Name: SenderSteamId
Members.Summary: The sender's Steam id as Steam reported it for the packet. Never read from the payload.

Members.Name: Payload
Members.Summary: The raw payload bytes.

Members.Name: IsText
Members.Summary: True when the sender used a text overload.

Members.Name: Text
Members.Summary: The payload decoded as UTF-8.

sidehustle.Name: GamemodeDescriptor
sidehustle.Summary: Everything a gamemode mod tells Side Hustle about itself. Pass one of these to `API.Register` (usually from your mod's OnInitializeMelon). Only `Id`, `DisplayName` and the launch callback for your `Support` mode are required; every multiplayer field is optional so a singleplayer-only mod registers minimally.

Members.Name: Id
Members.Summary: Stable, unique key (e.g. "doodesch.inkubator"). Used for de-duplication and, later, lobby filtering.
Members.Value: 3-48 characters of a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' or '-', e.g. "doodesch.prophunt". Another form logs a warning and still registers. Compared exactly, case included. Required: null or empty makes `API.Register` throw.

Members.Name: DisplayName
Members.Summary: Name shown in the gamemode list.
Members.Value: E.g. "PropHunt". Null or empty shows `Id` instead.

Members.Name: Description
Members.Summary: Short one-line description shown under the name.

Members.Name: Author
Members.Summary: Author shown in the list (optional).

Members.Name: Icon
Members.Summary: Icon sprite for the list row. If null, Side Hustle builds one from `IconTex`.

Members.Name: IconTex
Members.Summary: Icon texture; Side Hustle wraps it in a Sprite when `Icon` is null.

Members.Name: IconResource
Members.Summary:
Name of a PNG embedded in your mod's assembly (the manifest resource name, e.g. "YourMod.icon.png"). Used only when `Icon` and `IconTex` are both null: the hub loads it into `IconTex` the first time it draws the row, so you need no Unity image code. A name that does not resolve is logged together with the resource names the assembly does have. Since 3.0.0.

Embed the PNG as `<AssemblyName>.hub-icon.png` (csproj: `<EmbeddedResource Include="icon.png"
LogicalName="YourMod.hub-icon.png" />`) and the hub finds it without this field, and also while the boot gate holds your mod back, when none of your code has run yet.

Members.Name: Support
Members.Summary: Which play modes this gamemode supports.

Members.Name: Surface
Members.Summary: Whether the gamemode runs as a menu overlay or needs the game world.

Members.Name: DownloadUrl
Members.Summary: Where to get this mod (its Thunderstore/Nexus/GitHub page). When set, Side Hustle advertises this gamemode's live public lobbies to players who do NOT have it installed, with a "Download Mod" button that opens this page. Null = still advertised by name (see `Advertise`) but with no download link. Only links on known mod hosts (Thunderstore, Nexus, GitHub) are opened.
Members.Value: An absolute https link on thunderstore.io, nexusmods.com, github.com or doodesch.de, or a subdomain of one, e.g. "https://github.com/you/yourmode". Any other link is shown but never opened.

Members.Name: Advertise
Members.Summary: When true (default), this gamemode's PUBLIC lobbies are advertised in the Side Hustle menu of players who do not have it installed, so they can discover it. Set false to stay invisible to non-installers - e.g. a work-in-progress gamemode you do not want discovered during development. This only affects that discovery listing; the gamemode is always fully hostable and joinable by people who have it.

Members.Name: BlockVanillaQuests
Members.Summary: When true, Side Hustle blocks every vanilla quest from starting for the duration of the session (a Harmony prefix on Quest.Begin). Keeps a clean slate - no tutorial/dealer quest chains, phone prompts, or NPC waypoints fighting the gamemode. Quests are host-authoritative so this matters on the host. Default false.

Members.Name: AllowedQuestTitles
Members.Summary: Quest titles EXEMPT from `BlockVanillaQuests` - e.g. a gamemode's own guide quest. Their `Quest.Begin` is allowed through even while vanilla quests are blocked. Default none.
Members.Value: Each entry is compared exactly, case included, with the quest's `title`, e.g. "PropHunt" for PropHunt's guide quest. Null or empty entries are skipped.

Members.Name: SkipIntro
Members.Summary: When true, Side Hustle skips the new-game intro cutscene + character-creator (sets the player's HasCompletedIntro before the intro gate runs), so players drop straight into the world. Default false.

Members.Name: ForceNewGame
Members.Summary: Has no effect. Side Hustle boots a clean scratch world (clears the scratch folder and copies DefaultSave) on every World launch anyway, and never touches a real save slot. Kept so mods that set it still load. Default false.

Members.Name: BlockSaveDuringSession
Members.Summary: When true, Side Hustle blocks every vanilla save (both SaveManager.Save overloads) for the duration of the session. A gamemode runs on a throwaway scratch world and mutates transient state (teleports, locked doors, swapped appearances); persisting that to disk would corrupt the save. The Save button still appears but does nothing. Saving works normally again once the session ends. Default false.

Members.Name: SuppressNpcCombatReactions
Members.Summary: When true, Side Hustle stops NPCs from reacting to hunter/player GUNFIRE for the session (no panic/flee/cover, no civilian police-call, no WANTED pursuit, no bystander weapon-impact) - so a gamemode can fire weapons without derailing the NPC schedule. Purely subtractive (prefixes on NPCAwareness NoiseEvent/VisionEvent for the gunshot/discharge cases, NPC.SendImpact, and the ranged-weapon aim scan); every other NPC awareness (footsteps, deals, vandalism) is untouched. Default false.

Members.Name: DisableVanillaPlayerDeath
Members.Summary: When true, Side Hustle cancels all vanilla PLAYER death for the session (prefix on PlayerHealth.TakeDamage + SendDie) - players cannot die to real weapon damage while the session runs. Use this when elimination is the gamemode's own concern (e.g. a host-validated catch) and vanilla death + medical-centre respawn would eject a player from the play area. Damage to NPCs/props is untouched. Default false.

Members.Name: OnLaunchSingleplayer
Members.Summary: Invoked to start singleplayer. Required for Singleplayer/Hybrid gamemodes.

Members.Name: OnHostMultiplayer
Members.Summary: Invoked to start hosting a multiplayer session. Optional.

Members.Name: OnJoinMultiplayer
Members.Summary: Invoked to join a multiplayer session. Optional.

Members.Name: OnExitToHub
Members.Summary: Invoked when Side Hustle tears the gamemode down (e.g. the player backs out). Optional.

Members.Name: Policy
Members.Summary: Optional policy controlling which other mods may stay loaded while this gamemode runs. Null = no restriction (default). See `ModPolicy`.

Members.Name: DefaultRequiredModsOnly
Members.Summary: When true, the Host form defaults the mod-set choice to "Required mods only" (an isolated profile with just this gamemode's mods) instead of "Current installed mods" - e.g. a multiplayer gamemode that wants everyone on an identical, clean set. The host can still switch it before starting. Only takes effect when `Policy` is declared and would actually change the set (and is not blocked). Default false.

Members.Name: HostSettings
Members.Summary: Optional host-configurable settings. Side Hustle renders these as a form on the Host screen and ships the chosen values to your launch callbacks via `LaunchContext.Multiplayer`'s config blob. Null = none. See `SettingDescriptor`.
Members.Value: Shown in array order. Each `SettingDescriptor.Key` must be unique; a repeated key logs a warning and both controls write the same value.

Members.Name: Presets
Members.Summary: Optional one-click presets for `HostSettings`. Side Hustle shows a picker above the form; selecting a preset cascades its values into the matching controls (the host can still tweak after). Null/empty = no picker. See `SettingPreset`.
Members.Value: The form opens on the preset marked `SettingPreset.DefaultSelected`, else on the best fit for the lobby size, else on the first entry.

Members.Name: AllowsSingleplayer
Members.Summary: True when this descriptor can be launched in singleplayer.

Members.Name: AllowsMultiplayer
Members.Summary: True when this descriptor exposes multiplayer (host/join).

Every name here is true on the Side Hustle that ships it. The constants are compiled into your mod, so pass them to `Has`; do not read them to learn what is running.

Members.Summary: Per-gamemode mod policy (`GamemodeDescriptor.Policy`).

Members.Summary: The world hygiene flags on `GamemodeDescriptor` (quests, intro, saving, NPC combat, player death).

Members.Name: KickPlayer
Members.Summary: `API.KickPlayer`.

sidehustle.Name: GamemodeSupport
sidehustle.Summary: Which multiplayer modes a gamemode supports. Side Hustle uses this to decide whether selecting the gamemode launches straight into singleplayer or first shows the Singleplayer / Host / Join choice.

sidehustle.Name: GamemodeSurface
sidehustle.Summary: Where a gamemode runs. `MenuSpace` gamemodes build their own overlay on top of the main menu and never load a save (e.g. the Inkubator tattoo editor). `World` gamemodes need the actual game world, so Side Hustle boots a throwaway save before handing control over.

Members.Name: MenuSpace
Members.Summary: Runs as an overlay in the menu scene; no save is loaded.

Members.Name: World
Members.Summary: Needs the loaded game world; Side Hustle boots a throwaway save first.

sidehustle.Name: MultiplayerInfo
sidehustle.Summary: The multiplayer payload carried on `LaunchContext.Multiplayer`. Populated by Side Hustle from the Steam lobby's namespaced metadata (the `sh_*` keys). The host fills it from its host options; a joining client reads it back from the lobby. `ConfigBlob` is a free-form string the host writes (lobby key `sh_config`) so a gamemode can ship its own settings to clients with no extra netcode.

Members.Name: MaxPlayers
Members.Signature: public int MaxPlayers { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: Maximum players the host opened the lobby for.
Members.Value: The host form offers 2 up to the lobby cap. It starts at the host's last choice, else at 4 or the cap, whichever is lower.

Members.Name: HostName
Members.Signature: public string HostName { get; internal set; }
Members.Summary: The host's name as other players see it: the display name the host chose for this gamemode, or their Steam persona name when none is set (lobby key `sh_host_name`).

Members.Summary: True if the lobby is password-protected (lobby key `sh_pw` = "1").

Members.Name: ConfigBlob

Members.Signature: public string GamemodeId { get; internal set; }

Members.Name: DownloadUrl

sidehustle.Name: WorldHygiene
sidehustle.Summary: Ready-made sets of the world hygiene flags on `GamemodeDescriptor`, so a World gamemode does not have to know which five booleans belong together. Each method sets the flags on the descriptor you pass and returns it, and only ever switches flags ON: anything you set yourself stays set. Since 3.0.0.

Members.Name: CleanWorld
Members.Summary: A clean scratch world: vanilla quests blocked (except `allowedQuestTitles`), the intro skipped and saving blocked for the session. Fits most World gamemodes.
Members.Returns: The same descriptor, so the call fits inside `API.Register`.

Parameters.Name: descriptor
Parameters.Description: The descriptor to change. Null logs a warning and returns null.

Parameters.Name: allowedQuestTitles
Parameters.Description: Quest titles that may still start, e.g. "PropHunt"; see `GamemodeDescriptor.AllowedQuestTitles`. None keeps the titles already set.

Members.Name: Arena
Members.Summary: `CleanWorld` plus no NPC reactions to gunfire and no vanilla player death - for a gamemode whose players shoot and whose eliminations are its own (the set PropHunt uses).
Members.Returns: The same descriptor, so the call fits inside `API.Register`.

Parameters.Name: descriptor
Parameters.Description: The descriptor to change. Null logs a warning and returns null.

Parameters.Name: allowedQuestTitles
Parameters.Description: Quest titles that may still start, e.g. "PropHunt"; see `GamemodeDescriptor.AllowedQuestTitles`. None keeps the titles already set.

sidehustle.Name: ModPolicy
sidehustle.Summary:
An optional per-gamemode policy that controls which OTHER mods are active while the gamemode runs. When a gamemode with a policy is launched, Side Hustle restarts the game into a temporary, isolated profile that loads ONLY the allowed mods, after a confirmation that lists exactly what changes, then continues into the gamemode; leaving the gamemode restarts back to your full mod set. Your installed mods are never renamed, moved or deleted - the profile is a throwaway sandbox - so mod managers stay in sync and a normal launch always loads everything.

Mods are matched by their MelonLoader display name OR their DLL file name (case-insensitive, ".dll" optional). You never need to list the essentials - they are always kept: MelonLoader, S1API, Side Hustle, this gamemode's own mod, the Mod Manager & Phone App, and (for multiplayer gamemodes) the multiplayer libraries. Mods that a kept mod depends on are kept too.

Members.Name: AllowedMods
Members.Summary: Extra mods that are allowed to remain loaded alongside this gamemode. Everything loaded that is neither allowed, required, nor an essential (or a dependency of a kept mod) gets disabled.
Members.Value: MelonLoader names or DLL file names, e.g. `new[] { "Snitch", "Inkorporated" }`. A name that is not installed is skipped. Null or empty allows no extra mods.

Members.Name: RequiredMods
Members.Summary: Mods this gamemode needs. If present but disabled they are enabled; if a required mod is not installed at all the player is told to install it first. Required mods are implicitly allowed.
Members.Value: MelonLoader names or DLL file names, e.g. `new[] { "WhatsDab", "Sideload" }`. A required name that is not installed blocks a singleplayer launch, and hosting offers only the current mods. Null or empty requires nothing.

sideload.Name: Apps
sideload.Summary:
The Sideload framework's modder API. Reference Sideload.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod. Register an app and Sideload renders your HTML/CSS/JS bundle as a real phone app - no uGUI assembly by hand, no layout arithmetic, hot-reloadable while the game runs.

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when Sideload is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so you can ship this unconditionally with no hard dependency. Check `Available` only if you want to fall back to your own UI.

```csharp
using Sideload.Api;
Apps.Register("prophunt", "PropHunt.App", title: "PropHunt", iconLabel: "PropHunt");
```

The bundle prefix is the embedded-resource prefix of your web files inside your own assembly, so `PropHunt/App/index.html` embedded as `PropHunt.App.index.html` is reached with prefix `"PropHunt.App"`. A file at `Mods/<id>/index.html` overrides the embedded copy.

All calls MUST be made from the Unity main thread.
sideload.Remarks: Ids are compared case-insensitively and trimmed. Call and event names are compared case-insensitively. A bundle path is resolved in two places, and the file on disk wins: `Mods/<id>/<path>`, then the embedded resource `<bundlePrefix>.<path with / turned into .>`. So `css/app.css` with prefix `"MyMod.Assets.mystash"` is the resource `MyMod.Assets.mystash.css.app.css`.

Members.Name: Available
Members.Summary: True only when the Sideload host is installed AND bound. You rarely need this - the API is a safe no-op when absent; use it to decide whether to build a fallback UI instead.

Members.Name: Register
Members.Signature:
public static AppHandle Register(
    string id,
    string bundlePrefix,
    string title = null,
    string iconLabel = null,
    Assembly hostAssembly = null)
Members.Summary: Declare an app. It appears on the in-game phone with its own icon and renders `index.html` from your bundle. Load-order-proof: registering before Sideload has loaded is fine, the call is replayed once the host appears.
Members.Returns: The handle for the app's calls, events, badge and notifications. Every method on it chains.

Parameters.Name: id
Parameters.Description: Stable, unique id, e.g. "mystash". Also the folder name under Mods/ that overrides the embedded files. Compared case-insensitively. Registering the same id again replaces the earlier app. Null or empty registers nothing and returns a handle whose calls do nothing.

Parameters.Name: bundlePrefix
Parameters.Description: Embedded-resource prefix of your web files inside the calling assembly, e.g. "MyMod.Assets.mystash" for `MyMod.Assets.mystash.index.html`. It is the `LogicalName` prefix in your csproj. Null means no prefix.

Parameters.Name: title
Parameters.Description: App title, e.g. "Stash". Null or blank uses `id`.

Parameters.Name: iconLabel
Parameters.Description: Caption under the home-screen icon. Null or blank uses the title.

Parameters.Name: hostAssembly
Parameters.Description: The assembly holding the embedded bundle. Defaults to the caller's assembly; pass it explicitly if you wrap this call in a helper of your own.

sideload.Example:
The csproj embeds the web files under the prefix you pass to `Register`:

```csharp
<EmbeddedResource Include="Assets/mystash/*">
  <LogicalName>MyMod.Assets.mystash.%(Filename)%(Extension)</LogicalName>
</EmbeddedResource>
```

Then in `OnInitializeMelon`:

```csharp
Apps.Register("mystash", "MyMod.Assets.mystash", title: "Stash", iconLabel: "Stash")
    .OnCall("items.list", _ => string.Join("\n", Items))
    .OnCall("items.add", text => { Items.Add(text.Trim()); return "ok"; });
```

sideload.Name: AppHandle
sideload.Summary: Handle to a registered app: the two-way channel between your C# and the app's JavaScript. Kept deliberately thin; every method stays a no-op when Sideload is absent.
sideload.Remarks: Strings cross the boundary in both directions. Send JSON for anything structured. Every call is queued until Sideload binds, except `Icon` and `Show`.

Members.Name: Id
Members.Summary: The id this app was registered under.

Members.Name: OnCall
Members.Signature: public AppHandle OnCall(string name, Func<string, string> handler)

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Description: The name the page passes to `s1.call`, e.g. "chat.send". Compared case-insensitively. Null or blank registers nothing. The same name again replaces the handler.

Parameters.Name: handler
Parameters.Description: Gets the page's argument, or an empty string when it passed none. Its return value is what `s1.call` returns; null returns an empty string. An exception is logged and the page gets an empty string.

Members.Name: Emit
Members.Signature: public void Emit(string name, string payload = "")
Members.Summary: Push an event at this app's page, where `s1.on("<name>", fn)` is waiting for it. Use it when the game changes something the page did not ask for - a message arriving, a timer expiring.

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Description: The name the page listens on with `s1.on`, e.g. "chat.message". Compared case-insensitively. Null or blank sends nothing.

Parameters.Name: payload
Parameters.Description: The string the page's listener receives, e.g. JSON. Null sends an empty string.

Members.Name: AllowHost
Members.Summary:
Let this app's page reach one host with `fetch`. Without at least one of these the page reaches nothing: the allowlist starts empty and only the app's own mod can add to it, so a web bundle edited in the Mods folder can never talk to somewhere you did not name here.

Give a bare host name. `*.example.com` covers any single label under it, but not `example.com` itself. Ports are ignored, and the scheme must be https unless the host is `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`.

```csharp
Apps.Register("mystash", "MyMod.Assets.mystash")
    .AllowHost("api.example.com")
    .AllowHost("*.cdn.example.com");
```

Parameters.Name: host
Parameters.Description: A bare host name such as "api.example.com", or `*.example.com` for any single label under it. A full URL is accepted and only its host is kept. A port is ignored.

Members.Name: Orientation
Members.Summary:
Which ways round the phone may hold this app, in preference order. The FIRST one is what the app opens in; naming a second is what lets the player turn it, with the rotate keys the game already binds. Say nothing and the app is landscape only, which is the only safe reading of silence - an app that never styled portrait must not be turned into it.

Both are worth styling. Sideload evaluates `@media (orientation: portrait|landscape)` against the real viewport shape, so one stylesheet covers both without any script. The player's choice is remembered per app; you do not have to store it.

```csharp
.Orientation("landscape")               // landscape only, the phone never turns
.Orientation("portrait")                // portrait only
.Orientation("landscape", "portrait")   // both, opens landscape
.Orientation("portrait", "landscape")   // both, opens portrait
```

Parameters.Name: supported
Parameters.Description: "landscape", "portrait" or both, in preference order. Case-insensitive. Any other value is logged as a warning and ignored. Nothing recognisable keeps the previous setting, landscape only by default.

Members.Name: Badge
Members.Summary:
The unread count on this app's home-screen icon - the same red badge the vanilla apps use. Zero clears it. Counts above 99 read as "99+".

Set it whenever your own count changes, not on a timer: the value is remembered across a phone rebuild, so setting it once is enough and setting it again is cheap.

```csharp
app.Badge(unreadMessages);
```

Parameters.Name: count
Parameters.Description: The unread count. 0 clears the badge. A negative value counts as 0.

Members.Name: Notify
Members.Signature:
public AppHandle Notify(
    string title,
    string subtitle = "",
    float seconds = 0f)
Members.Summary:
Raise one of the game's own phone notifications - the slide-in the vanilla apps use, carrying this app's icon. Nothing happens if the app is not on a phone yet.

This interrupts whatever the player is doing, so spend it on what they would want to be interrupted for. A count that can wait belongs in `Badge`.

```csharp
app.Notify("Jessi Waters", "on my way");
```

Parameters.Name: title
Parameters.Description: The headline, e.g. a sender name like "Jessi Waters". Null counts as empty.

Parameters.Name: subtitle
Parameters.Description: The line under it, e.g. "on my way". Empty by default.

Parameters.Name: seconds
Parameters.Description: How long it stays up. Leave it at zero for Sideload's own timing (9 seconds), which suits a headline plus a sentence. Raise it for something the player has to act on, lower it for a passing remark. Clamped to between 2 and 30 seconds - the slide-in cannot be dismissed, so an app does not get to hold the corner of the screen. Zero or below means Sideload's own timing. Ignored, without failing, on a Sideload too old to have it.

Members.Name: IsOnScreen
Members.Summary:
Whether this app is the one the phone is showing right now. Ask before interrupting: an event the player is already watching happen does not deserve a notification, and the same event with the phone in their pocket does. False when Sideload is absent or the app is not on a phone yet.

```csharp
if (!app.IsOnScreen) app.Notify(sender, text);
```

Members.Name: Image
Members.Signature: public AppHandle Image(string name, byte[] png)
Members.Summary: Hand a picture your mod produced at runtime to the page, which draws it with ``. Null or empty bytes remove it, which is how you say "there is no picture for this one" and let the page fall back to whatever it draws without one. PNG bytes rather than a texture, because this file references no Unity type and is not going to start. Supplying the same name again replaces the picture. ```csharp app.Image("avatar/" + steamId, pngBytes); ```

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Description: The name after `s1://` in the page, e.g. "avatar/76561198". Trimmed. Null or blank does nothing.

Parameters.Name: png
Parameters.Description: PNG file bytes. Null or empty removes the picture.

Members.Name: Icon
Members.Summary:
Show or hide this app's home-screen icon while the game is running.

For an app whose way in is a key rather than a square, but only sometimes: hash puts an icon there exactly while the game's console is switched on, because that is the only time it can run anything, and that setting is a live toggle. Safe to call with the same value repeatedly.

Unlike `NoIcon` this is NOT queued until Sideload binds. A caller polling a condition would otherwise pile up one queued call per check against a host that never arrives; an unbound host simply ignores it, which is the right answer for a decision that is re-stated anyway.

Parameters.Name: visible
Parameters.Description: True shows the icon, false hides it.

Members.Name: NoIcon
Members.Summary:
Give this app no home-screen icon. For an app whose way in already exists somewhere else - a vanilla icon your mod has taken over, a world object, another app handing off.

With no icon, `Open` is the ONLY way in: call it from wherever your entry point is, or the app is unreachable. Check `CanOpenProgrammatically` first - against an older Sideload this is a no-op and the app would get an icon you did not plan for.

```csharp
Apps.Register("reflash-messages", "Reflash.Assets.reflash-messages", "Messages").NoIcon();
```

Members.Name: Open
Members.Summary:
Open this app as if the player had pressed its icon: whatever else is open closes first, and the phone turns to this app's orientation. Does nothing while the app is not on a phone - before the home screen exists there is nothing to open.

```csharp
if (playerPressedTheHijackedIcon) app.Open();
```

Members.Name: Close
Members.Summary: Close this app, returning the phone to its home screen. Does nothing if it is not the open one.

Members.Name: IsOpen
Members.Summary: Whether this app is the one the phone has open - true even with the phone in the player's pocket. For "can they actually see it", use `IsOnScreen`.

Members.Name: CanOpenProgrammatically
Members.Summary:
Whether the installed Sideload understands `NoIcon` and `Open`. False against an older host, where both are silent no-ops.

A mod that provides its own entry point must check this before registering anything: on an older host it would hide nothing, open nothing, and leave the player with apps they cannot reach. Refuse to set up and say which version is needed - that is a fixable message, an unreachable app is not.

```csharp
if (!AppHandle.CanOpenProgrammatically) { Log.Error("needs Sideload 1.1.0 or newer"); return; }
```

Members.Name: Show
Members.Summary:
Take the phone out AND open this app - what a key that opens an app has to mean, because `Open` on its own opens it on a phone that is still in the player's pocket.

The order matters and is why this exists rather than two calls at the call site: the page is built the first time it is opened, and a page built while its panel is hidden measures every line about ten times too short. Raising first means the very first frame is laid out against the real viewport.

Returns false when the game refused the phone - paused, asleep, dead, arrested - in which case nothing was opened either.

```csharp
if (consoleKeyPressed) app.Show();
```

Members.Name: OnKey
Members.Signature: public AppHandle OnKey(string keys, Func<string, bool> handler)
Members.Summary:
Ask for a key that reaches this app with the phone still in the player's pocket - the way IN, as opposed to `data-keys`, which only ever reaches a focused field in an already-open page.

Spell keys the way the DOM does, several separated by spaces or commas: `Enter`, `F8`, `Ctrl+Shift+K`. Modifiers match exactly, so `Enter` does not fire for Shift+Enter. `Escape` is refused - it is the game's own exit action.

**Your handler returns whether it TOOK the press.** Return false and the key goes to the next app that wants it, which is how you decline a key you cannot use right now - a chat with no lobby behind it should not open, and should not swallow the key on its way past. The argument is the key that fired, so one handler can serve several.

**When two apps want the same key, the one that notified most recently gets it.** Two messengers installed together then behave the way a phone should: the key answers the conversation that is actually waiting. An app that has never notified still wins a key nobody else claimed - it simply sorts last.

Sideload only reads the key where the game would let the player take their phone out anyway: never while they are typing, paused, asleep, arrested, or standing at a station, a shop or the developer console. While one of your apps is on screen it owns every key it claimed, and no other app is offered them.

```csharp
app.OnKey("Enter", _ => { if (!Online) return false; return app.Show(); });
```

Parameters.Name: keys
Parameters.Description: One or more key declarations, separated by whitespace or commas, e.g. "Enter F8". A declaration is optional modifiers `Ctrl` (or `Control`), `Shift` and `Alt`, joined by `+` to one key name. Key names: the letters a to z, the digits 0 to 9, `F1` to `F12`, `Enter` (or `Return`), `Tab`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Insert`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight` and `Space`. Case-insensitive. Punctuation keys are not accepted. A declaration that does not parse is logged as a warning and dropped; the rest still count.

Parameters.Name: handler
Parameters.Description: Runs on the Unity main thread. Gets the key that fired in its canonical spelling, e.g. "Enter", "Ctrl+Shift+k" or "F8"; letters come back lower-case. Returns whether it took the press. Null gives back every key this app holds.

Members.Name: CanClaimKeys
Members.Summary:
Whether the installed Sideload can hand an app a key. False against anything older than 1.10.0, where `OnKey` is a silent no-op.

Worth checking only when the key is the ONLY way into your app - pair it with `NoIcon` and a host that ignores both leaves the player with an app they can neither see nor reach.

Members.Name: Reload
Members.Summary: Rebuild this app's page from disk, script engine included - what saving a file in `Mods/<id>/` means to someone editing it. For a tool that writes the bundle itself and wants the change on screen now, without DevTools attached. A page that was never opened is left alone: it builds from disk the first time.

Members.Name: Unregister
Members.Summary: Take this app off the phone and forget it while the game runs. For an app that only exists for a while; a mod's own apps live as long as the game and never need this. Registering the same id again brings it back, handlers included - they are kept by id.

Members.Name: CanEditLive
Members.Summary: Whether the installed Sideload understands `Reload` and `Unregister`, and puts an app registered while the game runs on the phone at once. False against an older host, where an app registered after the home screen was built waits for the next scene load.

Members.Name: AllowGameWrites
Members.Summary:
Let this app's page CHANGE the game through `s1api`, for one area. Without it every `s1api` write is refused: a page is a file anyone can edit, so the permission has to come from the mod's own code, the same rule as `AllowHost`. Reading needs no permission.

```csharp
app.AllowGameWrites("money");   // s1api.money.change(amount) now works on this app's page
```

Parameters.Name: scope
Parameters.Description: The area, e.g. "money". "*" allows every area, which is rarely what you mean.

Members.Name: Hide
Members.Summary: Close this app and put the phone away. The mirror of `Show`.

sideload.Name: Surfaces
sideload.Summary:
HTML somewhere other than the phone: a column in the main menu, a panel on a machine, a board on a wall.

The renderer never cared about the phone - it draws into any RectTransform - so a surface is the same engine, the same CSS subset and the same `s1.call` / `s1.on` channel, only mounted somewhere else. What it does not have is everything that belongs to the phone: no home-screen icon, no orientation the player can turn, no badge, no notification.

```csharp
Surfaces.Mount(myPanelRectTransform, "sidehustle-menu", "SideHustle.Assets.menu")
        .OnCall("menu.state", _ => StateJson());
```

Needs Sideload 1.13.0. Against anything older `Mount` answers a handle whose calls are no-ops and `Available` is false, so a mod ships this without a hard version pin and keeps its own UI as the fallback.

Members.Name: Available
Members.Summary: Whether the installed Sideload can render outside the phone at all.

Members.Name: Mount
Members.Signature:
public static SurfaceHandle Mount(
    object hostRect,
    string id,
    string bundlePrefix,
    float designShortSide = 0f,
    Assembly hostAssembly = null)
Members.Summary: Render a bundle into a panel of your own.
Members.Returns: The handle for the surface's calls and events. It is returned even when nothing was mounted; check `IsMounted` to know.

Parameters.Name: hostRect
Parameters.Description: Your `UnityEngine.RectTransform`. Typed as object only so this file stays compilable in a mod with no Unity reference; pass the RectTransform straight in.

Parameters.Name: id
Parameters.Description: Stable id, unique across apps AND surfaces - they share one namespace, so a surface cannot take an app's `s1.call` handlers. Also the folder under Mods/ that overrides the bundle. E.g. "sidehustle-menu". Compared case-insensitively and trimmed. Mounting the same id again replaces the old surface. Null or empty mounts nothing.

Parameters.Name: bundlePrefix
Parameters.Description: Embedded-resource prefix of the web files inside the calling assembly, e.g. "SideHustle.Assets.menu". Null means no prefix.

Parameters.Name: designShortSide
Parameters.Description: What the panel's short side is worth in CSS pixels. 0 (the default) maps one CSS pixel to one device unit, which is what a panel uGUI has already laid out wants. Members.Name: Image
Members.Signature: public SurfaceHandle Image(string name, byte[] png)
Members.Summary: Publish a picture this surface's page can draw with ``, exactly as an app does. Null or empty bytes remove it. It was missing, and the store never cared: pictures are held by (id, name) and nothing asks whether the id belongs to an app or a surface. So a surface could always have them - it just had no supported way to say so, and the one mod that needed it reached past this file into the internals because it compiles the shim in as source. A mod that references the DLL could not have done that at all. PNG bytes rather than a texture, for the reason the whole file gives: nothing here references a Unity type and nothing here is going to start. ```csharp surface.Image("icon/" + itemId, pngBytes); ```

Parameters.Name: name
Parameters.Description: The name after `s1://` in the page, e.g. "avatar/76561198". Trimmed. Null or blank does nothing.

Parameters.Name: png
Parameters.Description: PNG file bytes. Null or empty removes the picture.

tightbeam.Name: Beam
tightbeam.Summary:
TightBeam's cross-mod control API for the player's flashlight. Reference TightBeam.Api.dll OR drop this single file into your mod. Drive the beam from any mod: on/off, brightness, range, colour, plus Blink/Flicker/Pulse and scoped per-field overrides (e.g. dim it in a dark room, flicker it near power).

Every call is a zero-overhead no-op when TightBeam is not installed and lights up automatically when it is, so you can ship this unconditionally with no hard dependency. All calls MUST be on the Unity main thread.

```csharp
using TightBeam.Api;
Beam.Blink(3);                                   // event blink
var ov = Beam.BeginOverride("MyMod");            // scoped, per-field override
ov.SetIntensity(1f).SetSpotAngle(28f);           //   dim + narrow while in a zone
ov.Dispose();                                    // release -> beam returns to the player's own settings
```
